summaries.title: Antecedents and correlates of improved cognitive performance in children exposed in utero to low levels of lead.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Capillary blood samples were collected when the children were 6, 12, 18, and 24 months old and venous samples when they were 57 months old. Data were collected prospectively for this research study, not from routine clinical records.
summaries.summary: Prospective longitudinal cohort study examining cognitive recovery between 24 and 57 months in children with varying prenatal and postnatal lead exposures, finding that higher prenatal exposure predicts greater relative improvement, moderated by postnatal lead levels and sociodemographic factors.
key_findings: Higher prenatal lead exposure (cord blood) was associated with greater relative cognitive improvement between 24 and 57 months (beta=0.03, p=0.016 adjusted).
Postnatal blood lead levels at 18, 24, and 57 months were inversely associated with cognitive improvement (e.g., 24-month level: beta=-0.22, p=0.005 adjusted).
Among children with high prenatal exposure, girls showed significantly greater cognitive improvement than boys (difference of 7.7 points, p=0.017).
Higher HOME scores, social class, maternal IQ, and older maternal age were associated with greater cognitive improvement.
No significant association was found between cognitive improvement and ethnicity (p=0.57 adjusted).
summaries.data_source_type: prospective research cohort with direct data collection
summaries.population: children followed from birth, assessed at 24 and 57 months (n=170 at 57 months)
limitations: restricted range of prenatal exposures in low/medium groups
potential regression to the mean
observational design with residual confounding
relatively advantaged cohort limits generalizability
cognitive tests measure different skills at different ages

summaries.title: Semiparametric modeling of age at achieving developmental milestones after prenatal exposure to methylmercury in the Seychelles child development study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The measure of exposure was the mean of the total mercury concentration in segments of maternal hair, representing growth during pregnancy. The raw data on age at achieving developmental milestones were collected by asking the child's mother or primary caregiver the age, in months, at which the child walked or first said words other than mama or dada. This question was asked in a face-to-face interview conducted when the child was 19 months ± 2 weeks of age.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal cohort study evaluating the effect of prenatal methylmercury exposure via maternal hair mercury levels on the age at achieving developmental milestones (walking and talking) in Seychellois children at 19 months, using generalized additive models.
key_findings: Very slight delays (<1 day) in walking were observed at mercury levels from 0 to 7 ppm, but the effect did not persist at higher exposure levels (p=0.036).
No significant association was found between prenatal mercury exposure and age at talking (flat curve, nonlinear components not significant).
Change in age at walking from 1 to 5 ppm was +0.04 months, and from 5 to 15 ppm was -0.03 months.
Higher home environment scores were associated with earlier walking, while positive medical history and higher maternal education were associated with later walking.
summaries.data_source_type: cohort study with biospecimen analysis and maternal interviews
summaries.population: 738 Seychellois children (365 females, 373 males) evaluated at 19 months of age
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal methylmercury exposure (maternal hair mercury concentration)
limitations: reliance on maternal recall for developmental milestones
small effect sizes (approximately 1 day)
non-monotonic dose-response relationship complicates causal inference
sparse data at mercury levels above 15 ppm
log transformation of mercury compresses higher exposure values

summaries.title: Air pollution and health effects: A study of medical visits among children in Santiago, Chile.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data on morbidity due to respiratory diseases among children under 15 years of age have been collected from a group of public primary health clinics.
summaries.summary: Time-series study examining associations between daily air pollution (PM10, ozone) and clinic visit counts for respiratory symptoms among children in Santiago, Chile.
key_findings: PM10 was significantly associated with lower respiratory symptoms (LRS) in both children under 2 and children aged 3-15.
PM10 was associated with upper respiratory symptoms (URS) only in the older cohort.
Ozone was associated with both URS and LRS in the older cohort.
For children under 2, a 50-μg/m3 increase in PM10 was associated with a 4-12% increase in LRS.
For children aged 3-15, a 50-μg/m3 increase in PM10 was associated with a 3-9% increase in LRS, and a 50 ppb increase in ozone was associated with a 5% increase.
No significant association was found between PM10 or ozone and nonrespiratory symptoms.
Ozone was not significantly associated with respiratory symptoms in children under 2.
summaries.population: children under 15 years old in Santiago, Chile (<2 years and 3-15 years)
limitations: aggregate daily counts rather than individual patient records
clinic visits reflect subjective parental decisions and may be influenced by clinic capacity and operating hours
data only represent lower and moderate income populations
lack of data on sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide
potential for discouraged demand bias at high pollution levels

summaries.title: Minority children at risk from ETS.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The teams measured four different biomarkers in the blood cells of 109 Hispanic and African-American children, ages 1 to 6.
summaries.summary: Study evaluating the association between environmental tobacco smoke (ETS) exposure and cancer-related biomarkers in young minority children.
key_findings: The four measured biomarkers increased with ETS exposure in all exposure groups.
summaries.population: 109 Hispanic and African-American children, ages 1 to 6

summaries.title: Evaluation of urinary porphyrin excretion in neonates born to mothers exposed to airborne hexachlorobenzene.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Information on maternal history, sex, and fetal exposure to alcohol and tobacco consumption was obtained through a questionnaire prepared ad hoc for this study. Using urine collection bags, we collected fresh urine samples on the third day after birth from 68 full-term neonates... We obtained 52 fetal cord blood and 56 maternal serum samples for HCB analysis.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional study assessing urinary porphyrin excretion in neonates born to mothers exposed to airborne hexachlorobenzene (HCB) near a chlorinated solvent factory in Flix, Spain, compared to a non-exposed control group.
key_findings: Median HCB levels were 1.08 ng/mL in cord blood and 3.35 ng/mL in maternal serum, significantly higher in the exposed group (p < 0.05).
Neonates from the exposed group had higher CPIII excretion than the non-exposed group (p < 0.05), but this association disappeared after adjusting for maternal smoking.
Maternal smoking was associated with higher total porphyrin and CPIII excretion (p < 0.05).
No positive relationship was found between urinary porphyrin excretion and HCB levels; total porphyrin excretion showed no alteration between groups.
A negative association between CPI/CPIII and the highest tertile of HCB remained statistically significant for CPI after adjusting for smoking and alcohol (p < 0.05).
Heptaporphyrin isomer III was detected in 35.9% of the exposed group and 9.4% of the non-exposed group (p < 0.012).
captured_features: urinary porphyrins (total, UPI, UPIII, CPI, CPIII, heptaporphyrins)
HCB levels in cord blood and maternal serum
summaries.population: 68 full-term singleton neonates and their mothers born in Móra d’Ebre Hospital, Spain (1997–1999), with 38 from the exposed area (Flix) and 30 from neighboring villages.
limitations: Small sample size (n=68)
Cross-sectional design limits causal inference
Confounding by maternal smoking and alcohol consumption
Variations in porphyrin excretion during the first days of life
Lack of dose-response data for specific exposure levels

summaries.title: Metal composition of ambient PM2.5 influences severity of allergic airways disease in mice.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We collected ambient air PM2.5 samples on Teflon filters in 1999 in Zerbst... and in Hettstedt... We used a well-characterized mouse model of allergic airways disease induced by ovalbumin (OVA) antigen...
summaries.summary: Experimental study using an ovalbumin-sensitized mouse model to determine if PM2.5 composition influences allergic airway disease severity and links to prior human epidemiological findings.
key_findings: Hettstedt PM2.5 administered before challenge increased PenH 190% compared to baseline, while Zerbst PM2.5 and control filter extract increased PenH 120% and 44%, respectively.

Hettstedt PM2.5 administered to allergic mice before challenge caused a significant increase in Mch responsiveness 2 days after challenge compared to allergic mice exposed to Zerbst PM2.5 or control filter extract.

Particles from Hettstedt increased sensitization to OVA allergen, as determined by serum levels of OVA-specific IgE collected 2 days after OVA challenge, when administered at either the sensitization phase or the challenge phase.

Eosinophil numbers in allergic mice exposed to Hettstedt PM2.5 before challenge were significantly increased 3-fold compared with allergic mice exposed both to control filter extract and to Zerbst PM2.5.
Both Hettstedt and Zerbst PM2.5 administered before challenge in allergic mice caused similar significant increases in protein, LDH, and NAG in comparison to corresponding nonallergic groups.

Levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ) in allergic mice were increased 6- to 8-fold by exposure to either Hettstedt or Zerbst PM2.5 particles before challenge compared with control filter extract.
captured_features: BAL cytokines (IL-1β, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-13, MIP-2, TNF-α, IFN-γ)
summaries.data_source_type: environmental monitoring and laboratory animal experiment
summaries.population: female Balb/c mice, 7 weeks old
limitations: limited sample quantities restricted sensitization phase analysis to allergic mice only
insufficient mice at 7 days post-challenge prevented statistical analysis
animal model may not fully replicate human allergic disease

summaries.title: Traffic-related air pollution and respiratory symptoms in children living along trunk roads in Chiba Prefecture, Japan.
summaries.ehr_evidence: A survey of respiratory symptoms was conducted on all subjects in September or October of each year from 1992 through 1995... a standard respiratory symptom questionnaire... was sent through the schools to the parents of all subjects.
summaries.summary: Prospective four-year cohort study evaluating the association between traffic-related air pollution (proximity to trunk roads) and respiratory symptoms in schoolchildren in Chiba Prefecture, Japan.
key_findings: Prevalence of asthma was higher among girls living <50 m from trunk roads.
Incidence of asthma significantly increased among boys living in roadside areas relative to rural areas (odds ratio = 3.75; 95% confidence interval: 1.00-14.06).
Incidence of asthma increased among girls living in roadside areas but was not statistically significant (odds ratio = 4.06; 95% confidence interval: 0.91-18.10).
Prevalence of bronchitis was significantly higher in children living in steel or reinforced concrete houses compared to wooden houses.
No significant association was found between maternal smoking and respiratory symptoms.
History of allergic diseases was significantly associated with increased incidence of asthma and wheeze in both sexes.
captured_features: Parental-reported respiratory symptoms (asthma, wheeze, bronchitis, cough/phlegm)
Distance of home to trunk roads (<50 m vs ≥50 m vs rural)
History of allergic diseases and parental allergy history
summaries.population: schoolchildren aged 6-9 years in Chiba Prefecture, Japan
summaries.exposure_domain: traffic-related air pollution and proximity to trunk roads
limitations: loss to follow-up due to residential changes
potential response bias from varying questionnaire formats across surveys
exposure assessment based on residential distance and area-level monitoring rather than personal measurements
potential selective migration bias

summaries.title: Blood lead secular trend in a cohort of children in Mexico City (1987-2002).
summaries.ehr_evidence: We extracted air lead information from the Statistical Compendium of the System of Atmospheric Monitoring of the Metropolitan Zone of the Valley of Mexico (MZVM), 1986–2002.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating secular trends in blood lead levels and environmental exposures in children born in Mexico City from 1987 to 1992 over their first 10 years of life.
key_findings: Yearly mean air lead decreased from 2.80 µg/m³ in 1987 to 0.07 µg/m³ in 2002.
Each natural log decrease in air lead was accompanied by a 23.7% decrease in blood lead concentration for children born in 1987, falling to nearly zero for those born in 1992.
Geometric mean blood lead rose from 8.4 µg/dL (95% CI, 7.7 to 9.2) at 1 year to 10.1 µg/dL (95% CI, 9.3 to 11.0) at 2 years, then decreased to 6.4 µg/dL (95% CI, 5.8 to 7.1) at 10 years.
Children from the lowest socioeconomic stratum had 32.3% (95% CI, 17.0 to 49.5) higher geometric mean blood lead than the highest stratum.
Children from families using lead-glazed ceramics had 18.5% (95% CI, 10.0 to 27.6) higher geometric mean blood lead than nonusers.
Children living in the northeast sector had 10.9% (95% CI, 2.4 to 18.6) higher geometric mean blood lead than those in the southwest.
Significant decrease (p < 0.01) in the percentage of children with blood lead ≥ 10 µg/dL across year of birth during the first 7 years of life.
captured_features: complete vs incomplete blood lead data
summaries.data_source_type: prospective cohort / biospecimen assays / environmental monitoring
summaries.population: 321 children born in Mexico City between 1987 and 1992, followed from birth to 10 years of age
summaries.exposure_domain: environmental lead (air lead, lead-glazed ceramics, socioeconomic status, residential location)
limitations: used only three air monitoring stations not necessarily representative of all subjects' residences
lead-glazed ceramic use not quantified and only assessed at study start
potential collinearity between air lead and age
loss to follow-up and incomplete blood lead data
reliance on maternal self-report for pottery use
unable to account for many sources of lead variance

summaries.title: Estimated risk for altered fetal growth resulting from exposure to fine particles during pregnancy: an epidemiologic prospective cohort study in Poland.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study relied on personal air monitoring, questionnaires, and reviewed maternal and child hospital records.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study in Poland assessing the association between personal prenatal exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and environmental tobacco smoke (ETS) and fetal growth outcomes.
key_findings: Higher personal PM2.5 exposure was associated with significantly lower birth weight (β = –200.8, p = 0.03), birth length (β = –1.44, p = 0.01), and head circumference (β = –0.73, p = 0.02).
An increase in PM2.5 exposure from 10 to 50 µg/m3 was predicted to reduce birth weight by 140.3 g, birth length by 1.0 cm, and head circumference by 0.5 cm.
No significant association was found between PM2.5 or ETS and gestational age.
The effect of ETS on birth outcomes was insignificant in all regression models.
captured_features: personal PM2.5 levels via air monitoring
birth weight, length, and head circumference
summaries.data_source_type: prospective cohort with personal air monitoring and chart review
summaries.population: 362 pregnant women aged 18-35 years in Poland, nonsmoking, singleton pregnancies
summaries.exposure_domain: fine particulate matter (PM2.5), environmental tobacco smoke
limitations: Personal exposure monitoring was limited to a short 48-hour period during the second trimester.
ETS exposure was based on self-reported questionnaires, which may be subject to recall or reporting bias.
PM2.5 may act as a proxy for a complex mixture of other toxic environmental agents.
Ambient monitor correlations may not perfectly capture individual exposure variability.

summaries.title: Blood lead changes during pregnancy and postpartum with calcium supplementation.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Blood and urine samples were obtained monthly during pregnancy and the postpregnancy period for ≥ 6 months. Environmental samples of 6-day duplicate diet, drinking water, house dust, gasoline, and ambient air were collected quarterly.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal study of blood lead changes and lead mobilization from bone during pregnancy and postpartum in immigrant women, evaluating the effect of calcium supplementation.
key_findings: Geometric mean blood lead at first sampling was 2.4 µg/dL (range, 1.4–6.5).
Hematocrit-corrected blood lead increased by 10 to 50% (geometric mean 25%) during the third trimester.
Postpartum blood lead increased by 30 to 95% (geometric mean 65%; n = 8) from the late pregnancy minimum.
Significant increases in lead isotopic ratios from late pregnancy minimum occurred in 3 of 8 subjects (p < 0.01).
Extra lead flux mobilized from bone during late pregnancy and postpartum ranged from 50 to 380 µg (geometric mean 145 µg).
Cord:maternal blood lead geometric mean ratio was 0.72 (range 0.55–0.93; r² = 0.93).

Calcium supplementation delayed the timing of blood lead increases to 6–8 months gestation and halved the extra bone flux compared to a low-calcium cohort, but provided limited benefit for lead toxicity during lactation.
summaries.population: pregnant and postpartum female immigrants to Australia (aged 19–32 years) and two nonpregnant controls
summaries.exposure_domain: lead exposure and mobilization from bone; calcium supplementation
limitations: small sample size (n=10 pregnant subjects, n=2 controls)
absence of a placebo control group
reliance on self-reported supplement compliance
potential unmeasured acute lead exposure sources (e.g., dietary changes at ethnic events)

summaries.title: Birth outcomes and prenatal exposure to ozone, carbon monoxide, and particulate matter: results from the Children's Health Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Birth certificate information for California-born children who participated in the CHS was obtained by computerized linkage of participants with the California Department of Health Services Birth Statistical Master Files and Birth Cohort Files.
summaries.summary: Population-based cohort study examining associations between prenatal ambient air pollution exposure and birth weight, low birth weight, and intrauterine growth retardation in term infants in California.
key_findings: A 12-ppb increase in 24-hr ozone averaged over the entire pregnancy was associated with 47.2 g lower birth weight (95% CI, 27.4–67.0 g).

A 1.4-ppm difference in first-trimester carbon monoxide exposure was associated with 21.7 g lower birth weight (95% CI, 1.1–42.3 g) and a 20% increased risk of intrauterine growth retardation (95% CI, 1.0–1.4).

A 20-µg/m3 difference in PM10 during the third trimester was associated with a 21.7-g lower birth weight (95% CI, 1.1–42.2 g), but this association was reduced and not significant after adjusting for ozone.
A 17-ppb difference in third-trimester ozone exposure increased the risk of intrauterine growth retardation by 20% (95% CI, 1.0–1.3).
NO2 levels were not associated with birth weight in this study.
captured_features: ambient air pollutant levels (O3, CO, PM10, NO2)
summaries.data_source_type: Birth certificates (linked registry), environmental monitoring, questionnaires
summaries.population: 3,901 term infants (gestational age 37-44 weeks) born in California between 1975 and 1987
summaries.exposure_domain: Ambient air pollution (ozone, carbon monoxide, PM10, nitrogen dioxide)
limitations: Exposure assigned based on ZIP code centroid at childbirth, which may not reflect actual exposure during the entire pregnancy due to residential mobility.
Lack of data on maternal employment location and commuting patterns.
Potential misclassification of gestational age based on maternal recall of last menstrual period.
Low prevalence of low birth weight limits statistical power for categorical outcomes.
Correlation between pollutants and environmental factors (temperature, elevation) may affect multipollutant model estimates.

summaries.title: Reduced intellectual development in children with prenatal lead exposure.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We recruited women at 12 weeks of pregnancy and measured BPb every 8 weeks to delivery. We evaluated children with psychometric tests, anthropometric measurements, and BPb at 6-month intervals after birth. We collected data on demographic, socioeconomic, and other factors that might constitute potential confounders or important control variables modifying the relationship between lead and child development.
summaries.summary: Prospective longitudinal cohort study evaluating the association between serial prenatal and postnatal blood lead concentrations and child intelligence quotient (IQ) from ages 6 to 10 in Mexico City.
key_findings: IQ at 6–10 years decreased significantly with increasing natural-log third-trimester BPb (β = –3.90; 95% CI, –6.45 to –1.36).
BPb at week 28 of pregnancy was the only prenatal lead measure significantly predicting lower FSIQ (β = –4.13, p < 0.001).
Higher 28- to 36-week BPb was associated with lower VIQ (β = –3.15, p = 0.007) and PIQ (β = –4.37, p = 0.004).
The logarithmic form of third-trimester BPb fit the data significantly better than a linear functional form (t = 2.15, p = 0.02).
No significant association was found between 6- to 10-year postnatal BPb and FSIQ after adjusting for covariates and other lead measures.
captured_features: Blood lead concentration (BPb) at multiple prenatal and postnatal time points
Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children–Revised (WISC-R) Full-scale, Verbal, and Performance IQ scores
Birth weight, gestational age, Apgar score, child sex
summaries.study_design: Prospective longitudinal cohort study with repeated measures and linear mixed-effects modeling
summaries.population: 175 children born in Mexico City between 1987 and 1992, followed until age 10 (150 with complete data)
summaries.exposure_domain: Prenatal and postnatal lead exposure (blood lead concentration)
limitations: High loss to follow-up from original sample of 321 to 150 with complete data
Relatively small sample size reducing statistical power
Potential test-learning bias from repeated administration of the same IQ test
Use of outdated Spanish versions of WISC-R and WAIS tests
Cultural bias of the HOME scale in the study population

summaries.title: Synergistic effects of traffic-related air pollution and exposure to violence on urban asthma etiology.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We developed geographic information systems (GIS)–based models to retrospectively estimate residential exposures to trafﬁc-related pollution for 413 children in a community-based pregnancy cohort, recruited in East Boston, Massachusetts, between 1987 and 1993, using monthly nitrogen dioxide measurements for 13 sites over 18 years.
summaries.summary: Observational study examining the synergistic effects of traffic-related air pollution (NO2) and exposure to violence (ETV) on childhood asthma etiology in an urban cohort.
key_findings: A 1-SD (4.3 ppb) increase in year-of-diagnosis NO2 was associated with elevated asthma risk solely among children with above-median ETV (adjusted OR = 1.63; 95% CI, 1.14–2.33).
Among lifetime residents, the association was magnified (adjusted OR = 2.40; 95% CI, 1.48–3.88).
No independent effect of ETV alone on asthma was found (OR = 0.98; 95% CI, 0.78–1.22).
The NO2-ETV interaction term was statistically significant (p = 0.03 for full cohort, p = 0.0009 for lifetime residents).
captured_features: NO2 exposure estimates via GIS/LUR models
Maternal education, smoking status, and asthma history
Child sex, age, and residential addresses
summaries.study_design: prospective community-based pregnancy cohort with retrospective exposure assessment
summaries.data_source_type: cohort study with environmental monitoring and questionnaires
summaries.population: 413 children recruited from a community-based pregnancy cohort in East Boston, Massachusetts (1987-1993), followed to age 4-11.5 years
summaries.exposure_domain: traffic-related air pollution (NO2) and exposure to violence (ETV)/chronic stress
limitations: Small sample size for investigating multiplicative effects
Reliance on NO2 as a marker for traffic-related pollution
Incomplete residential history leading to potential exposure misclassification
Potential confounding from indoor NO2 sources and behavioral changes due to violence fear
Recall bias and underreporting in retrospective violence assessment
Lack of long-term psychosocial stress measures beyond ETV

summaries.title: Secondary sex ratio among women exposed to diethylstilbestrol in utero.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were provided by women participating in the National Cancer Institute (NCI) DES Combined Cohort Study.
summaries.summary: Cohort study evaluating the association between in utero diethylstilbestrol (DES) exposure and the secondary sex ratio of offspring among US women.
key_findings: Overall, no significant association was observed between in utero DES exposure and secondary sex ratio (adjusted OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.95–1.17).

Among women with complete dose and timing data (33%), those first exposed earlier in gestation (<13 weeks) and to higher cumulative doses (≥5 g) had a significantly higher odds of a male birth (adjusted OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.04–1.48).
Results did not vary appreciably by maternal age, parity, cohort, or infertility history.
captured_features: gestational timing of first DES exposure
summaries.data_source_type: Research cohort / Questionnaires and medical records
summaries.population: Parous US women (daughters of DES-exposed mothers) from four NCI cohorts
limitations: High proportion of missing data on DES dose and timing (67%)
Reliance on self-reported reproductive and medical history
Potential for residual confounding despite adjustment
Small sample sizes in some cohort subgroup analyses

summaries.title: Vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis: a case report of flaccid monoparesis after oral polio vaccine.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data source was direct clinical assessment, physical examination, laboratory tests, MRI, and electrodiagnostic evaluations on a single patient.
summaries.summary: Case report describing a 4-month-old male infant in Korea who developed acute flaccid paralysis and persistent hypotonic monoparesis following oral polio vaccine administration.
key_findings: First clinically confirmed case of vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis (VAPP) in Korea.
Flaccid paralysis developed 4 weeks after OPV immunization.
Virus isolation from stool and CSF failed.
Persistent hypotonic monoparesis and atrophy remained after 18 months of rehabilitation therapy.
summaries.population: 4-month-old male infant, Korea
limitations: single case report limits generalizability
failed to isolate causative virus strain
diagnosis relied on clinical criteria without virological confirmation

summaries.title: Protection of newborn animals through maternal immunization.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Narrative review of veterinary literature on maternal immunization in animals.
summaries.summary: Narrative review discussing the use of maternal vaccination to provide passive immunity to neonatal animals (calves, puppies, piglets) against infectious diseases, highlighting safety, efficacy, and immunological mechanisms.
key_findings: No original empirical results reported; narrative review summarizing existing veterinary studies on maternal vaccine efficacy and passive immunity transfer.
summaries.population: neonatal animals (calves, puppies, piglets)
limitations: narrative review format
no original quantitative data
focuses on veterinary models rather than human/pediatric populations

summaries.title: Association between traffic-related black carbon exposure and lung function among urban women.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Women were voluntary participants in the Maternal–Infant Smoking Study of East Boston, a prospective cohort originally designed to study the effects of pre- and postnatal tobacco smoke exposure on childhood lung growth and development and respiratory health.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between long-term traffic-related black carbon exposure and lung function among urban women in Boston.
key_findings: BC per IQR increase was associated with a 1.1% decrease in FEV1 (95% CI, –2.5 to 0.3%), a 0.6% decrease in FVC (95% CI, –1.9 to 0.6%), and a 3.0% decrease in FEF25-75% (95% CI, –5.8 to –0.2%).
Former smokers experienced significant reductions in FEV1 (–4.4%), FVC (–3.1%), and FEF25-75% (–8.9%), while current smokers showed no significant effects.
Summer IQR increase in BC was associated with a –1.32% decrease in FEV1 (95% CI, –2.8 to 0.2%), –0.70% in FVC (95% CI, –2.1 to 0.2%), and –3.34% in FEF25-75% (95% CI, –6.3 to –0.4%).
summaries.population: 272 urban women aged 18-42 years recruited from an East Boston community health center during pregnancy
limitations: significant sample attrition over longitudinal follow-up
potential unmeasured or residual confounding, particularly regarding socioeconomic status
restricted variability in individual-level SES due to single-site recruitment
potential exposure misclassification from unmeasured work and other locations
use of predicted rather than observed exposure measurements introducing Berkson-type measurement error
lack of data on other spatially variable pollutants like NO2 and ozone

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to perfluorooctanoate (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonate (PFOS) and maternally reported developmental milestones in infancy.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We obtained data on Apgar scores by linking cohort members to the National Hospital Discharge Register (Copenhagen, Denmark) through use of the unique personal identification number assigned to all Danish residents at birth or immigration.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study investigating associations between maternal plasma PFOA/PFOS levels in early pregnancy and infant motor/mental developmental milestones at 6 and 18 months.
key_findings: No significant association was found between PFC levels and Apgar score (OR for Apgar < 10: 1.20 [95% CI, 0.67–2.14] for PFOS and 1.14 [95% CI, 0.57–2.25] for PFOA).

Children whose mothers had higher PFOS levels were more likely to start sitting without support at a later age (adjusted HR: 0.85 [95% CI, 0.72–0.99] for Q3 and 0.86 [95% CI, 0.73–1.01] for Q4 vs Q1; p for trend = 0.041).
Women with higher PFOS levels were more likely to have babies who did not use word-like sounds (OR for Q4 vs Q1 = 2.93; 95% CI, 1.00–8.56; p for trend = 0.04).
No significant associations were observed between PFOA or PFOS levels and the age when children could walk, or with most other developmental milestones at 6 or 18 months.
captured_features: maternal plasma PFOA and PFOS concentrations
developmental milestone achievement (sitting, walking, language, fine motor, attention, cognition)
maternal and infant demographic and lifestyle covariates
summaries.data_source_type: Birth cohort with national registry linkage
summaries.population: 1,400 pregnant women and their infants from the Danish National Birth Cohort
limitations: potential nondifferential misclassification of exposure and outcomes
residual confounding by childhood exposure variables
multi-collinearity between PFOA and PFOS
strong confounding by parity
lack of highly sensitive developmental measures to rule out subtle effects

summaries.title: Increased reproductive success of women after prenatal undernutrition.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The medical birth records provided information about the mother, the course of the pregnancy and the size of the baby and the placenta at birth. Socio-economic status (SES) of the mothers was based on the occupation of the head of the family at the time of delivery and classified as either manual or non-manual, using the information provided by the birth records. Trained nurses carried out all interviews to collect reproductive and demographic data.
summaries.summary: Investigation of whether prenatal exposure to the Dutch famine of 1944–1945 affected reproductive success (number of children, twinning, age at first delivery, childlessness) in a historical birth cohort traced at age 58.
key_findings: F1 women exposed in utero had more children (mean 2.0 vs 1.7, P=0.002).
Exposed women were younger at first delivery (23.2 vs 23.7 years, P=0.05).
Exposed women had higher twinning rates (OR 2.7 [95% CI 1.1 to 7.0]).
Exposed women were less likely to be childless (OR 0.80 [95% CI 0.66–0.98]).
Adjusted HR for age at first delivery was 0.8 [95% CI 0.6–1.0].
In F1 men, prenatal famine exposure was not associated with any alterations in reproductive success.
captured_features: duration of delay to first pregnancy
summaries.study_design: historical birth cohort study with follow-up interviews
summaries.data_source_type: historical birth registry and follow-up surveys
summaries.population: 2414 live-born singletons born in Amsterdam, Netherlands (1943-1947); 855 participants traced at age 58 (473 women, 382 men)
limitations: 55% participation rate may introduce selection bias
reliance on self-reported reproductive history via interviews
unable to fully rule out genetic confounding for fertility traits

summaries.title: Influence of glutathione S-transferase polymorphisms on cognitive functioning effects induced by p,p'-DDT among preschoolers.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We used data from 326 children assessed in a prospective population-based birth cohort at the age of 4 years.
summaries.summary: Gene-environment interaction study investigating how GSTP1, GSTM1, and GSTT1 polymorphisms modify the association between prenatal p,p´-DDT exposure and neurodevelopmental outcomes at age 4 in a Spanish birth cohort.
key_findings: p,p´-DDT cord serum concentration was inversely associated with general cognitive, memory, quantitative, verbal skills, executive function, and working memory in children with any GSTP1 Val-105 allele (general cognitive β = -8.41, p = 0.04).

Statistically significant gene-environment interactions were found between GSTP1 polymorphisms and prenatal p,p´-DDT exposure for general cognitive skills (p interaction = 0.05), quantitative skills (p = 0.02), executive function (p = 0.01), and working memory (p = 0.02).
No significant associations or interactions were found between p,p´-DDT and cognitive functioning according to GSTM1 and GSTT1 polymorphisms.
p,p´-DDE levels showed weak, non-significant associations with neurodevelopmental scores that were not modified by GST polymorphisms.
captured_features: Cord serum p,p´-DDT and p,p´-DDE concentrations
McCarthy Scales of Children's Abilities (MCSA) scores
summaries.population: 326 preschool children (age 4 years) from Menorca, Spain, born in 1997
limitations: Selection bias due to incomplete genotyping and exposure data
Small subgroup sizes limiting statistical power for interaction analyses
Lack of lipid adjustment for organochlorine measurements
Potential linkage disequilibrium with unmeasured genetic variants

summaries.title: Traffic-related air pollution and respiratory symptoms among asthmatic children, resident in Mexico City: the EVA cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Information concerning allergy test results, medication, and medical visits during the 2 preceding years was obtained from the medical record. The study primarily relied on daily symptom diaries, environmental monitoring stations (RAMA), and traffic counts.
summaries.summary: Prospective longitudinal panel study evaluating the association between traffic-related air pollution and respiratory symptoms/medication use among asthmatic and healthy children in Mexico City.
key_findings: An increase of 17.4 μg/m3 (IQR) in PM2.5 was associated with an 8.8% increase in wheezing (95% CI: 2.4% to 15.5%).
An increase of 34 ppb (IQR) in NO2 was associated with a 9.1% increase in wheezing (95% CI: 2.3% to 16.4%).
An increase of 48 ppb (IQR) in O3 was associated with a 10% increase in wheezing (95% CI: 3.2% to 17.3%).
Diesel-fueled vehicles were significantly associated with wheezing (IRR = 1.29; 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.62) and bronchodilator use (IRR = 1.32; 95% CI: 0.99 to 1.77) per 130 vehicles hourly increase.
Asthmatic children had a 3-fold higher incidence of coughing (IRR = 3.1) and 8.5-fold higher incidence of wheezing (IRR = 8.5) compared to healthy children.
Among healthy children, only NO2 was significantly associated with coughing (OR = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.03 to 1.45).
captured_features: daily symptom diaries (coughing, wheezing, breathing difficulty)
traffic density and vehicle type counts
summaries.data_source_type: environmental monitoring, daily symptom diaries, traffic counts, questionnaires
summaries.population: 147 asthmatic and 50 healthy children aged 6-14 years residing in Mexico City
summaries.exposure_domain: traffic-related air pollution (PM2.5, NO2, O3, diesel exhaust, traffic density)
limitations: exposure assessed via fixed-site monitors potentially causing misclassification
voluntary recruitment not representative of general pediatric population
small subsample for PM2.5 absorbance analysis
high correlation between traffic vehicle types complicating effect separation

summaries.title: Windblown lead carbonate as the main source of lead in blood of children from a seaside community: an example of local birds as "canaries in the mine".
summaries.ehr_evidence: Blood samples were collected from residents who wished to be tested, and analyzed for lead concentration and lead isotope ratios using thermal ionization mass spectrometry.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating blood lead levels and isotopic signatures in children and adults in Esperance, Western Australia, following a community exposure to windblown lead carbonate concentrate from a local port.
key_findings: Mean blood lead level in children was 7.5 µg/dL (range 1.5–25.7 µg/dL; n=49).
Magellan mine lead contributed 27% to 93% (mean 64%, median 71%) to children's blood lead.
A significant positive relationship was found between blood lead concentration and percentage of Magellan lead (R²=0.12, p=0.018).
Estimated background blood lead level for young children was approximately 2.3 µg/dL.
Inhalation of fine lead carbonate particles was identified as a significant exposure pathway for very young children and some adults.
captured_features: percentage contribution from Magellan mine lead
summaries.study_design: cross-sectional observational study with opportunistic blood sampling and isotopic source apportionment
summaries.data_source_type: primary biospecimen collection (blood) and environmental sampling
summaries.population: 49 children (mostly <5 years), 18 adults (>20 years), and 2 cord blood samples from Esperance, Western Australia
summaries.exposure_domain: environmental lead exposure from windblown lead carbonate concentrate at a shipping port
limitations: lack of isotopic data for environmental samples from individual houses
opportunistic sampling biased toward higher blood lead levels
small sample size for some subgroups
inability to fully identify non-Magellan lead sources

summaries.title: Regional and social differences concerning overweight, participation in health check-ups and vaccination. Analysis of data from a whole birth cohort of 6-year old children in a prosperous German city.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The main basis for the analyses are the data from the medical check-up of the cohort starting school in 2004, provided by the Department for Health and Environment of the City of Munich, Germany.
summaries.summary: Analysis of a whole birth cohort of 6-year-old children in Munich, Germany, examining regional and social differences in overweight, preventive health check-up participation, and vaccination coverage.
key_findings: Children with non-German speaking parents had a 2.96 times higher risk of overweight (OR 2.96, 95% CI 2.56–3.42) compared to German-speaking parents.
Non-German speaking parents were associated with higher odds of incomplete health check-ups (OR 2.94, 95% CI 2.63–3.28) but lower odds of incomplete immunizations (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.55–0.66).

School districts with a high percentage of low-education households showed increased odds of overweight (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.47–2.24) and incomplete check-ups (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.40–1.90), but decreased odds of incomplete immunizations (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.68–0.88).
Children without kindergarten attendance had higher odds of incomplete check-ups (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.67–2.56) and incomplete immunizations (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.07–1.59).
captured_features: percentage of single-parent households per school district
percentage of low-education households per school district
summaries.population: 9,353 children starting school in 2004 in Munich, Germany
limitations: Limited number of social and health indicators in the dataset
Lack of environmental exposure data (e.g., air pollution, traffic noise, green spaces)
Overweight classification based on German-specific 90th percentile cutoff
Regional variables act as ecological surrogates
Cross-sectional design limits causal inference

summaries.title: Thyroid hormone levels of pregnant inuit women and their infants exposed to environmental contaminants.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Blood samples were collected in vials containing EDTA as the anticoagulant and centrifuged (10 min, 5,000 rpm), and the plasma transferred into glass vials prewashed with hexane.
summaries.summary: Prospective mother-infant cohort study examining the association between prenatal and postnatal exposure to organochlorine and chlorinated phenolic compounds and thyroid hormone status in pregnant Inuit women and their infants.
key_findings: In pregnant women, a positive association was found between HO-PCBs and T3 concentrations (β = 0.57, p = 0.02).
In umbilical cord blood, PCB-153 concentrations were negatively associated with TBG levels (β = –0.26, p = 0.01).
In a subsample analysis, a negative relationship was found between maternal PCP levels and cord fT4 concentrations in neonates (β = –0.59, p = 0.02).
No association was observed between contaminants and thyroid hormones at 7 months of age.
A significant negative association between PCB-153 and TSH was found in simple regression for 7-month-old infants, but was no longer significant after adjustment for breast-feeding status.
captured_features: maternal plasma PCB-153, HCB, ΣHO-PCBs, PCP, TSH, fT4, T3, TBG, selenium, lipids
cord plasma PCB-153, HCB, ΣHO-PCBs, PCP, TSH, fT4, T3, TBG, selenium
infant plasma PCB-153, HCB, TSH, fT4, T3, TBG
maternal age, parity, socioeconomic status, alcohol/cigarette consumption, fish consumption, gestational age, birth weight, sex, breast-feeding status
summaries.population: Pregnant Inuit women from Nunavik, Québec, Canada, and their infants at birth and 7 months postpartum
summaries.exposure_domain: Environmental contaminants (organochlorines and chlorinated phenolic compounds: PCBs, HCB, HO-PCBs, PCP)
limitations: Small sample size for CPC analysis limits statistical power
Potential selection bias in subsample analyses (e.g., higher birth weight, lower selenium)
Lack of association with cord blood PCP despite high correlation with maternal levels
Unmeasured confounding by iodine intake
Differential thyroid hormone metabolism between fetuses and adults

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to cigarette smoke induces diet- and sex-dependent dyslipidemia and weight gain in adult murine offspring.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study used B6C3F1 mice exposed to mainstream cigarette smoke via whole-body inhalation from gestational day 4 to parturition.
summaries.summary: Controlled experimental study investigating whether prenatal exposure to cigarette smoke alters body weight and plasma lipid profiles in adult murine offspring, with diet and sex as modifying factors.
key_findings: Adult female mice prenatally exposed to MCS demonstrated significantly higher body weight and plasma HDL and LDL levels than air-exposed counterparts.
MCS-exposed dams showed a 31% decrease in triglyceride levels compared to air-exposed dams.
Male offspring prenatally exposed to MCS gained substantially more weight when fed a high-fat diet compared to sex-matched air-exposed controls.
NMR analysis showed significantly increased total LDL particle concentrations in MCS-exposed female offspring (air vs. MCS: 5.9 ± 5.9 vs. 56.6 ± 3.0 nmol/L).
Male offspring exposed to MCS had higher plasma HDL levels on a normal diet (air vs. MCS: 45.5 ± 3.2 vs. 63.6 ± 4.0 mg/dL).
No significant differences were observed in total antioxidant capacity between air- and smoke-exposed groups in either sex.
captured_features: plasma lipid parameters (total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides, phospholipids, albumin, total protein)
lipoprotein subclass particle numbers and sizes (NMR)
summaries.study_design: controlled experimental animal study with in utero exposure and postnatal diet intervention
summaries.population: B6C3F1 mice (pregnant dams and adult offspring, both sexes)
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal cigarette smoke exposure (mainstream cigarette smoke via whole-body inhalation)
limitations: small sample size for NMR analysis (n=3)
protein content differed between normal and high-fat diets, potentially confounding metabolic outcomes
findings are based on a murine model and may not fully translate to human physiology
exact biological mechanisms underlying the observed changes remain unknown

summaries.title: Childhood lead poisoning: conservative estimates of the social and economic benefits of lead hazard control.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data for children with BLLs < 10 μg/dL are estimated from CDC NHANES 2003–2006. Data for > 10 μg/dL are from state-level surveillance and assume uniform distribution of cases within each BLL group.
summaries.summary: Cost-benefit analysis quantifying the social and economic benefits of household lead paint hazard control compared to investment costs for children ≤ 6 years in the US.
key_findings: Each dollar invested in lead paint hazard control results in a return of $17–$221 or a net savings of $181–269 billion.
Total costs of lead hazard control range from $1.2 to $11.0 billion, while total benefits range from $192 to $270 billion.
Lead exposure is associated with 9.3–13.1 million points of IQ loss, translating to $165–233 billion in lost lifetime earnings.
summaries.data_source_type: NHANES survey data and state surveillance data
summaries.population: children ≤ 6 years of age in the United States
limitations: restricts analysis to lead-based paint as the primary source
uses conservative lower bounds for prevalence
excludes indirect crime costs and long-term adult health effects
assumes uniform distribution of BLLs within groups
small sample sizes prevent accurate categorizing of children into each BLL subgroup

summaries.title: Satisfactory safety and immunogenicity of MSP3 malaria vaccine candidate in Tanzanian children aged 12-24 months.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Participant information was captured on paper case report forms (CRFs), which were double-entered into a Microsoft Access data base.
summaries.summary: Phase Ib dose-escalation trial evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of the MSP3 malaria vaccine candidate in Tanzanian children aged 12–24 months.
key_findings: Grade 3 adverse events were infrequent, with only five detected throughout the study, all transient and resolved without sequelae.
Both 15 μg and 30 μg MSP3 dose regimens elicited strong cytophilic IgG1 and IgG3 antibody responses.
At day 84, 100% (15/15) and 83.3% (10/12) of children in the 15 μg and 30 μg MSP3 groups, respectively, showed an 8-fold increase in IgG1 antibodies.
All infants in the comparative analysis seroconverted with a mean titre of 10.68 ± 4.64 AU.
captured_features: solicited local and systemic adverse events
anti-MSP3 antibody titres (IgG, IgG1, IgG3, IgG2, IgG4, IgM)
summaries.study_design: randomized, double-blind, dose-escalation phase Ib clinical trial
summaries.population: children aged 12–24 months in Korogwe, Tanzania
limitations: small sample size (N=45)
subcutaneous administration route for MSP3 versus intramuscular for control may confound reactogenicity comparison
short follow-up period (84 days)
no efficacy or protective outcome data collected

summaries.title: Safety and immunogenicity of an inactivated thimerosal-free influenza vaccine in infants and children.
summaries.ehr_evidence: An AE diary card was used to record solicited local and systemic AEs during the 6 days following the day of vaccination.
summaries.summary: Prospective, open-label, phase III clinical trial evaluating the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of a thimerosal-free inactivated influenza vaccine in healthy children aged 6 months to <9 years.
key_findings: A maximum intensity of severe was reported for injection site pain and fever by only 3.0% and 3.4% of participants, respectively.
≥95% of both younger and older children achieved seroprotection after dose 2.
Of those seronegative at baseline, 97% became seroprotected after dose 1 against A/H3N2 versus 15% for A/H1N1 and 22% for B.
Only one participant had a confirmed case of influenza B after the booster vaccination, but the specimen was compromised during transportation.
captured_features: solicited local and systemic adverse events
summaries.study_design: prospective, open-label, phase III clinical trial
summaries.population: healthy children aged 6 months to <9 years
limitations: lack of a placebo control group
open-label design
single geographic region (Australia)
compromised laboratory specimen for one confirmed influenza case

summaries.title: Childhood incident asthma and traffic-related air pollution at home and school.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Parent-reported physician diagnosis of new-onset asthma (n = 120) was identified during 3 years of follow-up of a cohort of 2,497 kindergarten and first-grade children who were asthma- and wheezing-free at study entry into the Southern California Children’s Health Study.
summaries.summary: Prospective longitudinal cohort study evaluating the association between new-onset childhood asthma and traffic-related air pollution exposure at home and school, along with regional ambient pollutants, in Southern California.
key_findings: Nonfreeway traffic-related pollution (TRP) at home was associated with increased asthma risk (HR 1.51; 95% CI, 1.25–1.81; p < 0.001).
Nonfreeway TRP at school was associated with increased asthma risk (HR 1.45; 95% CI, 1.06–1.98).
Combined weighted exposure at home and school showed a stronger association (HR 1.61; 95% CI, 1.29–2.00).

Ambient NO2 measured at community monitors was associated with increased risk (HR 2.17; 95% CI, 1.18–4.00; p = 0.01), but this association was attenuated (HR 1.37; 95% CI, 0.69–2.71) when adjusted for modeled TRP.
No significant main effects were found for PM10, PM2.5, or O3 on new-onset asthma.
captured_features: central site ambient air pollutant measurements
demographic and clinical covariates from questionnaires
summaries.data_source_type: cohort study with environmental monitoring and questionnaires
summaries.population: 2,497 kindergarten and first-grade children (ages 4.8–9.0 at entry) in Southern California
summaries.exposure_domain: traffic-related air pollution at home and school, regional ambient pollutants
limitations: 3-year follow-up period
retrospective questionnaire assessment of early-life risk factors
conservative TRP estimates for school building centers may underestimate exposure
asthma diagnosis based on parent-reported physician diagnosis may involve misclassification
potential selection bias from loss to follow-up

summaries.title: Efficacy of the pentavalent rotavirus vaccine, RotaTeq®, in Finnish infants up to 3 years of age: the Finnish Extension Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Monitoring for health care encounters in FES followed the same approach that was used to monitor infants in REST... episodes of AGE requiring hospitalisation or an ED visit were collected at prespecified 12-week intervals by automated short message service contacts, sent via mobile phones, or by direct telephone calls... Case report forms in FES were modelled after the case report forms in REST
summaries.summary: Extension study (FES) evaluating the sustained efficacy of the pentavalent rotavirus vaccine (RV5) against rotavirus gastroenteritis and acute gastroenteritis hospitalizations and ED visits in Finnish infants up to 3.1 years post-vaccination.
key_findings: RV5 reduced RVGE hospitalizations and ED visits by 93.8% (95% CI: 90.8–95.9%) over up to 3.1 years.

Vaccine efficacy against combined hospitalizations and ED visits was 93.9% (95% CI: 89.1–96.9%) in children 4-11 months, 94.4% (95% CI: 90.2–97.0%) in 12-23 months, and 85.9% (95% CI: 51.6–97.2%) in 24-35 months.
RV5 reduced all-cause acute gastroenteritis hospitalizations and ED visits by 62.4% (95% CI: 57.6–66.6%).
Efficacy against G1 rotavirus was 95.3% (95% CI: 92.5–97.2%), but results for G4 were not significant due to low case numbers.
No cases of intussusception were observed during the FES period.
captured_features: rotavirus genotypes (G1, G2, G3, G4, G9)
summaries.study_design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (extension study)
summaries.population: Finnish infants enrolled at 6-13 weeks of age, followed up to 3.1 years post-vaccination
limitations: Small number of cases in year 3 limiting statistical power
Too few encounters for G2 and G4 serotypes to demonstrate significant efficacy
Wide confidence intervals for efficacy beyond 24 months
Variation in follow-up duration due to rolling enrollment

summaries.title: Temporal and spatial patterns of ambient endotoxin concentrations in Fresno, California.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Daily ambient endotoxin and air pollutants were collected at the central ambient monitoring site of the California Air Resources Board in Fresno and, for shorter time periods, at 10 schools and indoors and outdoors at 84 residences in the community.
summaries.summary: Characterization of the temporal and spatial variability of ambient endotoxin concentrations in Fresno, California, and identification of meteorologic and land-use correlates.
key_findings: Daily endotoxin concentrations were primarily driven by meteorologic factors, particularly air recirculation and relative humidity (model R2 = 0.55).
Highest concentrations were found in areas immediately downwind from agricultural/pasture land and concentrated animal feeding operations.
PMc was the only measured air pollutant correlated with endotoxin (R2 = 0.44 with PMc vs 0.15 with PM2.5).
Endotoxin was the most spatially variable pollutant, with coefficients of variation ranging from 0.08 to 0.75.
Geometric mean concentrations were lowest in the wet season (<0.7 EU/m3) and highest in the dry season (>2 EU/m3).
summaries.population: children 6-11 years with clinically active asthma (FACES cohort) and Fresno/Clovis community residents
limitations: analysis restricted to dry season months (May-October)
spatial mapping based on only 22 days
lack of daily data on potential source emissions
residential sampling was not a random sample

summaries.title: Determinants of age at menarche in the UK: analyses from the Breakthrough Generations Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Age at menarche data were collected retrospectively by questionnaire from 81 606 women aged 16 – 98, resident in the UK and participating in the Breakthrough Generations Study.
summaries.summary: Cohort study investigating determinants of age at menarche using self-reported questionnaire data from over 80,000 UK women.
key_findings: Menarche occurred earlier in women with low birthweight (Ptrend < 0.001), singletons (P < 0.001), prenatal pre-eclampsia (P < 0.001) or maternal smoking (P = 0.01), not breastfed (Ptrend = 0.03), non-white (P < 0.001), heavy or tall at age 7 (Ptrend < 0.001), and those who exercised little (Ptrend < 0.001).
Menarcheal age increased with number of siblings (P < 0.001) and had an inverse association with birth order (P < 0.001).
In the multivariate model, birthweight, ethnicity, weight, height, exercise, sibship size, birth order, and maternal age at birth remained significant.

A non-white girl who was much heavier and taller than peers at age 7 could reach menarche nearly 2 years earlier on average (difference = -22.8 months, 95% CI = -25.0 to -20.7 months) compared to a white girl of average weight and height.
Birthweight per 500 g increase was associated with 0.31 months later menarche in univariate analysis and 1.24 months in multivariate analysis.
No significant association was found with maternal age at birth in univariate analysis (Ptrend = 0.15) or vegetarian status before age 8 (P = 0.18).
summaries.population: 81,606 UK women aged 16-98 years
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal and early-life factors (birthweight, maternal smoking, pre-eclampsia, breastfeeding, childhood anthropometrics, exercise, family size, birth order, ethnicity, maternal age)
limitations: volunteer recruitment bias
retrospective self-reported data with recall error
survivor bias among older participants
imprecise measures of childhood weight and height
large amounts of missing data for breastfeeding and maternal smoking variables

summaries.title: Impact of air pollution on pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms in children. Longitudinal repeated-measures study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Environmental monitoring network of Salamanca and direct clinical/demographic data collection via questionnaires and spirometry.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal repeated-measures study assessing the impact of ambient air pollution on pulmonary function and respiratory symptoms in school-age children in Salamanca, Mexico.
key_findings: Obstructive lung function abnormalities were more frequent in highly exposed students (10.4% vs. 5.3%; OR = 1.95, 95% CI 1.0-3.7).
A 10 μg/m3 increase in PM10 was associated with increased wheezing (OR = 1.0478), rhinorrhea (OR = 1.0318), ARTI (OR = 1.0977), and dyspnea (OR = 1.0184).
An IQR increase in PM10 (18.8 μg/m3) was associated with 3-month deficits in FEV1 of -0.37% in girls and -0.43% in boys.
No significant effects were observed for NO2 on respiratory symptoms.
captured_features: air pollutant levels (O3, SO2, NO, NO2, NOx, PM10)
summaries.data_source_type: Environmental monitoring and direct clinical/demographic data collection
summaries.population: 464 school-age children (6-14 years) from two public schools in Salamanca, Mexico
summaries.exposure_domain: Ambient air pollution (O3, SO2, NO, NO2, NOx, PM10)
limitations: Lacked a non-polluted control area
Small sample size
Results cannot be generalized due to particular environmental and geographic features
Potential confounding from multi-collinearity among air pollution and weather variables
Unmeasured characteristics such as natural allergens, other pollutants, seasonal viral infections, and genetic predisposition

summaries.title: Low-level environmental lead exposure in childhood and adult intellectual function: a follow-up study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We recruited adults in the Boston area who had participated as newborns and young children in a prospective cohort study that examined the relationship between lead exposure and childhood intellectual function.
summaries.summary: Follow-up study assessing the relationship between early-life environmental lead exposure and adult intellectual function in a prospective cohort.
key_findings: Childhood blood-lead concentration (mean of ages 4 and 10) had the strongest relationship with Full-Scale IQ (b = -1.89 ± 0.70, p = 0.01).
Full-scale IQ was significantly related to blood-lead concentration at age 6 months (b = -1.66 ± 0.75, p = 0.03), 4 years (b = -0.90 ± 0.41, p = 0.03), and 10 years (b = -1.95 ± 0.80, p = 0.02).
Adjusting for maternal IQ altered the significance of the regression coefficient for blood lead.
captured_features: blood lead concentrations at multiple time points
summaries.population: adults aged 28-30 years (n=43) originally enrolled as newborns in a Boston cohort (1979-1981)
limitations: small sample size (n=43)
limited ability to perform multivariate analysis
potential confounding by maternal IQ cannot be excluded

summaries.title: Molecular Epidemiology, prenatal exposure and prevention of cancer.
summaries.ehr_evidence: In the New York City -based “Mothers and Newborns Cohort Study ”, pregnant mothers wore personal air monitors to measure their exposure to PAHs during pregnancy [9].
summaries.summary: Review and summary of molecular epidemiology studies on prenatal environmental exposures and their association with biomarkers of cancer risk in a birth cohort.
key_findings: Maternal and cord white blood cells had equivalent levels of PAH-DNA adducts despite the estimated fetal dose being about 10 times lower.
High prenatal PAH exposure was associated with a higher frequency of stable chromosomal aberrations in cord blood.
Global DNA methylation levels in cord blood decreased with increasing prenatal PAH exposure.
Global DNA methylation levels in cord blood were positively correlated with levels of PAH-DNA adducts.
Methylation levels in cord blood and blood collected at age 3 did not vary significantly over time.
captured_features: PAH-DNA adducts in cord and maternal blood
chromosomal aberrations in cord blood lymphocytes
global DNA methylation levels in cord blood
summaries.study_design: birth cohort study / molecular epidemiology perspective
summaries.data_source_type: birth cohort with biospecimen and environmental monitoring
summaries.population: pregnant mothers and newborns in New York City
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal environmental exposures (PAHs, tobacco smoke, pesticides, solvents, radiation, endocrine disruptors)
limitations: measured overall DNA methylation levels rather than specific genes
observational design
focus on biomarkers rather than clinical disease outcomes
limited to specific geographic cohort

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to perfluorinated chemicals and behavioral or coordination problems at age 7 years.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We used data from the Danish National Birth Cohort, which enrolled mothers in early pregnancy, and we measured maternal blood levels of PFOA and PFOS using specimens drawn around 8 weeks of gestation.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study investigating whether prenatal exposure to PFOA and PFOS is associated with behavioral or coordination problems in children at age 7.
key_findings: No significant association between maternal PFOA or PFOS levels and behavioral problems (SDQ total difficulties OR=0.91, 95% CI: 0.43–1.92 for highest vs lowest PFOA quartile) or motor coordination disorders (DCD OR=1.14, 95% CI: 0.46–2.81).

Inverse associations were observed for some PFOA quartiles with emotional symptoms (OR=0.48, 95% CI: 0.24–0.97) and hyperactivity (OR=0.51, 95% CI: 0.28–0.94), but overall background levels were not associated with neurodevelopmental problems.
captured_features: maternal plasma PFOA and PFOS concentrations
summaries.population: children aged 7 years from the Danish National Birth Cohort (n=787 for behavioral outcomes, n=537 for coordination outcomes)
limitations: selection bias due to higher socioeconomic status and healthier characteristics of participating mothers
loss to follow-up with approximately 35% not completing the 7-year interview
reliance on parent-reported questionnaires for outcomes
background exposure levels may not reflect high-dose effects observed in animal studies

summaries.title: Exposure to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during pregnancy and the risk of selected birth defects: a prospective cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data on NSAID exposure were available from a self-administered questionnaire completed around gestational week 17. Information on pregnancy outcome was obtained from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating associations between maternal NSAID use during the first 12 weeks of gestation and selected birth defects using data from the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study linked to the Medical Birth Registry of Norway.
key_findings: No significant association between overall NSAID exposure and selected birth defects (adjusted OR 0.7, 95% CI 0.4–1.1).
No significant associations found for specific NSAID types or congenital heart defects, septal defects, ventricular septal defects, or atrial septal defects.
Increased risk observed for septal defects with multiple NSAID exposure (crude OR 3.9, 95% CI 0.9–15.7), but based on only 2 exposed cases.
summaries.population: pregnant women in Norway enrolled in the MoBa cohort (1999-2006), n=67,891 after exclusions
summaries.exposure_domain: maternal NSAID use during gestational weeks 0-12
limitations: self-reported exposure via questionnaire
small number of exposed cases for specific birth defects
low participation rate (43.5%)
potential outcome misclassification in registry
confounding by indication

summaries.title: An integrated, multistudy analysis of the safety of Ann Arbor strain live attenuated influenza vaccine in children aged 2-17 years.
summaries.ehr_evidence: An integrated analysis of randomized, controlled trials of LAIV.
summaries.summary: Integrated safety analysis of Ann Arbor strain live attenuated influenza vaccine in children aged 2–17 years across 20 randomized controlled trials.
key_findings: LAIV recipients exhibited increased runny/stuffy nose (+7% vs placebo, +12% vs TIV, P<0.01), headache (+7%, P=0.02), and tiredness/decreased activity (+2%, P=0.03) after dose 1.
Higher rate of decreased appetite (+4%) was observed after year 2 revaccination (P=0.03).
No evidence of an increase in any potential vaccine-related serious adverse event in LAIV recipients.
No evidence that lower respiratory illness or wheezing illness occurred at a higher rate in LAIV recipients aged 2–17 years or specifically 24–35 months.
summaries.study_design: integrated analysis of randomized controlled trials
summaries.population: children aged 2–17 years
limitations: unadjusted P-values for multiplicity
aggregation across different annual vaccine formulations and seasons
data from multiple studies with varying follow-up periods

summaries.title: The influence of BCG vaccine strain on mycobacteria-specific and non-specific immune responses in a prospective cohort of infants in Uganda.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were collected from the Entebbe Mother and Baby Study, a prospective birth cohort in Uganda, using questionnaires, blood samples, ELISA assays, and clinical follow-up.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating the influence of three BCG vaccine strains (Russia, Bulgaria, Denmark) on mycobacteria-specific and non-specific immune responses, scarring, adverse events, and mortality in 1341 infants in Uganda.
key_findings: BCG-Denmark immunised infants showed the highest cytokine responses, with significantly higher IFN-γ geometric mean ratios compared to BCG-Russia across all stimuli (e.g., GMR 2.24 for cCFP, 3.09 for PHA).
BCG scar frequency differed significantly by strain: 52.2% for Russia, 64.1% for Bulgaria, and 92.6% for Denmark (p < 0.001).
Infants with BCG scars had higher IFN-γ and IL-13 responses to mycobacterial antigens than those without scars.
BCG-related adverse events were highest in the Denmark group (1.8%) compared to Russia (0.3%) and Bulgaria (1.0%) (p = 0.025).
Mortality differences between strain groups were not significant (HR 1.22 for Denmark vs Russia, 95% CI 0.42-3.53, p = 0.87).
summaries.population: 1341 infants from the Entebbe Mother and Baby Study in Uganda, followed up to 12 months of age
limitations: Not randomised to BCG strain, potential for confounding by seasonal exposures
Underpowered to detect significant mortality differences
Could not analyse TB outcomes or long-term effects
Analysis was a post-hoc subset of the original trial

summaries.title: Poor maternal nutrition programmes a pro-atherosclerotic phenotype in ApoE-/- mice.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Experimental animal model using pregnant ApoE− / − mice and their male offspring.
summaries.summary: Experimental study investigating the effect of maternal low-protein diet on atherosclerotic lesion development and progression in 6-month-old male ApoE− / − mice.
key_findings: LP offspring had significantly greater total plaque area per animal compared with controls (P<0.05).
LP offspring had significantly greater total cholesterol cleft containing area (P<0.05).
LP offspring showed significantly reduced vascular smooth muscle cell content (SMA staining: control 5.7%, LP 2.8%, P<0.05).
DNA damage marker p-H2AX was significantly increased in plaques of LP offspring (control 14, LP 36 cells/100,000 μm2, P<0.05).
Total and LDL-cholesterol levels were significantly higher in LP offspring (Total: control 6.73±1.01, LP 9.77±0.78 mmol/l, P<0.05; LDL: control 4.62±0.70, LP 8.65±0.70 mmol/l, P<0.01).
HMG-CoA reductase expression was significantly increased in the livers of LP offspring (P<0.05).
No significant differences were observed in HDL-cholesterol, triacylglycerol, non-esterified fatty acids, fasting glucose, Mac3, or p-ATM between groups.
summaries.population: male ApoE− / − mice at 6 months of age
limitations: limited to male offspring
animal model may not fully replicate human pathophysiology
mechanisms linking in utero exposure to atherosclerosis require further elucidation

summaries.title: Maternal Distress during Pregnancy and Offspring Childhood Overweight.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We performed a cohort study using prospective data from 37,764 women and child dyads from the Danish National Birth Cohort (1996–2002).
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between maternal distress during pregnancy and offspring childhood overweight at age 7.
key_findings: No significant association between maternal distress during pregnancy and childhood overweight at age 7 (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96–1.18).
A modest, non-significant increased risk of overweight was observed in boys (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.99–1.33) but not in girls (OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.85–1.13).
Maternal worrying during pregnancy was associated with a slightly increased risk of childhood overweight (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00–1.22).
Children of mothers with low or medium socioeconomic status had an increased risk of overweight.
captured_features: maternal anxiety, depression, and stress scores
maternal age, parity, prepregnancy BMI, smoking, exercise, gestational weight gain, breastfeeding duration
summaries.population: 37,764 mother-child dyads from the Danish National Birth Cohort, children aged approximately 7 years
limitations: self-reported exposure and outcome data
potential selection bias due to 40% loss to follow-up
relatively low exposure contrast in a healthy, high-SES cohort
single time-point measurement of childhood overweight

summaries.title: Childhood brain tumours and use of mobile phones: comparison of a case-control study with incidence data.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Rates are shown for the age group 5 –19 years living in the Nordic Countries obtained from NORDCAN
summaries.summary: Commentary responding to a previous critique, arguing that stable childhood brain tumour incidence trends in the Nordic countries are inconsistent with the increased risk suggested by the CEFALO case-control study on mobile phone use.
key_findings: Commentary presents no new primary quantitative results; argues that stable childhood brain tumour incidence trends in the Nordic countries over the last 20 years are inconsistent with the increased risk suggested by the CEFALO case-control study.
summaries.population: children and adolescents aged 5-19 years in the Nordic countries
limitations: reliance on retrospective self-reported exposure in the referenced case-control study
ecological comparison limitations
potential age-specific underreporting in cancer registry data

summaries.title: Pilot study of pesticide knowledge, attitudes, and practices among pregnant women in northern Thailand.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Questionnaires were administered via face-to-face interview in Thai language by two study nurses trained in basic interview techniques.
summaries.summary: Pilot cross-sectional survey assessing pesticide knowledge, attitudes, and practices among 76 pregnant women in northern Thailand to identify factors associated with unsafe pesticide use behaviors.
key_findings: Lower knowledge score and earliest trimester of pregnancy were marginally (p < 0.1) associated with unsafe practices in the home, but not at work.

Women who worked in agriculture or applied pesticides before becoming pregnant, or who had a previous child were significantly (p < 0.05) more likely to engage in unsafe behaviors in the home during their current pregnancy.
Risky behaviors at home were marginally associated with knowledge score (OR=0.9, 95% CI 0.7-1.0, p=0.10).
Risky behaviors at home were significantly associated with first trimester in univariate analysis (OR=5.0, 95% CI 1.1-23.9, p=0.04).

Risky behaviors at home were significantly associated with farmwork before pregnancy (OR=9.5, 95% CI 2.2-41.8, p<0.01), pesticide application before pregnancy (OR=12.2, 95% CI 2.0-75.1, p=0.01), previous child (OR=4.1, 95% CI 1.0-15.7, p=0.04), and child susceptibility score (OR=5.8, 95% CI 1.4-24.7, p=0.02).
Risky behaviors at work were significantly associated with risky behaviors at home (OR=2.2, 95% CI 1.1-4.5, p=0.03).
summaries.population: 76 pregnant women in Fang District, Chiang Mai Province, Thailand
summaries.exposure_domain: Pesticide exposure (knowledge, attitudes, practices, and unsafe behaviors)
limitations: Small sample size (n=76)
Self-reported data subject to social desirability and reporting bias
Lack of full validation study for questionnaire
Proxy measures for exposure rather than direct biomonitoring
Cross-sectional design limits causal inference
