summaries.title: Early metabolic defects in dexamethasone-exposed and undernourished intrauterine growth restricted rats.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Female and male (275–325 g) Sprague-Dawley OFA rats (Charles River Laboratories, France) were used for breeding and housed under specific pathogen-free conditions in an environmentally-controlled clean room at the School of Medicine animal facilities (Medical Center University, University of Geneva).
summaries.summary: Experimental study modeling intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) in rat pups via prenatal dexamethasone exposure or maternal undernutrition to assess early metabolic, pancreatic, and adipose tissue defects before weaning.
key_findings: DEX and UN pups had ~13% and 17% lower birth weight than controls (p<0.0001).
Hepatic Pck1 and G6pc mRNA increased by 46±19% and 101±35% in DEX pups, and 53±7% and 85±20% in UN pups at PND7 (p<0.05).
Basal glycaemia at PND21 was elevated in DEX (6.9±0.1 mmol/l) and UN (6.8±0.1 mmol/l) pups vs controls (6.2±0.2 mmol/l) (p<0.02).
GTT AUC was increased in DEX (868±27) and UN (870±26) pups vs controls (693±16 mmol/L*min) (p<0.0001).
Pancreatic islet number was reduced in DEX (62±5) and UN (52±4) pups vs controls (82±4 islets/section) (p<0.01).
Mean islet size was reduced in DEX (1462±66) and UN (1612±79) pups vs controls (1917±80 μm²) (p<0.02).
UN pups exhibited decreased glucose-induced insulin secretion at 15 min (0.51±0.09 vs 0.89±0.11 ng/mL, p<0.02).
DEX pups showed attenuated glycaemia drop in insulin tolerance test, indicating reduced insulin sensitivity.
UN pups had reduced epididymal white adipose tissue mass at PND21 (44±5 mg vs 71±7 mg controls, p<0.01).
captured_features: hepatic Pck1 and G6pc mRNA and protein levels
circulating corticosterone, leptin, insulin, and C-peptide levels
adipose tissue mass and gene expression
summaries.population: Sprague-Dawley rat pups (PND0-PND28) and gestating dams
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal dexamethasone exposure, maternal undernutrition (caloric restriction)
limitations: study restricted to pre-weaning period without catch-up growth
physiological tests performed only on male pups to avoid sex confounding
insulin tolerance test less sensitive than euglycaemic hyperinsulinemic clamps
rat model limitations for direct human translation

summaries.title: Assessment of prenatal exposure to arsenic in Tenerife Island.
summaries.ehr_evidence: A structured questionnaire on sociodemographic, lifestyle and dietary habits during pregnancy was administered to all participants the day after the delivery. Neonatal meconium was collected from the infant’s diaper.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional study evaluating prenatal arsenic exposure via meconium analysis in 96 mother-infant pairs in Tenerife, Spain, and its association with maternal diet, lifestyle, and neonatal outcomes.
key_findings: Prenatal arsenic exposure was detected in 38.5% of meconium samples.
Frequent vegetable intake was associated with detectable arsenic (OR: 1.31; 95% CI: 1.02–1.68).
Low weekly egg intake was associated with arsenic exposure (OR: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.34–0.94).
Children with detectable arsenic had significantly higher birth weight (OR: 1.00; 95% CI: 1.00–1.02).
No significant association was found between arsenic exposure and other obstetric or perinatal outcomes (p > 0.05).
summaries.population: 96 pregnant women and their newborns in Tenerife, Spain
limitations: no arsenic speciation data to differentiate inorganic vs organic forms
small sample size (n=96)
cross-sectional design prevents causal inference
dietary intake based on self-reported frequency rather than quantitative mg/day
results limited to Tenerife and not generalizable

summaries.title: Maternal and offspring fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes-associated genetic variants and cognitive function at age 8: a Mendelian randomization study in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Extensive data have been collected from the mothers and their offspring from pregnancy onwards by questionnaire, abstraction from medical notes, record linkage and by attendance at research clinics.
summaries.summary: Mendelian randomization study investigating the causal relationship between maternal and offspring genetic risk scores for fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes and childhood cognitive function (IQ) at age 8 in the ALSPAC cohort.
key_findings: Maternal and offspring FGGRS were not associated with child IQ.
Maternal T2DGRS was positively associated with offspring IQ (mean difference 0.47, 95% CI 0.12, 0.81; p=0.01).
Offspring of mothers with diabetes/glycosuria had lower IQ scores (mean difference -3.5, 95% CI -5.6, -1.5; p=0.001).
FGGRS was strongly associated with offspring fasting glucose and HbA1c levels.
No association was found between offspring T2DGRS and child IQ.
captured_features: confounders (maternal age, education, smoking, birthweight, gestational age)
summaries.study_design: Mendelian randomization study within a prospective birth cohort
summaries.population: Mothers and offspring from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC) cohort, Bristol, England
summaries.exposure_domain: Genetic risk scores for fasting glucose and type 2 diabetes
limitations: Lack of statistical power to detect small effects
Most participants had fasting glucose and HbA1c levels within the normal range
Genetic risk scores may not fully capture the disease phenotype or environmental confounders
Associations with individual SNPs disappeared after Bonferroni correction

summaries.title: Prenatal p,p´-DDE exposure and neurodevelopment among children 3.5-5 years of age.
summaries.ehr_evidence: In 2001 we started a perinatal cohort study in four municipalities in the state of Morelos, Mexico, an endemic area for malaria where DDT was used until 1998 as part of an anti-malaria campaign.
summaries.summary: Prospective perinatal cohort study assessing the association between prenatal DDE exposure and child neurodevelopment at 42–60 months of age in Morelos, Mexico.
key_findings: A doubling of serum DDE in the third trimester was associated with statistically significant reductions of –1.37, –0.88, –0.84, and –0.80 points in the general cognitive index, quantitative, verbal, and memory components, respectively.

Among children with DDE measurements in all three trimesters, third-trimester DDE was significantly associated with reductions of –2.01, –2.06, –1.14, and –1.26 points in GCI, quantitative, verbal, and memory components, respectively.
Average DDE exposure during pregnancy was significantly associated with a –1.78 point reduction in the quantitative component (95% CI: –3.2, –0.4; p = 0.01).
No significant statistical interactions with sex or breastfeeding were observed.
captured_features: McCarthy Scales of Children’s Abilities components
summaries.population: 203 children aged 3.5–5 years (42–60 months) and their mothers from Morelos, Mexico
limitations: Lack of information regarding postnatal DDE exposure
Lack of validation of the McCarthy Scale in the Mexican population
Potential residual confounding
Attrition rate of about 30% before 42 months
Lack of information on postnatal lead exposure or infant nutrition

summaries.title: Prospective surveillance study of acute respiratory infections, influenza-like illness and seasonal influenza vaccine in a cohort of juvenile idiopathic arthritis patients.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Routine clinical evaluations, including the Pediatric American College of Rheumatology 30% ( ACRPed30) were conducted during both surveillance periods prior to and at 30, 90 and 180 days after influenza vaccination.
summaries.summary: Prospective surveillance study evaluating the frequency and impact of acute respiratory infections and influenza-like illness on juvenile idiopathic arthritis disease activity, and assessing the immunogenicity and safety of the influenza vaccine in JIA patients.
key_findings: 105 ARI episodes were reported, with 26.6% classified as ILI.
60% of 33 respiratory samples were positive for at least one virus, with influenza and rhinovirus detected in 30% of samples.
20% of 50 observed JIA flares were temporally associated with ARI episodes.
Influenza seroprotection rates exceeded 70% (91-100%) and seroconversion rates exceeded 40% (74-93%).
Patients using anti-TNF alpha drugs presented lower seroconversion to the H1N1 strain (p=0.03).
No significant differences were found in ACRPed30 scores after vaccination (p=0.22).
No patient reported ILI symptoms during the 6-month post-vaccination follow-up period.
summaries.population: children and adolescents with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), mean age 10.7-11.0 years, Brazil
summaries.exposure_domain: respiratory viral infections and influenza vaccination
limitations: small sample size
observational design limits causal inference between ARI and JIA flares
potential confounding by seasonality and immunosuppressive therapy
lack of statistical power to adjust for all covariates

summaries.title: Clonal expansion within pneumococcal serotype 6C after use of seven-valent vaccine.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from children aged four years and under with written parental/guardian informed consent... All serotype 6C invasive disease isolates (n = 4) from blood or cerebrospinal fluid specimens received by the HPA South East regional microbiology laboratory between 2006 and 2010 were included
summaries.summary: Genomic epidemiology study investigating clonal expansion and genetic diversity of Streptococcus pneumoniae serotype 6C following PCV7 vaccine introduction in Southampton, England.
key_findings: Serotype 6C carriage increased fourfold from 3.8% in 2006/7 to 13.5% and 13.7% in subsequent winters.
The largest clonal complex (CC395) comprised 12 isolates and was uniquely characterized by a lantibiotic synthesis locus.
Single nucleotide polymorphisms separating isolates from the reference strain ranged from 8 to 19,829, with up to 172 SNPs within the CC395 clonal complex.
One carriage isolate (SOT2029) showed resistance to erythromycin and tetracycline and carried ermB and tetM resistance genes.
Two invasive isolates clustered together despite being collected two years apart, indicating persistence of a virulent clone.
summaries.study_design: Genomic epidemiology study using whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic network analysis
summaries.population: Children aged ≤4 years (carriage) and adult patients (invasive disease) in Southampton, England
limitations: Small sample size (n=19 sequenced isolates)
Single geographical location (Southampton, England)
Cross-sectional collection limits temporal causal inference

summaries.title: Environmental factors predicting blood lead levels in pregnant women in the UK: the ALSPAC study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study sample was derived from the ALSPAC study, a population-based study investigating environmental and genetic influences on the health, behaviour and development of children.
summaries.summary: Observational cohort study assessing environmental, lifestyle, and socioeconomic factors associated with blood lead levels in pregnant women and their children in the UK.
key_findings: Mean maternal blood lead level was 3.67 ± 1.47 mg/dl (n=4285).
Higher educational qualification was a strong independent predictor of BLL ≥5 mg/dl (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12–1.42; p<0.001).
Cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, coffee drinking, and coal fire heating were independently associated with increased BLL.
Dietary calcium intake and iron supplementation showed protective effects against high lead levels.
Maternal and child BLL at 30 months were significantly correlated (r = 0.278, n = 233; p<0.001).
summaries.population: pregnant women in the Avon area of the UK (n=4285) and their children at 30 months
summaries.exposure_domain: environmental lead exposure, lifestyle factors, diet, and socioeconomic status
limitations: selection bias (women with BLL data were older and more educated than the full cohort)
lack of data on housing age and renovation activities
modest effect sizes (odds ratios)
child BLL samples analyzed using different methods and at different times than maternal samples

summaries.title: Exposure to the Chinese famine in early life and the risk of anaemia in adulthood.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We used the data of 2007 adults born between 1954 and 1964 in Jiangsu province from the 2002 Chinese National Nutrition and Health Survey.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional analysis examining the association between early life exposure to the Chinese famine (1959–1961) and the risk of anaemia in adulthood.
key_findings: Fetal exposure to famine was associated with a 37% increased risk of anaemia compared to non-exposed (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.09-1.71).
The association was stronger in men (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.21-2.87), overweight/obese individuals (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.20-2.56), and those with low education (RR 2.07, 95% CI 1.37-3.12).
No significant association between famine exposure and anaemia was found among urban residents.
Total iron intake did not differ significantly across famine exposure groups.
summaries.population: 2007 adults born between 1954 and 1964 in Jiangsu province, China
limitations: Lack of iron metabolism biomarkers and menstruation status data
Unassessed regional variation in famine severity
Small sample size in fetal-exposed group limiting subgroup power
Potential selection bias from selective mortality or reduced fertility
Absence of inflammation biomarkers to explore anaemia aetiology

summaries.title: Monitoring the immune response to vaccination with an inactivated vaccine associated to bovine neonatal pancytopenia by deep sequencing transcriptome analysis in cattle.
summaries.ehr_evidence: For this study, jugular blood was taken i mmediately prior a further booster vaccination with PregSure® and 14 days later.
summaries.summary: Experimental RNAseq study monitoring the immune response to vaccination with an inactivated BVDV vaccine in cattle, identifying a novel cytokine-like gene and coordinated immune pathways.
key_findings: 2901 differentially expressed loci at a significance threshold of q < 0.05.
Novel locus XLOC_032517 showed a highly significant (p < 0.0001) 3.51 fold upregulation after vaccination.

Three cows that had never encountered PregSure® vaccination showed a significantly lower XLOC_032517 expression (p = 0.008) compared to the 12 cows which had received at least three PregSure® vaccinations.
Pathway analysis revealed coordinated immune response to dsRNA or a dsRNA analogue, upregulation of T cell response, and suppression of B cell activation.
summaries.population: 12 lactating and non-lactating cows aged three to five years (German Holstein × Charolais crossbred)
limitations: RNAseq restricted to blood transcriptome
small sample size (n=12)
lack of functional annotation for novel locus XLOC_032517

summaries.title: Deep phenotyping of the unselected COPSAC2010 birth cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: All information was obtained by personal interview at clinical visits by medical doctors (MDs) and research assistants both with paediatric training. Medical, familial, environmental, and socio-economic histories were assessed by predeﬁned questions and closed response categories and entered online into a dedicated database running an audit trail (Oracle database on a Novel SQL server).
summaries.summary: Cohort description of the COPSAC 2010 birth study, detailing recruitment, deep phenotyping protocols, biobanking, and embedded randomized controlled trials investigating perinatal exposures and genetic interactions on childhood allergic and inflammatory diseases.
key_findings: 738 mothers were recruited from week 24 of gestation, and 700 of their children were included in the birth cohort.
Adherence was high with 685 children (98%) attending the 1 year clinic visit and 667 children (95%) attending the 2 year visit.
Participants had a higher prevalence of asthma, eczema, and hayfever, and higher income/education levels compared to non-participants.
summaries.study_design: prospective longitudinal birth cohort study with embedded randomized controlled trials
summaries.population: unselected cohort of pregnant women and their offspring in eastern Denmark, followed from pregnancy/infancy to age 3+ years
summaries.exposure_domain: perinatal exposures, human microbiome, maternal nutrition, environmental factors, medications
limitations: over-representation of atopic parents
recruitment bias towards higher socioeconomic status
intensive follow-up schedule
primary outcome data not yet analyzed

summaries.title: Progress in immunization information systems--United States, 2011.
summaries.ehr_evidence: CDC annually surveys 56 immunization program grantees using the IIS Annual Report (IISAR).
summaries.summary: Report on progress in U.S. Immunization Information Systems in 2011, assessing child participation rates and completeness of core vaccination data elements.
key_findings: Nationally, 19.2 million U.S. children aged <6 years (84%) participated in an IIS in 2011.
32 of 54 grantees (59%) included fields for all 18 NVAC core data elements in their IIS.
Completeness of vaccine manufacturer and lot number fields increased from 37% in 2006 to 63% and 60%, respectively, in 2011.
captured_features: vaccine manufacturer and lot number fields
summaries.study_design: Cross-sectional surveillance report based on annual grantee survey
summaries.population: U.S. children aged <6 years; 54 immunization program grantees
limitations: Data from the IISAR were self-reported and self-validated.
Nationwide participation and completeness rates may be underestimated or overestimated because two of 56 grantees did not report data.

summaries.title: Selenium protects neonates against neurotoxicity from prenatal exposure to manganese.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were collected prospectively through face-to-face interviews, umbilical cord blood sampling, and clinical NBNA tests.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the protective effect of prenatal selenium against manganese-induced neurotoxicity in neonates using cord blood metal levels and behavioral assessments.
key_findings: High cord blood Mn (≥P75, ≥9.1 μg/L) was associated with lower NBNA scores (adjusted ß = -1.2, 95% CI: -1.4 to -1.0, p<0.001) and higher risk of low NBNA (adjusted OR = 8.0, 95% CI: 2.8 to 23.0, p<0.001).

With low cord Se (<P50, <63.1 μg/L), Mn was negatively associated with NBNA scores (adjusted ß = -1.1, 95% CI: -1.3 to -0.9, p<0.001) and increased risk of low NBNA (adjusted OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 2.8 to 11.5, p<0.001).
With high cord Se (≥P50, ≥63.1 μg/L), the adverse effect of Mn was attenuated (NBNA: adjusted ß = 0.1, 95% CI: -0.3 to 0.5, p = 0.746; Low NBNA: adjusted OR = 4.5, 95% CI: 0.4 to 46.7, p = 0.205).
High Mn/low Se group had significantly lower NBNA scores than high Mn/high Se group (38.0 ± 1.6 vs 39.5 ± 0.9, p<0.001).
Mn/Se ratio was moderately correlated with NBNA scores (r = -0.41, p<0.001).
summaries.data_source_type: primary prospective cohort (interviews, biospecimens, clinical exams)
summaries.population: 933 term newborns and mothers in Shanghai, China (2008-2009)
limitations: dietary manganese and selenium intake not assessed
no long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up
potential residual confounding despite multivariable adjustment

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to organophosphate pesticides and neurobehavioral development of neonates: a birth cohort study in Shenyang, China.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Information on each subject was obtained by questionnaire. Dialkyl phosphate (DAP) metabolites were detected in the urine of mothers during pregnancy to evaluate the exposure level to OPs.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study assessing the association between prenatal organophosphate pesticide exposure (urinary DAP metabolites) and neonatal neurobehavioral development (NBNA scores) in Shenyang, China.
key_findings: A 10-fold increase in total DAP concentration was associated with a decrease of 1.78 in NBNA Summary scores (95% CI, -2.12 to -1.45).
Neonates in the highest quintile of prenatal OP exposure had an estimated 2.11-point lower summary NBNA score compared to the lowest quintile.
Maternal OP exposure was the strongest risk factor for lower NBNA scores among tested prenatal factors.
captured_features: Urinary DAP metabolites (DMP, DMTP, DEP, DETP, DEDTP)
summaries.population: 249 pregnant women and their neonates in Shenyang, China
summaries.exposure_domain: Organophosphate pesticide exposure (urinary dialkyl phosphate metabolites)
limitations: Single time-point urine measurement reflecting only recent exposure
Urinary DAPs cannot quantify exposure to specific pesticides
Potential residual confounding
Small sample size

summaries.title: Long-term effects of maternal deprivation on cholinergic system in rat brain.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study used Wistar rats and brain tissue for biochemical and immunohistochemical analysis.
summaries.summary: Experimental study examining the long-term effects of maternal separation on acetylcholinesterase activity and cholinergic fiber density in the brains of Wistar rats.
key_findings: AChE activity significantly decreased in the cortex (P<0.05) and significantly increased in the hippocampus (P<0.05) compared to controls.
No significant change in AChE activity was observed in the thalamus or caudate nuclei.
ChAT positive fiber density significantly increased in the hippocampal CA1 region, with no change in CA3 or dentate gyrus.
ChAT positive fiber density significantly decreased in the retrosplenial cortex.
summaries.population: male Wistar rats, postnatal day 9 to 60
limitations: small sample size (n=5-8 per group)
single 24-hour maternal separation protocol on postnatal day 9
only male animals tested
limited to specific brain regions and cholinergic markers

summaries.title: Determining prenatal, early childhood and cumulative long-term lead exposure using micro-spatial deciduous dentine levels.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Mother–child pairs in this study were drawn from the longitudinal birth cohort studies in Mexico City that comprise the Early Life Exposures in MExico and NeuroToxicology (ELEMENT) project.
summaries.summary: Validation study assessing micro-spatial dentine lead levels as a biomarker for accurately estimating prenatal, early childhood, and long-term cumulative lead exposure by comparing them with maternal blood, bone, cord blood, and serial childhood blood samples.
key_findings: Dentine Pb at birth significantly associated with cord blood Pb (Spearman r = 0.69; n = 27; p<0.0001).
Prenatal dentine Pb associated with maternal patella Pb (r = 0.48; n = 59; p<0.0001) and tibia Pb (r = 0.35; n = 41; p<0.03).
Dentine Pb at 3 months significantly associated with concurrent child blood Pb (r = 0.64; n = 55; p<0.0001).
Secondary dentine Pb correlated positively with cumulative blood lead index (CBLI) (r = 0.38; n = 75; p<0.0007).
Birth dentine Pb not significantly associated with child blood Pb after 2 years of age.
Secondary dentine Pb correlations with maternal bone and blood during pregnancy were weaker and statistically insignificant.
summaries.population: 85 mother-child pairs from the ELEMENT cohort in Mexico City, children followed from birth to 6-11 years
limitations: Incomplete biomarker data on all participants due to incomplete follow-up and sample collection
Only one tooth per participant analyzed, preventing assessment of tooth type influence
Small sample sizes for some specific comparisons

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to maternal bereavement and childbirths in the offspring: a population-based cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The unique personal identification number, which is assigned to all live-born children and new residents, was used to link children to their relatives and to obtain information on demographic variables, vital statistics, health outcomes and socio-economic variables from different national registers.
summaries.summary: Population-based cohort study examining the association between prenatal exposure to maternal bereavement and fertility outcomes in offspring.
key_findings: No overall association between prenatal maternal bereavement and having a child (HR=0.98 [0.96–1.01] for males, HR=1.01 [0.98–1.03] for females).
Females born to mothers who lost a parent had a slightly reduced probability of having children (HR=0.97 [0.94–0.99]).
Females born to mothers who lost another child (HR=1.09 [1.04–1.14]), spouse (HR=1.29 [1.12–1.48]), or sibling (HR=1.13 [1.01–1.27]) had an increased probability.
Sudden death of a relative was associated with increased probability in females (HR=1.21 [1.14–1.29]).
No difference in age-specific mean number of childbirths between exposed and unexposed (HR=0.99 [0.96–1.01] males, HR=1.00 [0.98–1.02] females).
summaries.population: 2,112,770 males and 2,008,826 females born in Denmark (1968-1996) and Sweden (1973-1994), followed from age 12 to 41
limitations: inability to adjust for lifestyle factors or directly measure fecundity using registry data
follow-up only until age 41 does not cover full fertility life
incomplete linkage of mothers to relatives in early years in Denmark leading to exposure misclassification
potential for multiple testing false positives
possible confounding by postnatal paternal behavior
summaries.data_availability_statement: The authors confirm that, for approved reasons, some access restrictions apply to the data underlying the findings. All data is stored at the secure platform of Denmark Statistics, which is the central authority on Danish statistics with the mission to collect, compile and publish statisti cs on the Danish society. By legislations, researchers who want to get access to the data must apply for permissions from Both Statistics Denmark and Danish Data Prote ction Agency. Anyone with interests in this data can contact the authors of the study.

summaries.title: Quantity and diversity of environmental microbial exposure and development of asthma: a birth cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: House dust samples were collected at 2 months of age, and health outcomes were assessed using repeated questionnaires and venous blood samples for specific IgE.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the association between environmental microbial exposure (quantity and diversity scores from house dust) and the development of asthma, respiratory symptoms, atopic dermatitis, and allergic sensitization in children up to age 6.
key_findings: Total microbial quantity score showed a significant inverted-U-shaped association with asthma incidence (P < 0.001), with the highest risk at medium levels (aOR 2.24, 95% CI 0.87–5.75 for 3rd quintile) and lowest risk at highest levels (aOR 0.34, 95% CI 0.09–1.36 for 5th quintile).
Microbial diversity score was inversely associated with wheezing risk and significantly associated (inverted-U shape) with sensitization to inhalant allergens at age 6.
No significant associations were found between single microbial markers and asthma, respiratory symptoms, atopic dermatitis, or sensitization.
captured_features: house dust microbial markers (endotoxin, muramic acid, ergosterol, β-D-glucan, qPCR for specific bacteria/fungi)
parent-reported respiratory symptoms and asthma diagnoses
summaries.population: 410 children born in Eastern and Middle Finland, followed from birth to 6 years of age
summaries.exposure_domain: environmental microbial exposure (house dust bacterial and fungal markers)
limitations: small cohort size (N=410)
lack of adjustment for multiple testing
microbial markers do not capture total microbial exposure without error
potential misclassification of exposure based on single dust sample at 2 months

summaries.title: An unusual case of vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were derived from clinical case presentation, MRI findings, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, stool cultures, and immunization records from a public health unit and hospital.
summaries.summary: Case report describing an immunocompetent child who developed vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis after receiving oral polio vaccine in China, despite prior inactivated polio vaccine doses.
key_findings: Stool culture and sequencing identified Sabin poliovirus type 3 strain with 99.7% homology to the parent OPV strain.
MRI revealed bilateral symmetric increased signal within the anterior horns of the spinal cord gray matter.
Polio antibody titres were <1:8 for type 1, 1:32 for type 2, and 1:128 for type 3.
captured_features: cerebrospinal fluid white blood cell count and protein
summaries.population: single immunocompetent child, almost one year of age
limitations: single case report limits generalizability
no CSF viral culture or PCR conducted initially
potential for recall bias in immunization history

summaries.title: Altered cortical thickness following prenatal sodium valproate exposure.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were acquired on the 3T Siemens Magnetom Trio at Murdoch Childrens Research Institute, Melbourne, using a 12-channel coil.
summaries.summary: Neuroimaging study comparing cortical thickness and verbal abilities in 16 children prenatally exposed to valproate versus 16 matched controls.
key_findings: Increased cortical thickness in left inferior frontal gyrus and left medial occipital cortex (P < 0.05, corrected).
Significant interaction between group and hemispheric thickness in inferior frontal region (F(1, 29) = 12.38, P = 0.001), showing absence of normal right-left asymmetry in exposed children.
VPA dose significantly correlated with right inferior frontal gyrus thickness (r = 0.57, P = 0.02).
No significant correlation between VPA dose and left inferior frontal gyrus thickness (r = -0.17, P = 0.53).
No significant difference in total cortical white and grey matter between groups (both P > 0.1).
Trend towards poorer verbal abilities and greater left inferior frontal gyrus thickness in exposed children (r = -0.42, P = 0.12).
summaries.population: 16 children (mean age 7.2 years) prenatally exposed to valproate and 16 age- and sex-matched controls (mean age 8.1 years)
limitations: small sample size (16 cases, 16 controls)
minor age discrepancy between groups
cross-sectional design limits causal inference
limited dose range (relatively low average dose)

summaries.title: Prenatal organochlorine and methylmercury exposure and memory and learning in school-age children in communities near the New Bedford Harbor Superfund site, Massachusetts.
summaries.ehr_evidence: A sample of 788 mother–infant pairs were recruited from St. Luke’s Hospital in New Bedford, Massachusetts, at the time of the infant’s birth, between 1993 and 1998.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating associations between low-level prenatal exposure to PCBs, DDE, and methylmercury and childhood memory and learning at age 8.
key_findings: Each 1 μg/g increase in maternal hair Hg was associated with decrements of –2.8 on Visual Memory (95% CI: –5.0, –0.6, p = 0.01), –2.2 on Learning (95% CI: –4.6, 0.2, p = 0.08), and –1.7 on Verbal Memory (95% CI: –3.9, 0.6, p = 0.14).
No significant adverse associations were found for ∑PCB4, dioxin-like PCBs, or DDE with WRAML indices.
After excluding three high-exposure outliers, the adjusted estimate for DDE and Learning Index was essentially null.
captured_features: Cord serum PCB and DDE levels
WRAML indices (Visual Memory, Verbal Memory, Learning)
summaries.population: 393 children aged 7–11 years (mean 8.1) born 1993–1998 to mothers residing near New Bedford Harbor, Massachusetts
limitations: Low statistical power for PCB associations at low exposure levels
Hair mercury may be less sensitive than blood biomarkers
Missing data for covariates and exposures
Potential selection bias as included children had higher maternal IQ and education
Cross-sectional assessment of neurodevelopment at a single time point

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to arsenic and cadmium impacts infectious disease-related genes within the glucocorticoid receptor signal transduction pathway.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Twelve datasets were gathered from previous human cohort studies evaluating mRNA changes, DNA methylation changes, or protein expression changes associated with prenatal exposure to iAs or Cd.
summaries.summary: A comparative genomic enrichment analysis integrating twelve human pregnancy cohort datasets to identify genes and pathways linking prenatal arsenic and cadmium exposure to infectious disease susceptibility.
key_findings: 82 infection and exposure-related (IER) genes were identified that overlap between infectious disease signaling and prenatal iAs/Cd exposure.
19 of 82 IER genes were enriched for the glucocorticoid receptor signal transduction pathway (p = 1.58 × 10−18).
9 of 82 IER genes were present in the TNFR1 pathway (p = 5.01 × 10−13).
8 of 82 IER genes were present in the toll-like receptor pathway (p = 6.31 × 10−13).
61% (50/82) of IER genes were shown to be modulated by iAs and 41% (34/82) by Cd in the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database.
summaries.data_source_type: published genomic, epigenomic, and proteomic datasets from human pregnancy cohorts
summaries.population: pregnant women and newborns/infants from cohorts in Bangladesh, Thailand, Mexico, and the United States
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal and early-life exposure to inorganic arsenic and cadmium
limitations: genomic and epigenomic endpoints can be transient
original studies had small sample sizes
incomplete analysis of confounders in source studies
variations in exposure duration and demographics across cohorts
reliance on published gene lists rather than raw data
CTD validation included in vitro and animal model data

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals in relation to thyroid hormone levels in infants - a Dutch prospective cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: information on T4 levels in heel prick blood spots was obtained through the neonatal screening programme in the Netherlands.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study assessing the association between prenatal exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) and thyroxine (T4) levels in newborns in the Netherlands.
key_findings: Girls in the highest quartile of DDE exposure showed significantly increased T4 levels compared to the lowest quartile (+24.8 nmol/L, 95% CI 0.79, 48.75; p=0.043).
Girls in the highest quartile of PFOA exposure showed significantly increased T4 levels compared to the lowest quartile (+38.6 nmol/L, 95% CI 13.34, 63.83; p=0.004).
Boys in the second quartile of PFOS and PFOA exposure had lower T4 levels in crude models, but associations were attenuated and non-significant after full adjustment.
No significant associations were observed for DEHP metabolites, PCB-153, or HCB.
captured_features: T4 levels from heel prick blood spots
DDE, PFOS, PFOA, PCB-153, HCB, DEHP metabolites in cord plasma and breast milk
summaries.population: 83 mother-child pairs (newborns) in the Netherlands
limitations: small sample size (n=83)
reduced statistical power due to quartile and gender stratification
no correction for multiple testing
T4 measured 4-7 days post-birth
lack of thyroid binding protein data
homogenous population limits generalizability

summaries.title: Interim CDC guidance for polio vaccination for travel to and from countries affected by wild poliovirus.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Literature review and public health surveillance data synthesized by CDC/ACIP.
summaries.summary: CDC interim public health guidance and vaccine recommendations for travelers to and from countries with active wild poliovirus circulation.
key_findings: No original research results reported; this is a public health guidance document.
summaries.study_design: Public health guidance and policy recommendation
summaries.data_source_type: Literature review and public health surveillance
summaries.population: Infants, children, and adults traveling to or residing in polio-endemic/exporting countries
summaries.exposure_domain: Travel to polio-endemic regions / wild poliovirus exposure
limitations: Lack of data on lifelong immunity after routine polio vaccine series
Limited experience with administration of multiple additional IPV doses

summaries.title: Notes from the field: rotavirus vaccine administration errors--United States, 2006-2013.
summaries.ehr_evidence: CDC searched for reports to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) (2) of rotavirus vaccine administration errors involving injection and eye splashes in the United States during the period January 1, 2006–August 1, 2013.
summaries.summary: Analysis of 66 VAERS reports on rotavirus vaccine administration errors (injection and eye splashes) in the US from 2006 to 2013.
key_findings: 66 total reports of rotavirus vaccine administration errors were identified.
39 reports involved administration by injection (33 for RV1, 6 for RV5).
19 of 39 injection reports (49%) documented an adverse event, most commonly irritability (7 cases) and injection site redness (5).
30 of 39 injection reports (77%) lacked an explanation for the error.
27 reports involved eye splashes, with 21 cases (78%) describing nonserious minor eye irritation.
summaries.population: infants and children in the United States, 2006–2013
limitations: passive surveillance system likely captures only a small fraction of errors
reporting bias inherent to VAERS
no denominator data to calculate error rates

summaries.title: Reactogenicity and safety of the human rotavirus vaccine, Rotarix™ in The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India: a post-marketing surveillance study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Baseline demographic data was reported on the case report form by the investigators at the time of enrolment/first visit. AEs were recorded on diary cards after each vaccine dose.
summaries.summary: Post-marketing surveillance study evaluating the reactogenicity and safety of the Rotarix™ rotavirus vaccine in healthy infants across The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India.
key_findings: In The Philippines, 14.7% (95% CI: 12.9–16.7) of infants reported at least one Grade 2/3 solicited adverse event, with irritability most common (32.2% post-Dose-1; 23.5% post-Dose-2).
In Sri Lanka, 14.9% (95% CI: 12.0–18.3) reported Grade 2/3 solicited AEs, with fever most common (18.0% post-Dose-1; 20.2% post-Dose-2).
In India, 12.7% (95% CI: 9.3–16.7) reported Grade 2/3 solicited AEs, with irritability most common (23.0% post-Dose-1; 13.2% post-Dose-2).
Unsolicited AEs were reported in 24.5% of infants in The Philippines, 4.8% in Sri Lanka, and 6.9% in India.
Forty-one serious adverse events occurred in The Philippines, with six in four infants considered causally related to vaccination; no SAEs were reported in Sri Lanka or India.
captured_features: solicited adverse events (fever, vomiting, diarrhea, irritability, cough/runny nose, loss of appetite)
summaries.study_design: open, single-group, multi-center post-marketing surveillance study
summaries.population: healthy infants aged at least 6 weeks at first dose in The Philippines, Sri Lanka, and India
limitations: low sample size limiting detection of rare AEs
open, single-group design without controls
passive reporting leading to potential underreporting of AEs and SAEs
varying exclusion criteria across countries
loss to follow-up for the infant who developed intussusception

summaries.title: Gender-specific mortality in DTP-IPV- and MMR±MenC-eligible age groups to determine possible sex-differential effects of vaccination: an observational study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The data were available from Statistics Netherlands, who linked demographic data of persons included in the Municipal Personal Records Database (GBA) with causes of death derived from Statistics Netherlands.
summaries.summary: Observational study of gender-specific mortality among Dutch children aged 0-11 years (2000-2011) to assess sex-differential effects of DTP-IPV and MMR ± MenC vaccinations.
key_findings: Mortality rate for natural causes was higher among boys than girls in all age groups.
Adjusted IRRs for girls compared with boys ranged between 0.81 (95% CI 0.74-0.89) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.77-1.07) across age groups.
No statistically significant differences in IRRs were observed between vaccine-related age groups (p = 0.723, p = 0.493, p = 0.868).
Sensitivity analyses including only indigenous Dutch children, specific death categories, and time periods yielded no statistically significant differences in IRR between vaccine-related age groups.
pathologies_diseases: diseases of the nervous, circulatory, and respiratory systems
summaries.population: all Dutch children aged 0-11 years from 2000 to 2011 (N=6,261,472)
summaries.exposure_domain: routine childhood vaccinations (DTP-IPV, MMR ± MenC, and boosters)
limitations: individual vaccination status could not be verified and was assumed based on national schedule
changes in vaccination schedule during the study period
low overall childhood mortality limits statistical power to detect non-specific effects
potential selection and survival bias
BCG vaccination for specific subgroups could interfere with results

summaries.title: In vitro and in vivo growth alter the population dynamic and properties of a Jeryl Lynn mumps vaccine.
summaries.ehr_evidence: JL-CK vaccine was provided by the Official Medicines Control Laboratory-Prague, Czech Republic. Mu90, a clinical mumps isolate passaged four times on Vero cells, and RIT4385 were archived material held at NIBSC. African green monkey (Vero) and Madin Darby canine kidney (MDCK) cell lines were used. Neonatal rat pups were inoculated intracerebrally.
summaries.summary: Comparative genomic and phenotypic analysis of two Jeryl Lynn mumps vaccine strains to assess genetic heterogeneity, in vitro growth kinetics, and in vivo neurovirulence in neonatal rats.
key_findings: JL-CK produced 100-fold more progeny virus in Vero cells (p < 0.0001) and MDCK cells (p = 0.0365) compared to RIT4385.
Sanger sequencing identified 14 regions of heterogeneity in JL-CK, with only 4% of the population corresponding to the parental strain.
JL-CK showed significantly higher neurovirulence than RIT4385 in neonatal rats (p = 0.0035), but lower than wild-type Mu90 (p < 0.001).
In vivo passage in rat brains increased the K36R mutation frequency 9.6-fold, indicating preferential selection of the JL-CK1 variant.
summaries.study_design: Experimental laboratory study (in vitro and in vivo)
summaries.data_source_type: Laboratory experiments / Cell culture and animal model
summaries.population: Neonatal rats, Vero and MDCK cell lines
summaries.exposure_domain: Vaccine production substrate (canine kidney cells vs chicken embryo fibroblasts)
limitations: Small sample sizes for animal groups
Lack of human clinical correlation
Limited cell lines tested
Conflicting data between neurovirulence scores and in vivo variant frequencies
summaries.data_availability_statement: Associated DataSupplementary Materials

summaries.title: Perinatal Exposure to Traffic-Related Air Pollution and Atopy at 1 Year of Age in a Multi-Center Canadian Birth Cohort Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The CHILD study (http://www.canadianchildstudy.ca) is a prospective longitudinal national birth cohort that recruited over 3,600 families between 2008 and 2012 in four Canadian cities.
summaries.summary: Prospective multi-center birth cohort study examining the association between perinatal traffic-related air pollution (NO2) exposure and atopy at 1 year of age in Canadian children.
key_findings: TRAP exposure after birth increased risk for atopy to any allergens (aOR = 1.16 per 10 μg/m3 NO2; 95% CI: 1.00, 1.41).
No association was found during pregnancy (aOR = 1.02; 95% CI: 0.86, 1.22).
Association was stronger among non-daycare attendees (aOR = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.28, 2.01) compared to daycare attendees (aOR = 1.05; 95% CI: 0.81, 1.28).
Positive but non-significant trends were found for food (aOR = 1.17; 95% CI: 0.95, 1.47) and inhalant allergens (aOR = 1.28; 95% CI: 0.93, 1.76).
captured_features: Maternal atopy, asthma, smoking, and SES
summaries.population: 2,477 children approximately 1 year of age from four Canadian cities
limitations: Exposure assessment derived from modeled estimates rather than direct measurements
Reliance on self-reported environmental and parental risk factors
Cohort bias toward higher socioeconomic status
Infiltration model developed for US cities applied to Canadian homes
Missing covariate data reduced sample sizes for some analyses
Lack of sufficient power for certain subgroup analyses

summaries.title: Association between levels of persistent organic pollutants in adipose tissue and cryptorchidism in early childhood: a case-control study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Adipose tissue biopsies were taken during surgery, and chemical concentrations were measured by gas chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry. Obstetric data were obtained from medical records, and breastfeeding data were collected via questionnaires.
summaries.summary: Case-control study assessing the association between prenatal exposure to persistent organic pollutants (PCBs, PCDD/Fs, PBDEs) measured in adipose tissue and congenital cryptorchidism in early childhood.
key_findings: Total-TEq was positively associated with cryptorchidism after adjustment [OR 3.21 (95% CI 1.29–9.09), p=0.02].
Sum of PCDD/Fs was positively associated with cryptorchidism after adjustment [OR 3.69 (95% CI 1.45–10.9), p=0.01].
Sum of PCBs was close to significant [OR 1.92 (95% CI 0.98–4.01), p=0.07].
Sum of PBDEs was not associated with cryptorchidism [OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.47–1.54), p=0.61].
Unadjusted chemical concentrations showed no significant associations with cryptorchidism risk.
captured_features: Adipose tissue concentrations of PCBs, PCDD/Fs, PBDEs, and total-TEq
summaries.population: boys operated for cryptorchidism (cases) or inguinal/umbilical hernia or hydrocele (controls) in Finland and Denmark, aged 0-5 years (Finland) or no limit (Denmark)
limitations: small sample size
control group included boys with inguinal hernia which is associated with cryptorchidism
recruitment at surgical departments limits generalizability to mild cases
potential inclusion of acquired undescended testes in cases
inability to adjust for lipid content of adipose samples
recall bias for Danish mothers' data collected ~10 years later
lack of data on children's body size

summaries.title: Obesogen Holdover: Prenatal Exposure Predicts Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Childhood.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study included nearly 700 mother–child pairs from the Rhea cohort in Greece.
summaries.summary: Observational birth cohort study examining the association between prenatal exposure to persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and cardiometabolic risk factors in 4-year-old children in Greece.
key_findings: A 10-fold increase in maternal HCB concentrations was associated with higher risks of generalized and abdominal obesity, greater skinfold thickness, higher systolic blood pressure, and a modest increase in child BMI z-score.
Prenatal DDE exposure was associated with higher BMI z-score, increased risk of abdominal obesity, and higher diastolic blood pressure.
PCBs were not associated with any of the assessed cardiometabolic risk factors.
captured_features: maternal blood concentrations of DDE, HCB, and PCBs
child weight, height, waist circumference, skinfold thickness
child blood pressure and blood lipid levels
summaries.population: nearly 700 mother-child pairs from the Rhea cohort in Greece, children assessed at age 4
limitations: observational design limits causal inference
lack of sex-stratified analysis despite potential effect modification
unclear long-term health implications
single regional cohort may limit generalizability

summaries.title: Early-Life Exposure to Clostridium leptum Causes Pulmonary Immunosuppression.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study utilized an experimental murine model using BALB/c mice delivered by caesarean section or vaginal delivery, with exposure to Clostridium leptum and ovalbumin allergen.
summaries.summary: Experimental study evaluating the impact of early-life Clostridium leptum exposure on asthma development, airway hyper-responsiveness, and pulmonary immune responses in a murine model.
key_findings: Early-life C. leptum feeding increased Treg cell frequency and number in caesarean-delivered mice compared to vaginally delivered mice.
C. leptum exposure significantly reduced airway hyper-responsiveness and BALF cell counts (eosinophils, neutrophils, lymphocytes, macrophages) in OVA-sensitized mice compared to controls.
Th1, Th2, Th9, and Th17 cell levels and associated cytokines were statistically decreased in C. leptum-exposed OVA-sensitized mice compared to OVA-sensitized controls (p < 0.05).
IL-10 and TGF-β1 levels were significantly higher in C. leptum-exposed OVA-sensitized mice compared to OVA-sensitized controls.
No significant difference in Th22 frequency or IL-22 production was observed between C. leptum-exposed and control OVA-sensitized groups.
summaries.population: BALB/c mice (caesarean-delivered and vaginally delivered)
limitations: murine model may not fully replicate human asthma pathophysiology
single bacterial strain and allergen model limits generalizability
lack of human clinical validation
summaries.data_availability_statement: All relevant data are within the paper.

summaries.title: Long-term effect of early-life stress from earthquake exposure on working memory in adulthood.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The subjects of present study were recruited from workers of Kailuan Mining Group in six coal reserve bases, two communities, and two related units.
summaries.summary: Observational study investigating the long-term effect of early-life earthquake exposure on working memory performance in adulthood.
key_findings: BVMT-R scores were markedly decreased in the infant exposure group compared with the no exposure group (P<0.05).
Subjects exposed prenatally in the second and third trimesters had significantly lower BVMT-R scores compared with the first trimester (P=0.035 for 2nd test, P=0.038 for total score).
HVLT-R scores did not show significant differences across the three groups (P>0.05).
Education level (OR=2.289, 95% CI=1.435–3.650, P<0.001) and earthquake exposure (OR=1.437, 95% CI=1.061–1.947, P=0.019) were independent risk factors for impaired visuospatial memory.
summaries.study_design: observational cross-sectional study based on historical birth dates and natural disaster exposure
summaries.population: 907 adult workers born in Tangshan, China between 1975 and 1978
summaries.exposure_domain: early-life stress from earthquake exposure (prenatal and infant periods)
limitations: confounding factors such as genetic background, adult life events, lifestyle, diet, alcohol, and drug abuse were difficult to quantify
no imaging or biological studies were performed to explore underlying mechanisms
relatively small sample size

summaries.title: Effectiveness of introducing point of care capillary testing and linking screening with routine appointments for increasing blood lead screening rates of young children: a before-after study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Numerator data for all analyses were obtained from routinely collected data extracted from the Lead Management Program ACCESS database, which contains information on all blood lead tests conducted at both the mainstream and Indigenous health clinics.
summaries.summary: Before-after study evaluating the impact of switching from venous to capillary blood lead screening and linking it with routine immunization appointments on screening participation rates among young children in Broken Hill, Australia.
key_findings: Annual screening participation increased from 0.39 in 2008 to 0.75 in 2012.
Cumulative screening by 24 months increased from 0.63 for the 2007 birth cohort to 0.98 for the 2010 birth cohort.
Attendance stabilized after capillary screening was introduced and increased markedly when linked with immunization.
No evidence that changing to capillary sampling affected the estimate of the underlying population blood lead level, which continued to fluctuate at or slightly below previous levels.
No consistent change in the proportion of children with blood lead levels equal to or greater than 5 or 10 μg/dL.
summaries.population: 7–59 month old children resident in Broken Hill, NSW, Australia
limitations: use of administrative data sets to calculate denominators with assumed linear change between census years
uncertainty in NSW Midwives Data Collection due to time delays and lack of migration accounting
before-and-after design limits ability to control for other factors
single community setting without a control group

summaries.title: Exposure to grass pollen--but not birch pollen--affects lung function in Swedish children.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Children belonging to the Swedish birth cohort BAMSE underwent clinical examination including lung-function testing and blood sampling for measuring serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) against common airborne and food allergens (ImmunoCAP System; Phadia AB, Uppsala, Sweden) at eight (N = 1838) and sixteen years of age (N = 2063) (year 2003 – 2004 and 2011 –2012, respectively).
summaries.summary: Investigation of the effect of grass and birch pollen exposure on lung function in 8- and 16-year-old children from the Swedish BAMSE birth cohort.
key_findings: Increased grass pollen exposure the day before testing was associated with reduced FEV1 in 8-year-olds (-32.4 ml; 95% CI: -50.6 to -14.2 per 3 pollen counts/m³).
The negative effect was stronger in children sensitized to pollen allergens (FEV1: -41.6 ml; 95% CI: -68.3 to -14.8).
No associations were found for birch or other pollen exposure in 8-year-olds.
Pollen exposure was not related to lung function in 16-year-olds.
captured_features: ambient air pollution levels (ozone, NO2, PM10, PM2.5)
demographic and clinical covariates (sex, age, height, allergic heredity)
summaries.data_source_type: birth cohort and environmental monitoring stations
summaries.population: children aged 8 and 16 years from the BAMSE birth cohort in Stockholm, Sweden
summaries.exposure_domain: airborne pollen and ambient air pollution
limitations: Lung function tests were not conducted during the peak summer pollen season, limiting assessment of acute exposure.
Lack of IgG/IgG4 data to evaluate tolerance development.
Potential confounding by differences in indoor/outdoor time between age groups.
Relatively low pollen concentrations during study years.

summaries.title: Effects of 4-nonylphenol on oxidant/antioxidant balance system inducing hepatic steatosis in male rat.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Twenty-four male Sprague-Dawley rats (70–80 g) were obtained from the Experimental Animal Center of Tongji Medical College Animal Laboratory (Wuhan, China).
summaries.summary: Experimental study investigating the effects of intraperitoneal administration of 4-nonylphenol on hepatic steatosis, oxidative stress, and apoptosis in male rats.
key_findings: Liver weight significantly increased at 10 mg/kg (9.23 ± 0.78 g) and 50 mg/kg (9.44 ± 0.67 g) compared to control (7.63 ± 1.54 g).
Serum GOT, GPT, LDH, and γ-GT activities significantly increased in 4-NP-treated groups (p < 0.05 to p < 0.001).

H2O2 levels significantly increased at 50 mg/kg (3.066 ± 0.47 μmol/mg prot, p < 0.01) and MDA increased at 10 mg/kg (3.013 ± 0.46 nmol/mg prot, p < 0.01) and 50 mg/kg (3.199 ± 0.81 nmol/mg prot, p < 0.01).
Antioxidant enzymes CAT, GSH-Px, and SOD significantly decreased (p < 0.05 to p < 0.001).
Gene expression of Casp-9, Bax, Fas, FasL, and TNF-α significantly increased, while Bcl-2 significantly decreased (p < 0.05).
PCNA positive cells increased to 4.64%, 8.87%, and 9.07% at 2, 10, and 50 mg/kg doses respectively.
captured_features: Serum hepatic enzymes (GOT, GPT, LDH, γ-GT)
Gene expression (SOD1, GPx, HSP70, Casp-9, Bax, Bcl-2, Fas, FasL, TNF-α)
summaries.population: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (70–80 g)
limitations: Small sample size (n=6 per group)
Short exposure duration (30 days)
Intraperitoneal administration route may not reflect typical human environmental exposure
Lack of protein-level validation (immunoblotting recommended for future work)
Single species and strain limits generalizability

summaries.title: Mitochondrial oxidative DNA damage and exposure to particulate air pollution in mother-newborn pairs.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We recruited mother-newborn pairs (only singletons) in the East-Limburg Hospital in Genk, Belgium who are part of the ongoing birth cohort “ENVIRONAGE”.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study assessing the association between prenatal particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5) exposure and mitochondrial oxidative DNA damage (8-OHdG) in maternal and cord blood.
key_findings: PM10 exposure during the entire pregnancy was associated with an 18.3% (95% CI: 5.6 to 33.4%, p=0.004) increase in maternal mitochondrial 8-OHdG.
PM10 exposure during the third trimester was associated with a 28.1% (95% CI: 8.6 to 51.2%, p=0.004) increase in maternal 8-OHdG.
PM2.5 exposure during the entire pregnancy was associated with a 13.9% (95% CI: 0.4 to 29.4%, p=0.04) increase in maternal 8-OHdG.
PM2.5 exposure during the third trimester was associated with a 28.1% (95% CI: 3.6 to 58.4%, p=0.02) increase in maternal 8-OHdG.
PM10 exposure during the first and second trimesters was associated with 23.0% (95% CI: 5.9 to 42.8%, p=0.007) and 16.6% (95% CI: 1.8 to 33.5%, p=0.03) increases in cord blood 8-OHdG, respectively.
No significant association was found between PM exposure and cord blood 8-OHdG during the entire pregnancy (p>0.11).
High 8-OHdG levels correlated with high mtDNA content in maternal (r=0.44, p<0.0001) and cord blood (r=0.58, p<0.0001).
No association was found between PM exposure or 8-OHdG levels and birth weight or small for gestational age.
summaries.population: 293 pregnant women and their newborns from the ENVIRONAGE birth cohort in Genk, Belgium
limitations: Mitochondrial 8-OHdG measured only at end of pregnancy, limiting assessment of changes during gestation.
Potential residual confounding by unknown factors.
Exposure estimated via spatial interpolation rather than personal monitoring.
No significant associations found with adverse pregnancy outcomes like birth weight.

summaries.title: Is There a Causal Relation between Maternal Acetaminophen Administration and ADHD?
summaries.ehr_evidence: Pregnant CD1 mice (N = 8/group) were allocated to receive by gavage either APAP (150 mg/kg/day, equivalent to the FDA-approved maximum human clinical dose), or 0.5% carboxymethylcellulose (control group), starting on embryonic day 7 until delivery.
summaries.summary: Preclinical experimental study investigating whether prenatal acetaminophen exposure causes hyperkinetic dysfunction/ADHD-like behavior in mouse offspring using behavioral, MRI, and histological assessments.
key_findings: Maternal serum APAP concentration peaked at 30 min after gavage, reaching a mean of 117 μg/ml.
No significant differences in maternal serum ALT concentrations between groups (P = 0.3 and P = 0.5).
No significant differences in locomotor activity parameters between groups (all P > 0.008).
No significant differences in volumes of 29 brain areas on MRI or neuronal quantification between groups.
summaries.population: pregnant CD1 mice and postnatal day 30 offspring
limitations: lack of established animal model for ADHD
oral gavage may act as a stressor
absence of 24hr home cage activity monitoring
narrow focus on hyperkinetic behavior only
intervention limited to pregnancy without lactation period
summaries.data_availability_statement: All relevant data are within the paper and its Supporting Information files.

summaries.title: Feasibility and acceptability of oral cholera vaccine mass vaccination campaign in response to an outbreak and floods in Malawi.
summaries.ehr_evidence: This study made use of the available health facility data and reports on cholera outbreak and oral cholera vaccine campaign.
summaries.summary: Documentation of the feasibility, acceptability, and coverage of a reactive mass oral cholera vaccine campaign in Nsanje district, Malawi, following floods and a cholera outbreak.
key_findings: Round 1 campaign achieved 97.6% coverage (156,592 of 160,482 target population).
Round 2 achieved 85.8% coverage (137,629 recipients), with 67.6% fully immunized (108,247).
Of 320,000 doses sourced, 294,221 (91.9%) were administered.
Demographics of vaccinated individuals showed 54.4% females and 55.4% children under 15 years.
No severe adverse events following immunization were reported.
The main reason for non-vaccination or incomplete dosing was absence during the campaign period.
The 2014/2015 cholera outbreak across eight districts resulted in 693 cases and 11 deaths (CFR 1.6%).
summaries.study_design: descriptive documentation of a mass vaccination campaign
summaries.data_source_type: health facility registers and administrative reports
summaries.population: over 160,000 people aged one year or more in 19 displacement camps and surrounding communities in Nsanje district, Malawi
limitations: Reliance on health facility data and reports leads to incompleteness and bias.

summaries.title: Prenatal Exposure to Phthalates and Anogenital Distance in Male Infants from a Low-Exposed Danish Cohort (2010-2012).
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study was based on data from the Odense Child Cohort. Fasting spot urine samples were collected at approximately GA 28 weeks before 0930 hours and stored in freezers at the Odense Patient data Explorative Network (OPEN).
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study investigating the association between maternal urinary phthalate metabolite concentrations during pregnancy and anogenital distance (AGD) and penile width in male offspring at 3 months of age.
key_findings: No dose-dependent association was found between any prenatal phthalate metabolite and AGD or penile width (p > 0.05).

Mean AGDas was lower for boys in the second, third, and fourth quartiles of MEP compared with the first quartile [–0.64 mm (95% CI: –2.52, 1.23), –1.68 mm (95% CI: –3.56, 0.20), and –1.37 mm (95% CI: –3.27, 0.54)], but differences were not statistically significant.
Maternal ∑DiNPm and ∑DEHPm levels in higher quartiles were associated with shorter AGD compared to the first quartile, but associations were not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
summaries.data_source_type: cohort biospecimen collection and clinical examination
summaries.population: pregnant women and male infants in Odense, Denmark (2010–2012)
limitations: single spot urine sample may not reflect fetal exposure in sensitive developmental windows
potential residual confounding by co-exposure to other environmental chemicals, lifestyle, or health behavior
selection bias with only 42% participation and better-educated participants
temporal and seasonal variation in phthalate levels
fasting state may affect urine concentration

summaries.title: Severe and Moderate Asthma Exacerbations in Asthmatic Children and Exposure to Ambient Air Pollutants.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We studied asthmatic children born between 1 April 1996 and 31 March 2011 in the province of Quebec (Canada) and identified from a population open birth cohort created with the Quebec Integrated Chronic Disease Surveillance System (QICDSS) [25].
summaries.summary: Population-based cohort study assessing the association between birth and time-dependent exposure to ambient air pollutants (NO2, O3, PM2.5) and severe asthma exacerbations in asthmatic children in Quebec, Canada.
key_findings: Of 162,752 asthmatic children followed, 35,229 had at least one exacerbation.
Time-dependent exposure to NO2 (IQR 4.95 ppb) was associated with an increased risk of exacerbation (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.058–1.131).
Time-dependent exposure to O3 (IQR 3.85 ppb) was associated with an increased risk of exacerbation (HR 1.052, 95% CI 1.037–1.066).
Time-dependent exposure to PM2.5 (IQR 1.82 µg/m3) was associated with an increased risk of exacerbation (HR 1.025, 95% CI 1.017–1.031).
Birth exposure to PM2.5 was positively associated with exacerbation risk (HR 1.051, 95% CI 1.049–1.053).
No significant associations were found between birth exposure to NO2 (HR 1.001, 95% CI 0.995–1.005) or O3 and exacerbations.
A significant effect modification was found between NO2 exposure and sex, with increased risk observed in girls.
summaries.population: Asthmatic children born 1996-2011 in Quebec, Canada (<13 years)
limitations: Health care service use definition may miss milder exacerbations
30-day buffer period may underestimate recurring events
Exposure assigned at postal code centroid causing measurement error
PM2.5 exposure constant over follow-up period
Lack of individual-level SES and secondhand smoke data
Self-reported residential addresses

summaries.title: Bisphenol A and Adiposity in an Inner-City Birth Cohort.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Study subjects are participants in the prospective birth cohort of the Columbia Center for Children’s Environmental Health (CCCEH) in Northern Manhattan and the South Bronx, New York.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal birth cohort study examining associations between prenatal and early-childhood urinary bisphenol A (BPA) exposures and childhood adiposity measures (FMI, %BF, WC, BMIZ) in an inner-city NYC population.
key_findings: Prenatal urinary BPA was positively associated with age 7 FMI (β = 0.31 kg/m2; 95% CI: 0.01, 0.60, p = 0.04), %BF (β = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.03, 1.55, p = 0.04), and WC (β = 1.29 cm; 95% CI: 0.29, 2.30, p = 0.01).
Prenatal BPA was not associated with BMIZ at ages 5 or 7, or change in BMIZ between ages 5 and 7 (all p > 0.1).
The association between prenatal BPA and FMI was sex-specific, with positive associations observed in girls but not boys.
Child urinary BPA concentrations were not associated with childhood anthropometric outcomes (all p > 0.05).
Child BPA concentrations showed a borderline negative association with ΔBMIZ from 5 to 7 years (β = –0.10; 95% CI: –0.02, 0.005, p = 0.06).
captured_features: Maternal prepregnancy BMI and obesity status
summaries.population: African American and Dominican mother-child pairs in Northern Manhattan and the South Bronx, New York (children followed to age 7 years)
limitations: Use of spot urine samples leading to potential exposure misclassification due to low intraclass correlation
Lack of dietary data during pregnancy and childhood
Body composition assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis rather than gold-standard methods
Lack of pubertal timing data to account for sex-specific developmental differences
Missing anthropometric and biomarker data due to loss to follow-up

summaries.title: Moderate Prenatal Cadmium Exposure and Adverse Birth Outcomes: a Role for Sex-Specific Differences?
summaries.ehr_evidence: The sample was derived from the ALSPAC study, a population-based study investigating environmental and genetic influences on the health, behaviour, and development of children.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between moderate prenatal cadmium exposure (maternal blood Cd) and birth outcomes, with a focus on sex-specific effects.
key_findings: Maternal blood Cd was adversely associated with birthweight (unstandardized B coefficient -62.7 g, 95% CI -107.0, -18.4) and crown-heel length (-0.28 cm, 95% CI -0.48, -0.07) in adjusted regression models.

Stratified by sex, maternal blood Cd was adversely associated with birthweight (-87.1 g, 95% CI -144.8, -29.4), head circumference (-0.22 cm, 95% CI -0.39, -0.04), and crown-heel length (-0.44 cm, 95% CI -0.71, -0.18) in girls but not in boys.
No significant association was found between maternal blood Cd and low birthweight or preterm delivery.
Maternal blood Cd did not mediate the association between smoking and birth outcomes.
summaries.data_source_type: Primary cohort study with biospecimen analysis and questionnaire data
summaries.population: Pregnant women and their singleton live-born infants from the ALSPAC cohort in the UK (n=4191)
summaries.exposure_domain: Prenatal cadmium exposure (maternal blood cadmium levels)
limitations: Potential unmeasured confounders such as other environmental pollutants
Large number of cadmium values below limit of detection affecting continuous variable modeling
Reliance on self-reported smoking data

summaries.title: Effects of low-level prenatal lead exposure on child IQ at 4 and 8 years in a UK birth cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study sample was derived from the ALSPAC, a population-based study investigating environmental and genetic influences on the health, behaviour and development of children.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the association between low-level prenatal lead exposure and child IQ at ages 4 and 8 years, including sex-specific effects and moderation by prenatal exposure.
key_findings: No association of prenatal lead exposure with child IQ at 4 or 8 years in adjusted regression models.
Positive association for IQ at age 8 years in girls: predicted increase per 1 mg/dl prenatal B-Pb was verbal 0.71 (p=0.021), performance 0.57 (p=0.099), and total 0.73 (p=0.017).
In boys, coefficients tended to be negative: verbal -0.15, performance -0.42, and total -0.29 points per 1 mg/dl (all p > 0.200).
No evidence for prenatal B-Pb moderating the association between child B-Pb and IQ at age 4 or 8 years.
summaries.population: Pregnant women and their offspring enrolled in the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), UK
limitations: Small sample size for IQ at age 4 and moderation analysis
Potential measurement error in IQ tests due to child factors
Unmeasured confounders such as maternal and paternal IQ
Lack of data on concomitant exposure to other pollutants like cadmium
Unknown childhood lead exposure not accounted for
Single time-point prenatal blood sampling may not capture full gestational exposure

summaries.title: Reduction of in utero lead exposures in South African populations: Positive impact of unleaded petrol.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Participants also consented to access and use of hospital birth outcome data (including maternal and neonate characteristics such as weight, length and head circumference, gestational age, Apgar score, as well as birth complications, if any) for research purposes. The actual data source was biological samples (maternal blood, urine, cord blood) and questionnaires.
summaries.summary: Assessment of in utero lead exposure and its association with birth outcomes in a large South African cohort following the legislative removal of lead from petrol.
key_findings: Overall, the geometric mean of maternal blood lead was 1.32 μg/dL (n = 640; 95% CI, 1.24–1.40).
In the subset cohort, paired maternal and cord blood lead levels were positively correlated (rho = 0.65, p < 0.001).
Geographical differences were found in gestational age (p<0.001), birth length (p=0.028), head circumference (p<0.001), Apgar score at 5 min (p<0.001), and parity (p<0.002).
In female neonates, cord blood lead was positively associated with head circumference (rho = 0.243; p<0.016).
No significant association was found between maternal blood lead and infant weight, length, or head circumference overall.
Multivariate analysis showed mothers who did not use pesticides at home had lower lead levels compared to those who did (β = -0.14; 95% CI, -0.26 to -0.02).
summaries.population: pregnant women and neonates in coastal regions of South Africa
limitations: recall bias in dietary intake
cord blood samples limited to Indian Ocean sites only due to financial constraints
cross-sectional assessment at delivery

summaries.title: The Hokkaido Birth Cohort Study on Environment and Children's Health: cohort profile-updated 2017.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Parent and infant medical records were obtained from physicians at the participating hospitals or clinics.
summaries.summary: Cohort profile of the Hokkaido Birth Cohort Study on Environment and Children’s Health, detailing two prospective cohorts investigating prenatal environmental chemical exposures on birth outcomes, child development, allergies, and epigenetic modifications.
key_findings: PCDD/PCDFs significantly decreased birth weight (2,3,4,7,8-PeCDF: β = −24.5 g, 95% CI −387.4 to −61.5).
PFOS was negatively correlated with birth weight (per log10 unit: β = −269.4 g, 95% CI −465.7 to −73.0).
PFOA was negatively associated with ponderal index (per log10 unit: β = −0.73 kg/m3, 95% CI −1.44 to −0.02).
DEHP significantly decreased ponderal index (per log10 unit: β = −1.28, 95% CI −2.43 to −0.13).
PFOA was negatively associated with mental development in 6-month-old girls (per log10 unit: β = −0.296, 95% CI −11.96 to −0.682).
Polychlorinated dibenzofuran was associated with increased risk of otitis media in male infants (OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.1–5.9).
PFTrDA decreased the risk of eczema at 24 months (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.45–0.86).
PFOS was associated with reduced cortisol and cortisone levels in cord blood (Q4 vs Q1: β = −23.98 ng/mL, 95% CI −47.12 to −11.99).
Prenatal PFOA exposure was significantly inversely associated with IGF2 methylation, mediating reduced ponderal index.
captured_features: environmental chemical concentrations (blood, hair, milk, dust, urine)
summaries.study_design: prospective birth cohort study with nested case-cohort design

summaries.exposure_domain: environmental chemicals (dioxins, PCBs, PFASs, organochlorine pesticides, phthalates, bisphenol A, methylmercury, tobacco smoke)
