loss to follow-up at birth
reliance on self-reported questionnaires for some covariates
potential residual confounding
low environmental chemical exposure levels in Japan may limit generalizability
multiple comparisons without strict correction in some analyses

summaries.title: Body Burden of Dichlorodiphenyl Dichloroethene (DDE) and Childhood Pulmonary Function.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were collected via blood samples, pulmonary function tests, and self-administered questionnaires from a primary cohort of school children in Hesse, Germany.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal study assessing the association between blood DDE levels and pulmonary function (FVC, FEV1) in children aged 8-10 years, examining mediation by height and weight.
key_findings: Linear mixed models showed no significant associations between DDE and pulmonary function parameters after adjustment.
Path analysis demonstrated DDE at age 8 had significant inverse indirect and total effects on FVC at age 10 (−0.18 L per µg/L) and FEV1 at age 10 (−0.17 L per µg/L), mediated by height and weight.
DDE had negative total effects on height (−0.28 cm per µg/L) and weight (−0.24 kg per µg/L).
Sex-stratified analyses showed significant indirect negative effects of DDE on FVC (−0.25 L/µg/L in females, −0.21 L/µg/L in males) and FEV1 (−0.24 L/µg/L in females, −0.19 L/µg/L in males).
summaries.study_design: Longitudinal cohort study with repeated measurements and structural equation modeling (path analysis)
summaries.data_source_type: Primary cohort study / field data collection
summaries.population: Children aged 8-10 years in Hesse, Germany (n=328-344 with complete DDE and PFT data)
summaries.exposure_domain: Persistent organic pollutants / organochlorines (DDE blood levels)
limitations: DDE exposure not measured at age 9 years (values carried forward from age 8)
Missing data required multiple imputation
Reduced statistical power in sex-stratified analyses due to smaller sample sizes
Potential residual confounding from unmeasured immune markers or other environmental factors

summaries.title: Proteomic Biomarkers for Bisphenol A-Early Exposure and Women's Thyroid Cancer.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Matched pairs of thyroid tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues were collected from women thyroid cancer patients (n=28; age, 47.4±11.6 years; papillary carcinoma, 100%; metasatasis, 10.4% of the subjects), who received a surgical treatment at Hanyang University Hospital, Seoul, Korea.
summaries.summary: Experimental study using in utero BPA-exposed mice and human thyroid tissue samples to identify proteomic biomarkers associated with early-life BPA exposure and women's thyroid cancer.
key_findings: 17 proteins were altered in a dose-dependent manner in mouse thyroid tissues following prenatal BPA exposure.
No significant differences were found in mRNA expression of ANXA6, ATP5B, HSPA5, or VCP between tumor and adjacent non-tumor thyroid tissues in women (p > 0.05).
Blood BPA was detected in 90% of thyroid cancer patients (range 0-10.32 ng/mL).

Strong positive associations were observed between blood BPA levels and mRNA expression of VCP (r2=0.47, p=0.02) and ANXA6 (r2=0.37, p=0.03) specifically in thyroid tumor tissues, but not in normal tissues.
captured_features: mRNA expression of ANXA6, ATP5B, HSPA5, VCP
thyroid tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues
summaries.study_design: In utero animal exposure study with ex vivo human tissue validation
summaries.population: Female ICR mice offspring and women with papillary thyroid cancer (n=28, mean age 47.4 years)
limitations: small sample size of human tissues (n=28)

summaries.title: Assessment of Nutritional Status of Infants Living in Arsenic-Contaminated Areas in Bangladesh and Its Association with Arsenic Exposure.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Interviewers collected information by face to face interview using a structured questionnaire on socio-demographics, drinking, bathing, washing, use of cooking water and history of water use. Trained field workers took anthropometric measurements. Drinking water samples from the selected tube wells were transferred and analyzed.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal prospective cohort study assessing the association between household arsenic exposure in drinking water and infant nutritional status (stunting, wasting, underweight) from birth to 9 months in rural Bangladesh.
key_findings: Stunting rates were 10% at 3 months and 44% at 6 and 9 months.
Wasting rates were 23.3% at 3 months and 0% at 6 and 9 months.
Underweight rates were 25% at 3 months and 10% at 6 months, with 0% at 9 months.
Significant association found between stunting at 9 months and household drinking water arsenic exposure ≥50 μg/L (p = 0.009).
No significant association was found between household arsenic exposure and other nutritional indices (wasting, underweight) over time.
captured_features: Household tube well water arsenic concentration
summaries.population: 120 mother-infant pairs in rural Bangladesh, followed from birth to 9 months of age
summaries.exposure_domain: arsenic exposure via household drinking water (tube well concentration <50 μg/L vs ≥50 μg/L)
limitations: Small sample size (n=120)
Short follow-up period (9 months)
Potential change in household drinking water sources during the study leading to exposure misclassification
Lack of maternal anthropometric and nutritional intake data
Possible statistical anomaly for the observed stunting association

summaries.title: Correction to: Early-life exposure to PM2.5 and risk of acute asthma clinical encounters among children in Massachusetts: a case-crossover analysis.
summaries.ehr_evidence: This manuscript is a correction notice to a previously published study and does not describe the primary data source.
summaries.summary: Correction notice addressing an incorrect demographic count in Table 1 of a previously published case-crossover study on early-life PM2.5 exposure and acute asthma clinical encounters in Massachusetts.
summaries.population: children in Massachusetts

summaries.title: Low-fidelity Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus polymerase mutants to improve live-attenuated vaccine safety and efficacy.
summaries.ehr_evidence: This study utilized in vitro cell cultures (Vero, HEK-293, BHK, C7/10, U4.4) and in vivo murine models (6-day-old and 7-week-old CD-1 mice) for viral passaging, plaque assays, and survival/immunogenicity testing.
summaries.summary: Experimental study evaluating low-fidelity RdRp mutations in the Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV) TC-83 vaccine strain to assess attenuation, immunogenicity, and genetic stability in cell culture and murine models.
key_findings: TC-83 3x and 4x mutants produced significantly higher mean neutralizing antibody titers compared with TC-83 (p = 0.0049 and p = 0.0012, respectively; n = 8 per group).
All vaccinated animals (n = 8 per group) showed complete protection from weight loss and death following lethal VEEV challenge, whereas sham-vaccinated controls all succumbed by Day 9.
TC-83 3x was significantly more virulent than parent virus in intracranial infant mice (mean time to death 3.91 days vs 5.36–5.54 days, p < 0.05).
Subcutaneous injection of 3x and 4x mutants in infant mice initially showed reduced mortality compared to TC-83, but outcomes varied significantly by electroporation pool.
After 10 serial intracranial passages in infant mice, 3x and 4x mutants reached virulence equivalent to unpassaged TC-83 and could not increase virulence past that point.
TC-83 4x passage 10 survived up to 1 week longer than passage 5, suggesting decreased fitness with additional passaging.
Illumina sequencing showed the 3x mutant produced a significantly higher amount of genetic diversity than parental TC-83, independent of the cell type used.
captured_features: genetic diversity and mutation frequency via Illumina sequencing
summaries.study_design: Experimental in vitro and in vivo murine model study
summaries.data_source_type: Cell culture and animal model data
summaries.population: Vero, HEK-293, BHK, C7/10, U4.4 cell lines; 6-day-old and 7-week-old CD-1 mice
summaries.exposure_domain: Viral RdRp fidelity mutations and nucleoside analog treatment
limitations: Phenotypic instability of low-fidelity mutants dependent on electroporation pool and mutant spectrum
Lack of atomic resolution structure for alphavirus RdRp limits mechanistic understanding
Results derived exclusively from murine models and cell culture, lacking human clinical or epidemiological data
Short-term passaging may not reflect long-term vaccine stability in natural settings

summaries.title: Local- and regional-scale air pollution modelling (PM(10)) and exposure assessment for pregnancy trimesters, infancy, and childhood to age 15 years: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents And Children (ALSPAC).
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study used residential address history from the ALSPAC contact database and hourly PM10 measurements from the UK Automatic Urban and Rural Network (AURN) monitoring sites.
summaries.summary: Development and evaluation of local and regional-scale PM10 dispersion models to estimate individual-level historical air pollution exposures from pregnancy through age 15 years for the ALSPAC birth cohort.
key_findings: PM10 exposures declined on average by 11.6 μg/m3 from the first year of life (mean 31.2 μg/m3) to age ~15 (mean 19.6 μg/m3).
Intra-subject exposure contrasts were largest between pregnancy trimesters (5th to 95th centile: 24.4–37.3 μg/m3).
Local sources contributed 18.5%–19.5% during pregnancy/infancy and 14.4%–17.0% for longer periods, with main roads contributing ~3.0%.
Model evaluation showed good correlation with measured weekly PM10 concentrations (r = 0.71, p < 0.001), though the model underestimated concentrations (MB = -4.1 μg/m3, MPB = 21%).
summaries.study_design: Methodological exposure assessment study using dispersion modelling within a prospective birth cohort
summaries.data_source_type: Birth cohort (ALSPAC) with environmental monitoring and dispersion modelling data
summaries.population: Children in the ALSPAC birth cohort from pregnancy through age ~15 years, residing in the Avon region/south west England
summaries.exposure_domain: Air pollution (PM10), including local (traffic, industry, housing) and regional/long-range sources
limitations: Single monitoring site used for model evaluation
Lack of historic emissions data for specific industrial and domestic sources
Inability to model terrain, buildings, and wet deposition effects
Use of constant value for natural PM10 sources due to lack of pre-1993 monitoring data
Potential overestimation of background concentrations from imputed central site data

summaries.title: Total mercury exposure in early pregnancy has no adverse association with scholastic ability of the offspring particularly if the mother eats fish.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC) aimed to study all births to women resident in a geographic area (Avon) in the UK, whose expected date of delivery lay between the 1st April 1991 and 31st December 1992. (Data source is a prospective birth cohort with questionnaires and biospecimen assays, not EHR.)
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study assessing the association between prenatal total blood mercury levels and offspring scholastic abilities, with stratification by maternal fish consumption.
key_findings: After adjustment, no significant associations were found between prenatal total blood mercury and any of the 15 scholastic test outcomes (all p > 0.05).

Stratified analysis revealed a significant interaction with maternal fish consumption: children of non-fish-eating mothers showed negative associations between mercury and mathematics/science reasoning scores, whereas children of fish-eating mothers showed positive associations.
No statistically significant differences were observed between boys and girls (data not shown).
captured_features: offspring scholastic test scores (reading, spelling, phoneme, mathematics, science)
demographic and lifestyle covariates (maternal age, parity, education, housing, smoking, alcohol, breastfeeding, stress, family adversity)
summaries.population: children born in Avon, UK (1991–1992), followed into childhood and adolescence (ages 7–13)
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal mercury exposure and maternal fish consumption
limitations: notable attrition bias with excess drop-out from young parents, smokers, and lower socioeconomic groups
relatively small sample size of children whose mothers did not eat fish
single first-trimester blood draw may not reflect mercury levels later in pregnancy
observational design limits causal inference

summaries.title: Occupational exposure to organic solvents during pregnancy and childhood behavior: findings from the PELAGIE birth cohort (France, 2002-2013).
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were collected via the PELAGIE birth cohort using self-reported questionnaires and parent-completed behavioral checklists (CBCL, PSBQ, SDQ).
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study examining the association between maternal occupational exposure to organic solvents during pregnancy and childhood behavioral outcomes at ages 2 and 6.
key_findings: Increased externalizing behavior score at age 2 was associated with prenatal exposure to solvents (standardized score: 0.34 (95% CI = 0.11, 0.57) for occasional exposure and 0.26 (0.05, 0.48) for regular exposure).
This association was attenuated at age 6 (0.22 (−0.02, 0.47) for occasional exposure and 0.07 (−0.14, 0.28) for regular exposure).
No association was observed for internalizing behavior at either age.
summaries.population: 715 mother-child pairs from the PELAGIE birth cohort in France, children assessed at ages 2 and 6
summaries.exposure_domain: occupational exposure to organic solvents during pregnancy
limitations: exposure assessment based on maternal self-reports
groups defined by frequency rather than intensity
use of different behavioral tools at ages 2 and 6
potential lack of measurement invariance between sexes
inability to account for other maternal or postnatal environmental exposures to solvents

summaries.title: Analysis By Deep Sequencing of Discontinued Neurotropic Yellow Fever Vaccine Strains.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Viruses. Wild-type French viscerotropic (FVV) and Asibi strains were obtained from the World Reference Center for Emerging Viruses and Arboviruses (Galveston, TX, USA) as lyophilized cell culture supernatant.
summaries.summary: Deep sequencing and in silico analysis of archived yellow fever vaccine strains (FNV and 17D) and wild-type parental strains to assess genetic diversity, population structure, and reversion to wild-type identity in relation to neurotropic phenotypes.
key_findings: FNV strains showed lower genetic diversity than wild-type FVV, with 19 conserved amino acid substitutions across all four FNV strains.
Eight nucleotide positions were highly unstable, with reversion to wild-type identity most evident in low-neurotropism strains FNV-FC and FNV-NT.
FNV-FC and FNV-NT had higher variant counts (n=131 and n=165) and higher revertant frequencies than high-neurotropism strains FNV-Yale and FNV-IP (n=91 variants each).
17D-204 vaccine diversity was significantly lower than parental Asibi (mean NSE 0.029 vs 0.118, p < 0.001).
Kruskal-Wallis tests showed significant differences in NSE (X2 = 2773.51, df = 6, p < 0.001) and RMSD (X2 = 29970, df = 6, p < 0.001) across all seven strains.
summaries.study_design: in vitro genomic sequencing and in silico bioinformatics analysis
summaries.population: archived yellow fever virus strains (FNV, 17D-204, Asibi, FVV) from institutional and commercial collections
limitations: passage histories of archived strains are unknown
limited sample size of four FNV strains
neurovirulence data is historical and cited rather than generated in this study
relationship to original Dakar strain is unknown

summaries.title: Sex-Dependent Impact of Low-Level Lead Exposure during Prenatal Period on Child Psychomotor Functions.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study utilized the Polish Mother and Child Cohort (REPRO_PL), collecting questionnaire data, biological samples, and neurodevelopmental assessments directly from participants.
summaries.summary: Prospective mother-child cohort study evaluating the sex-dependent impact of low-level prenatal lead exposure on child psychomotor and cognitive development up to 24 months of age.
key_findings: Among boys, increasing cord blood lead levels were associated with lower cognitive function scores (β = −2.07; p = 0.04).
No statistically significant impact of prenatal lead exposure on girls' psychomotor abilities was observed.
For language and motor abilities, results were not statistically significant for either sex (p > 0.05).

Bayley cognitive, language, and motor scores

lack of data on home environment quality, parent-child relationship, parental roles, and maternal IQ
potential selection bias as sample represents urban population with high SES
lack of measurement/inclusion of other neurotoxic elements (As, Cd, Hg)

summaries.title: Is intrauterine exposure to acetaminophen associated with emotional and hyperactivity problems during childhood? Findings from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We performed a prospective longitudinal population-based study using data from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort.
summaries.summary: Prospective longitudinal birth cohort study investigating the association between prenatal acetaminophen exposure and childhood emotional and hyperactivity symptoms at ages 6 and 11 in a Brazilian population, finding sex-specific associations primarily in boys at age 6.
key_findings: At age 6, intrauterine acetaminophen exposure increased odds of emotional problems in boys (OR = 1.47; 95% CI: 1.07–2.02) and hyperactivity/inattention problems (OR = 1.42; 95% CI: 1.06–1.92).
At age 11, associations for boys were attenuated and lost statistical significance after adjustment (emotional: OR = 1.31; 95% CI: 0.99–1.73; hyperactivity/inattention: OR = 1.25; 95% CI: 0.95–1.65).
No significant associations were observed for girls at either age 6 or 11.
Sensitivity analyses confirmed the effect was specific to acetaminophen, as other nonsteroidal analgesics showed no association with behavioral outcomes.
captured_features: Maternal self-reported acetaminophen use during pregnancy
summaries.population: children from the 2004 Pelotas birth cohort in Brazil, assessed at ages 6 and 11 years
limitations: Retrospective recall of maternal medication use may lead to underreporting.
Lack of data on exposure timing (trimester) and dosage.
Potential residual confounding by socioeconomic position.
Absence of information on reasons for medication use (e.g., fever or infection).

summaries.title: Early-life antibiotics attenuate regulatory T cell generation and increase the severity of murine house dust mite-induced asthma.
summaries.ehr_evidence: C57BL/6J nursing mothers with 3-week-old female pups were purchased from the Jackson Laboratory (Bar Harbor, ME, USA).
summaries.summary: Experimental murine study investigating how early-life pulsed antibiotic exposure affects the severity of house dust mite-induced allergic airway disease, microbiome diversity, and regulatory T cell generation.
key_findings: HDM+ABX Mix animals exhibited threefold higher BAL leukocytosis (29.0 × 10^5 vs. 9.0 × 10^5 cells, p < 0.01).
HDM+ABX Mix had twofold higher relative eosinophilia (43% vs. 20%, p < 0.01) and over fivefold higher total eosinophils (14.0 × 10^5 vs. 2.4 × 10^5, p < 0.01).
HDM+ABX Mix had significantly higher HDM-specific IgE (0.95 vs. 0.50 mean AUC, p < 0.05).
HDM+ABX Mix showed more severe lung histopathology (2.5 vs. 1.5 median score, p < 0.01).
HDM+ABX Mix had significantly higher respiratory system resistance AUC (5.1 vs. 3.8, p < 0.05).
ABX exposure reduced fecal microbiome diversity (Simpson index 0.747 vs. 0.954, p < 0.01).
HDM+ABX Mix had lower pulmonary Treg proportions (8.9% vs. 11.1%, p < 0.05).
Microbiome diversity positively correlated with Treg proportion (Spearman's r = 0.7109, p < 0.01).
captured_features: fecal microbiome diversity (Simpson index, 16S rRNA sequencing)
summaries.population: C57BL/6J mice
limitations: ABX cocktail combination is unlikely to be utilized clinically.
Study does not conclusively establish that immunologic changes are exclusively derived from microbiome disruption.
Limited sample size for some Treg assessments.
Results may not directly translate to other diseases.

summaries.title: Prenatal Exposure to Select Phthalates and Phenols and Associations with Fetal and Placental Weight among Male Births in the EDEN Cohort (France).
summaries.ehr_evidence: Placental and birth weight were obtained at birth from hospital maternity records. Phenol and phthalate metabolite urinary concentrations were assessed in spot urine samples collected during pregnancy.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study examining associations between prenatal urinary concentrations of phenols and phthalates and placental weight, birth weight, and placental-to-birth weight ratio among 473 male births in France.
key_findings: Sum of parabens positively associated with placental weight (b = 7.12 g, 95% CI: 0.41, 13.9).
Benzophenone-3 positively associated with placental weight (b = 4.76 g, 95% CI: -1.77, 11.3).
Triclosan negatively associated with placental weight (b = -4.11 g, 95% CI: -8.26, 0.05).
MCNP negatively associated with placental weight (b = -10.9 g, 95% CI: -21.8, 0.09).
Benzophenone-3 positively associated with birth weight (b = 21.0 g, 95% CI: -3.45, 45.5).
MCOP and MCNP negatively associated with PFR (MCOP: b = -0.23, 95% CI: -0.58, 0.11; MCNP: b = -0.20, 95% CI: -0.54, 0.13).
No associations remained significant after FDR correction in sensitivity analyses (lowest corrected p-value = 0.39).
captured_features: Urinary phenol and phthalate metabolite concentrations

summaries.title: SSRIs target prefrontal to raphe circuits during development modulating synaptic connectivity and emotional behavior.

key_findings: SERT-KO mice have a 40% increase in the number of VGLUT1+ axon boutons in the DRN compared to SERT+/- mice at 4 weeks of age.
Postnatal fluoxetine induces a 47% increase in the number of VGLUT1+ cortical synaptic innervations in the DRN.
Cortex-specific conditional SERT invalidation led to a 30% increase in the number of VGLUT1+ synaptic boutons in the DRN.
67 ± 8.0% of the VGLUT1+/synapsin+ terminals in the DRN were colabeled with TdTomato, indicating they arise from PFC-SERT+ neurons.

focus on a single brain circuit may not capture whole-brain effects

summaries.title: Development of a novel multiplex electrochemiluminescent-based immunoassay to aid enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli vaccine development and evaluations.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We used the serum and ALS (antibody in lymphocyte supernatant) samples from the volunteers vaccinated with ACE527 vaccine and placebo volunteers challenged with H10407 ETEC for validation of the multiplex ECL assay.
summaries.summary: Development and validation of a novel 8-plex multiplex electrochemiluminescent (ECL) immunoassay using the MSD platform to measure immune responses to ETEC antigens, compared against conventional ELISA.
key_findings: Intra-assay variability showed percent CV below 20% (range 5.3%–18.1%) for all 8 antigens.
Inter-assay variability showed percent CV below 20% (range 7.7%–17.9%) across 3 consecutive days.
Dilution linearity yielded R² values between 90% and 100% for high titer samples and 75% to 90% for low titer samples.
Specificity testing showed over 60% inhibition for all antigens.
Concordance analysis showed no significant difference between ECL and ELISA for most antigens (p < .05), except CS3 (p = .0087) and LTB IgG (p = .0200).
ECL demonstrated higher sensitivity than ELISA, with a maximum to minimum signal ratio of 1434.62 compared to 87.63 for ELISA.

Observed cross-reactivity between some antigens

summaries.title: Dietary Patterns Are Not Consistently Associated with Variability in Blood Lead Concentrations in Pregnant British Women.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The primary source of data collection was self-completed questionnaires sent to the mother. Blood samples were collected by midwives during pregnancy.
summaries.summary: Observational analysis of the ALSPAC birth cohort evaluating associations between maternal dietary patterns/food groups and blood lead concentrations during pregnancy.
key_findings: Negative association between the 'confectionery' dietary pattern and likelihood of B-Pb ≥5 µg/dL (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.41, 0.94).
Positive association between 'all leafy green and green vegetables' consumption and likelihood of B-Pb ≥5 µg/dL (OR: 1.45; 95% CI: 1.04, 2.01).
Negative association between 'cakes and biscuits' consumption and likelihood of B-Pb ≥5 µg/dL (OR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.93).

After multiple imputation, a positive association was found for the 'healthy' diet pattern (OR: 1.58; 95% CI: 1.27, 1.97) and a negative association for milk consumption (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61, 0.98).
No significant associations were found for other dietary patterns or food groups in adjusted models.
captured_features: Dietary pattern scores derived from FFQ

Temporal mismatch between first-trimester blood sampling and third-trimester dietary data collection
Self-reported dietary data subject to misreporting
Selection bias due to subsample characteristics
Residual confounding possible
Inconsistency between complete-case and multiple-imputation results

summaries.title: Mitotically heritable effects of BMAA on striatal neural stem cell proliferation and differentiation.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We used primary neuronal cell cultures and embryonic neural stem cells from rat striatum.
summaries.summary: In vitro study investigating the direct and mitotically heritable effects of the cyanobacterial neurotoxin BMAA on rat striatal neural stem cell proliferation, differentiation, and morphology.
key_findings: 250 µM BMAA reduced neural stem cell proliferation through apoptosis and G2/M arrest.
50-100 µM BMAA reduced differentiation into neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes.
BMAA-induced morphological alterations (reduced neurite length, processes, and branches) were mitotically heritable to daughter cells (D1 and D2).

P1 cells treated with 100 µM BMAA showed decreased neuron percentage (31.72% to 16.66%, p<0.001), astrocyte percentage (34.38% to 15.49%, p<0.01), and oligodendrocyte percentage (15.75% to 9.42%, p<0.05).
Glutamate antagonists MK-801 and MCPG completely protected against BMAA-induced decreases in cell viability, proliferation, and morphological alterations.
captured_features: differentiation markers (β III-tubulin, GFAP, Oligo4, nestin)
summaries.study_design: in vitro mechanistic cell culture study
summaries.population: embryonic rat striatal neural stem cells and primary neurons
limitations: in vitro model limitations
lack of randomization
extrapolation to human development requires caution

summaries.title: The effect of H1N1 vaccination on serum miRNA expression in children: A tale of caution for microRNA microarray studies.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Serum samples were obtained from children aged 6 months to 12 years enrolled in an open label randomised control trial of two pandemic influenza (H1N1) vaccines, in which participants received either ASO3B adjuvanted split virion or a whole virion non-adjuvanted vaccine.
summaries.summary: A randomized controlled trial sub-study profiling serum microRNA expression in children before and 21 days after H1N1 vaccination using microarray and RT-qPCR, highlighting validation challenges.
key_findings: Microarray analysis identified 19 differentially expressed miRNAs post-vaccination (fold-change >1.2, adjusted p<0.05).
RT-qPCR confirmed significant downregulation of miR-142-3p in the discovery cohort (mean log2 fold-change = -0.312, p = 0.003).
Downregulation of miR-142-3p was not replicated in the validation cohort (mean log2 fold-change = 0.15, p = 0.89).
Only 3 out of 19 differentially expressed miRNAs were detectable by RT-qPCR, with many showing no amplification or high background.
summaries.study_design: randomized controlled trial sub-study with microarray and RT-qPCR validation
summaries.population: children aged 6 months to 12 years
limitations: lack of replication in independent validation cohort
potential false positives from microarray cross-hybridization
single microarray platform used

summaries.title: Repeated holdout validation for weighted quantile sum regression.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Using data from 718 mother-child pairs in the Swedish Environmental Longitudinal, Mother and Child, Asthma and Allergy (SELMA) study, we assessed the association between prenatal exposure to 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals and child Intelligence Quotient (IQ).
summaries.summary: Methodological paper demonstrating repeated holdout validation for weighted quantile sum regression using SELMA cohort data to assess prenatal chemical mixture exposure and child IQ.
key_findings: WQS index estimate was significant when all data was used (β = -2.2, CI = -3.43, -0.98), but attenuated and nonsignificant using repeated holdout validation (β = -0.82, CI = -2.11, 0.45).
DPHP had the second highest mean weight (10%) but seven of 100 repetitions were below the chemical of concern threshold.
Triclosan mean weight was 3% but 26% of repetitions had weights above the threshold.
captured_features: prenatal exposure to 26 endocrine disrupting chemicals

finite sample sizes may limit stability
training-test split percentages are somewhat arbitrary
potential for random error or unmeasured confounding

summaries.title: Serious adverse event: late neurotropic disease associated with yellow fever vaccine.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Clinical case report of a 9-month-old infant at Hospital Geral de Carapicuíba, with data from physical examination, laboratory tests, computed tomography, and vaccination records.
summaries.summary: Case report of a previously healthy 9-month-old infant who developed late neurotropic disease 20 days after yellow fever vaccination, presenting with fever, strabismus, cervical muscle weakness, and leg weakness, followed by complete recovery after supportive care.
key_findings: Positive IgM for yellow fever virus in cerebrospinal fluid confirmed vaccine-associated neurotropic disease (N=1).
Patient showed clinical improvement by day 5 and complete recovery by day 10.
Tests for bacteria and herpes-virus were negative.

summaries.title: Early-life inhalant allergen exposure, filaggrin genotype, and the development of sensitization from infancy to adolescence.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The Manchester Asthma and Allergy Study is an unselected birth cohort described in detail elsewhere. The source actually consisted of prospectively collected home dust samples, skin prick test results, genotyping data, and questionnaire responses.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal birth cohort study examining how early-life inhalant allergen exposure interacts with filaggrin (FLG) loss-of-function mutations to influence the development of allergic sensitization from infancy to age 16.
key_findings: Significant interaction between FLG mutations and Fel d 1 exposure on cat sensitization (OR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.02-1.80; P = .035), with a greater effect in children with FLG mutations.
Increased risk of mite sensitization with Der p 1 exposure was consistently greater among children with FLG mutations, but the interaction did not reach statistical significance.

Significant interaction between FLG mutations and dog ownership on sensitization to any allergen (OR, 0.16; 95% CI, 0.03-0.86; P = .03), with significantly lower risk in children with FLG mutations exposed to a dog in infancy.
No significant interaction was found between FLG mutations and Can f 1 exposure on dog sensitization.
captured_features: Dust allergen concentrations (Der p 1, Fel d 1, Can f 1)
Demographic and confounding variables (sex, socioeconomic status, breast-feeding)

Smaller sample size at age 1 year and in some subgroups

summaries.title: BCG Moreau Vaccine Safety Profile and NK Cells-Double Protection Against Disseminated BCG Infection in Retrospective Study of BCG Vaccination in 52 Polish Children with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Retrospective hospital clinical records from the Children’s Memorial Health Institute (CMHI), Warsaw. 'The profiles of 52 SCID patients vaccinated at birth with BCG, hospitalized in Children’s Memorial Health Institute, Warsaw (CMHI), in the years 1980–2015 were compared with those of 349 BCG-vaccinated SCID patients from other countries analyzed by Beatriz E. Marciano et al. in a retrospective study.'
summaries.summary: Retrospective study evaluating the safety profile and clinical outcomes of the BCG Moreau vaccine in 52 Polish children with severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) hospitalized at the Children’s Memorial Health Institute in Warsaw between 1980 and 2015, compared with an international cohort.
key_findings: Disseminated BCG infection occurred in 10 out of 52 SCID patients (19%), significantly lower than the 34% rate in the external Marciano cohort (p = 0.0028).
Localized BCG complications were observed in 12 patients (24%), not significantly different from the external cohort's 17% (p = 0.2417).
Disseminated BCG complications were exclusively found in SCID patients with low NK cell counts (p < 0.000001), while T cell counts showed no significant impact (p = 0.0915).
Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) was performed in 43 patients (83%), significantly higher than the 54% rate in the external cohort (p = 0.0001).
Mortality from BCG complications was 5% (3 deaths) in the CMHI cohort versus 13% (46 deaths) in the external cohort (p = 0.1724).
captured_features: immunological cell counts (T, B, and NK cells)
genetic mutation status (e.g., IL2RG, JAK3, RAG1/2)

summaries.title: Childhood type 1 diabetes: an environment-wide association study across England.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We obtained type 1 diabetes data from National Health Service (NHS) Digital hospital episode statistics (HES) records.
summaries.summary: Ecological EnWAS assessing associations between 53 demographic and environmental factors and childhood type 1 diabetes incidence across England.
key_findings: Overall incidence was 21.2 (95% CI 20.9, 21.6) per 100,000 children aged 0–9 years.
15 of 53 factors were significantly associated with incidence after multiple testing.
Multivariable ecological regression showed the living environment domain of IMD was inversely associated with risk (RR 0.995; 95% CrI 0.991, 0.998).
Radon potential class was positively associated with risk (RR 1.044; 95% CrI 1.015, 1.074).
Air pollutants, lead in soil, overcrowding, population density, and ethnicity showed significant unadjusted associations but were not significant in the multivariable model.

summaries.title: Early-Life Famine Exposure and Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases in Later Life: Findings From the REACTION Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We used data from REACTION (Risk Evaluation of Cancers in Chinese Diabetic Individuals: A Longitudinal) Study, which recruited a total of 259 657 community-dwelling adults aged 40 years or older from 25 centers across mainland China between 2011 and 2012.
summaries.summary: Observational study examining the association between early-life exposure to the Chinese famine (1959-1962) and the risk of cardiovascular diseases in adulthood among a large Chinese cohort.
key_findings: Fetal famine exposure was associated with increased risk of total CVD (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.20–1.52), MI (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.08–2.35), stroke (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.11–1.78), and CHD (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.26–1.65).

Childhood famine exposure was associated with increased risk of total CVD (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.40–1.81), MI (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.52–3.20), stroke (OR 1.82, 95% CI 1.45–2.28), and CHD (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.56–2.09).

Adolescent famine exposure was associated with increased risk of total CVD (OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.27–1.81), MI (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.28–3.35), stroke (OR 1.92, 95% CI 1.42–2.58), and CHD (OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.50–2.24).
Individuals in severely affected famine areas had significantly increased risk of total CVD compared to those in less severely affected areas across all exposure groups.
The association between early-life famine exposure and CVD risk was stronger in women, non-smokers, non-drinkers, and those without moderate-to-vigorous physical activity.
Part of the impact of famine exposure on CVD was mediated via metabolic syndrome.
captured_features: lifestyle factors (smoking, drinking, physical activity, diet)
anthropometric measurements (height, weight, BMI, waist circumference)
serum lipids (total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides)

lack of early-life lifestyle data

summaries.title: DNA methylome signatures of prenatal exposure to synthetic glucocorticoids in hippocampus and peripheral whole blood of female guinea pigs in early life.
summaries.ehr_evidence: At PND 14, one female juvenile offspring per litter was randomly selected and euthanized by an unblinded experimenter. Animals were euthanized via isoﬂurane inhalation, and hippocampus and whole blood samples were immediately collected via cardiac puncture from each subject (1/litter, n = 6/tissue type/treatment: Suppl Fig. 1A).
summaries.summary: Experimental study examining DNA methylation signatures in the hippocampus and whole blood of juvenile female guinea pigs following prenatal exposure to synthetic glucocorticoids.
key_findings: Identified 7004 differentially methylated CpG sites (DMCs) in the hippocampus (79.9% hypermethylated, 20.3% hypomethylated).
Identified 16,740 DMCs in whole blood (62.7% hypermethylated, 37.3% hypomethylated).
Found 1044 DMCs at identical CpG sites in both tissues, representing 14.9% of hippocampal and 6.2% of blood DMCs.
Positive correlation between methylation difference percent in hippocampus and blood (R = 0.31, n = 1044, P < .0001).
134 genes showed differential methylation in both tissues, with 61 genes showing changes at identical CpG sites.
Gene pathway enrichment indicated alterations in clusters involved in brain development and neurogenesis.
No enrichment of glucocorticoid regulatory element (GRE) motifs was observed at differentially methylated sites.
captured_features: DNA methylation levels at single-nucleotide resolution via RRBS
Differentially methylated CpG sites (DMCs) and regions (DMRs)
Spearman correlation coefficients for methylation concordance

summaries.population: juvenile female guinea pigs (Hartley strain), offspring of mothers treated with betamethasone or saline during late gestation
limitations: animal model limits direct human translational applicability
small sample size (n=6 per treatment group)
only female offspring examined

summaries.title: Assessment of chronic bronchitis and risk factors in young adults: results from BAMSE.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Questionnaire data and clinical measures from the 24-year follow-up of the Swedish BAMSE (Child (Barn), Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm, Epidemiological) cohort were used.
summaries.summary: Assessment of chronic bronchitis prevalence and early-life risk factors in young adults from the Swedish BAMSE birth cohort.
key_findings: Overall prevalence of chronic bronchitis at 24 years was 5.5% (n=158).
Daily smoking was associated with chronic bronchitis (aOR 3.85, 95% CI 2.32–6.39, p<0.001).
Black carbon exposure at ages 1–4 years was associated with chronic bronchitis (aOR 1.71 per 1 μg·m−3 increase, 95% CI 1.14–2.57, p=0.009).
Exclusive breastfeeding for ≥4 months was protective (aOR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44–0.99, p=0.044).
Childhood asthma at age 1–16 years was a strong risk factor (OR 3.08, 95% CI 2.17–4.35, p<0.001).
49% of chronic bronchitis cases experienced >3 respiratory infections in the past year versus 18% of non-cases (p<0.001).
captured_features: Geocoded residential, day-care, and school addresses
Modeled air pollution concentrations (NOx, black carbon)
summaries.data_source_type: Birth cohort / Questionnaire and clinical measurements
summaries.population: Young adults (mean age 22.4 years) from the Swedish BAMSE birth cohort, originally recruited 1994–1996
summaries.exposure_domain: Early-life environmental exposures (traffic-related air pollution: black carbon, NOx), smoking, breastfeeding
limitations: Chronic bronchitis definition based on questionnaire without specified time period
Exploratory analyses without multiple testing correction
Potential misclassification of asthma as chronic bronchitis
Self-reported respiratory health events
Lack of laboratory workup for infections
Critically ill newborns excluded

summaries.title: Aspartame and cancer - new evidence for causation.
summaries.ehr_evidence: RI subjected all HLTs from aspartame-exposed animals to immunohistochemical analysis using a battery of markers and to morphological reassessment using the most recent Internationally Harmonized Nomenclature and Diagnostic (INHAND) criteria.
summaries.summary: Commentary re-evaluating Ramazzini Institute rodent toxicology studies, confirming aspartame-induced hematolymphatic malignancies and prenatal carcinogenic effects through immunohistochemical and morphological reassessment.
key_findings: Immunohistochemical and morphological re-evaluation confirmed malignancy in 92.3% of originally diagnosed hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue tumors.
Six lesions originally diagnosed as lymphoma were reclassified: 3 to lymphoid hyperplasia and 3 to chronic inflammation with fibrosis.
No histological evidence of Mycoplasma pulmonis infection was found.
Statistically significant increase in incidence of all hematolymphatic malignancies (p = 0.006), including lymphomas (p = 0.032) and leukemias (p = 0.031).
Positive dose-response relationship observed between aspartame exposure and hematolymphatic malignancy incidence.
Prenatal exposures produced dose-related increases in malignancies at lower exposure levels and shorter latency than adult exposures.
captured_features: immunohistochemical markers (Ki67, CD3, PAX5, CD20, CD68, TdT, CD45, CD14, CD33)
hematopoietic and lymphoid tissue tumor diagnoses
summaries.population: Sprague-Dawley rats and Swiss mice
limitations: re-evaluation based on existing rodent bioassay data
extrapolation of rodent findings to human health risks

summaries.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of AS03-adjuvanted H5N1 Influenza Vaccine in Children 6-35 Months of Age: Results From a Phase 2, Randomized, Observer-blind, Multicenter, Dose-ranging Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study collected primary data through clinical trial visits, blood samples for serologic testing, cell-mediated immunity assessments, and adverse event reporting.
summaries.summary: Phase 2 randomized, multicenter, dose-ranging clinical trial evaluating the immunogenicity and safety of different formulations of an AS03-adjuvanted H5N1 influenza vaccine in children 6–35 months of age.
key_findings: All formulations elicited strong homologous immune responses with seroconversion rates of 100% and seroprotection rates of 100% at day 42.
The 1.9 µg HA/AS03B formulation ranked highest on the immunogenicity-fever index.
Antibody levels persisted >4 times above baseline at day 385 for all formulations.
Overall per-subject incidence of fever ranged from 28.6% (3.75 µg HA/AS03D) to 60.5% (1.9 µg HA/AS03B).
Grade 3 fever (≥39.0 °C) was reported in 18.4% of subjects in the 1.9 µg HA/AS03B group.
Serious adverse events were reported for 29 subjects (15.7%), none of which were fatal or related to vaccination.
captured_features: Geometric mean titers (GMT), seroprotection rate (SPR), seroconversion rate (SCR)
summaries.study_design: Phase 2, randomized, observer-blind, multicenter, dose-ranging clinical trial
summaries.population: Children 6–35 months of age (n=185) from Thailand and Taiwan
limitations: Small sample size
Absence of a placebo control to assess vaccine safety
Immunogenicity-fever index did not include other reactogenicity indicators
Limited generalizability

summaries.title: Maternal high-fat diet modifies myelin organization, microglial interactions, and results in social memory and sensorimotor gating deficits in adolescent mouse offspring.
summaries.ehr_evidence: C57BL/6N female mice aged 5 – 6 weeks were obtained from Charles River and habituated to pair-housing for one week.
summaries.summary: Preclinical study investigating how maternal high-fat diet modifies myelin organization, microglial interactions, and behavioral outcomes in adolescent mouse offspring.
key_findings: Increased myelin optical density in mHFD-exposed male offspring compared to female mHFD-exposed offspring (p=0.0082).
Reduced area of cytosolic myelin channels in mHFD-exposed male offspring compared to control males (p=0.0016).
Lower hippocampal expression of Mbp, Cspg4, Olig2, and Igf1 in mHFD-exposed males (Mbp p=0.0014 vs male CD).
mHFD-exposed microglia exhibited reduced numbers of mature tertiary lysosomes and increased synaptic contacts.
mHFD-exposed offspring of both sexes showed decreased social novelty preference and reduced prepulse inhibition at 9 dB prepulse.
No significant differences in oligodendrocyte density, distribution, or maturation between diet groups.
captured_features: cytosolic myelin channel area and ratio
gene expression (Mbp, Cspg4, Olig2, Igf1, Gpnmb)
behavioral metrics (social preference, social novelty preference, anxiety index, prepulse inhibition)
summaries.population: adolescent C57BL/6N mouse offspring (male and female)
limitations: preclinical mouse model limits direct human translation
small sample sizes per group (n=4-5 animals)
lack of direct microglial modulation to establish causality
sex-specific mechanisms not fully elucidated beyond male/female dichotomy

summaries.ehr_evidence: Narrative review synthesizing published clinical trial data, surveillance reports, and historical literature on rotavirus vaccine development and implementation.

summaries.title: Nasal spray live attenuated influenza vaccine: the first experience in Italy in children and adolescents during the 2020-21 season.
summaries.ehr_evidence: A questionnaire was given out to parents on the day of the vaccination, on a voluntary and anonymous basis, through which information about children and their parents was collected.
summaries.summary: Observational study evaluating the safety, adverse events, and parental satisfaction of the first use of nasal quadrivalent live attenuated influenza vaccine (qLAIV) in Italian children and adolescents aged 2-17 years during the 2020-21 season.
key_findings: Adverse events were reported in 24.8% of children (80.6% mild, 18.1% moderate, 1.3% significant).
Most common adverse events were cold/rhinitis (52.5%) and fever (24.4%).
Children aged 2-5 years had an increased risk of adverse events compared to 6-10 years (aRR 1.7, 95% CI 1.5-1.9, p<0.001) and 11-17 years (aRR 1.5, 95% CI 1-2.2, p=0.051).
Children with at least one acute infectious disease in 2020 had higher risk (aRR 1.2, 95% CI 1.1-1.4, p=0.004) and those with chronic diseases had higher risk (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.1, p=0.001).
Males had a decreased probability of adverse reactions compared to females (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.8-1, p=0.011).

No significant association was found between adverse events and prematurity (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.7-1.1, p=0.220), allergic diseases (aRR 1.1, 95% CI 0.7-1.5, p=0.667), or previous influenza vaccination (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.8-1.1, p=0.382).
83.3% of parents were very satisfied and 83.8% intended to re-vaccinate their children.
Adverse reactions were the main reason for not repeating vaccination (aRR 5.5, 95% CI 2.4-12.5, p<0.001).
captured_features: Demographic data (age, sex, birthplace, gestational age, siblings, daycare attendance)
Vaccination history (previous flu vaccine, chronic diseases, acute infectious diseases)
Adverse event type and severity (mild, moderate, significant)
Parental satisfaction and intention to re-vaccinate
summaries.population: children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in Milan, Italy
summaries.exposure_domain: influenza vaccination (quadrivalent live attenuated influenza vaccine)
limitations: self-reported data via questionnaires and phone calls
selection bias due to high proportion of university-educated parents and Italian nationality
low representation of adolescents (3.6%)
telephone follow-up attrition (600 null questionnaires excluded)

summaries.title: The association between in utero exposure to maternal psychological stress and female reproductive function in adolescence: A prospective cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The Raine Study, formed from a pregnancy cohort study, was designed to measure the relationships between early life events and subsequent health and behavior.
summaries.summary: Prospective cohort study examining the association between maternal psychological stress (stressful life events) during pregnancy and reproductive function in female offspring aged 14–16 years.
key_findings: Exposure to one or more maternal stressful life events in late gestation was associated with greater uterine volume (β = 0.13, 95% CI 0.04; 0.23) and higher ovarian AFC (β = 0.19, 95% CI 0.02; 0.35) in adjusted multivariate linear regression analyses.
No associations between stressful life events in early or late gestation and circulating AMH or Inhibin B were observed.
captured_features: offspring age, height, BMI, menarche timing
summaries.population: 228 female adolescents (aged 14–16 years) from The Raine Study pregnancy cohort in Western Australia
summaries.exposure_domain: maternal psychological stress / stressful life events during pregnancy
limitations: moderate sample size limiting statistical power
potential residual confounding by unmeasured pre- and postnatal factors
self-reported stress via questionnaire may vary in perceived severity
transabdominal ultrasound may be less accurate than transvaginal ultrasound
multiple testing without strict Bonferroni correction may increase false positive risk

summaries.title: Early life exposure to house dust mite allergen prevents experimental allergic asthma requiring mitochondrial H(2)O(2).
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study utilized wild-type and MCAT transgenic mice purchased from Jackson Laboratories and housed at the University of Pittsburgh.
summaries.summary: Experimental mouse study demonstrating that early-life low-dose house dust mite (HDM) exposure induces airway tolerance via mitochondrial H2O2 production in lung dendritic cells, preventing allergic asthma.
key_findings: Early-life exposure to low-dose HDM (0.5 µg) at 2 weeks prevented airway inflammation and mucus upon challenge at 6 weeks, whereas high-dose HDM (5 µg) did not.
Low-dose HDM reduced BAL fluid cellularity and significantly decreased IL-13- and IL-5-producing CD4+ T cells compared to the inflammation group.
WT tolerant mice showed a 50% decrease in total lung dendritic cell numbers compared to naïve mice.
MCAT mice (mitochondrial H2O2-depleted) failed to establish tolerance and harbored approximately 3-fold more total DCs and cDC1/cDC2 subsets than WT tolerant mice.
Depletion of mitochondrial H2O2 abolished tolerance, resulting in increased airway hyperreactivity, eosinophil-dominated inflammation, and elevated serum IgE levels.
RT-qPCR revealed 2-fold higher S100a4:Irf8 and 1.5-fold higher Irf4:Irf8 expression ratios in DCs from tolerant MCAT mice compared to tolerant WT mice.
captured_features: lung histology inflammation and mucus scores
lung tissue cytokine and gene expression (Ifng, Il13, Il17a, Irf4, Irf8, S100a4)
flow cytometry quantification of T cell subsets and DC/macrophage populations
summaries.population: 2-week-old and 6-week-old wild-type and MCAT transgenic mice
limitations: Inability to assess DC functional capacity using T cells with TCR specificity for HDM antigen Der p 1.
Findings are derived from a murine model, limiting direct translation to human clinical settings.

summaries.title: Characterisation of lung function trajectories and associated early-life predictors in an Australian birth cohort study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Our study included participants from the Raine Study, a prospective pregnancy cohort, with at least two spirometry measurements.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal birth cohort study characterizing lung function trajectories (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC) from age 6 to 22 and identifying early-life predictors including asthma, maternal smoking, and air pollution exposure.
key_findings: Childhood asthma at age 6 was associated with a low FEV1 trajectory (RRR 1.68, 95% CI 1.20–2.36).
Pre- and postnatal maternal smoking was associated with a very low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 2.47, 95% CI 1.52–3.90).
Early-life PM2.5Absorbance exposure was associated with a low FEV1 trajectory (RRR 1.63, 95% CI 1.06–2.51).
Early-life PM2.5Absorbance exposure was associated with an average–low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 0.52, 95% CI 0.35–0.79).
Early-life NO2 exposure was associated with an average–low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.84–0.96).
Low birthweight was associated with a low–average FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 2.03, 95% CI 1.11–3.71).
Childhood aeroallergens or combined food allergies were associated with an average–low FEV1/FVC trajectory (RRR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51–0.95).
summaries.study_design: Prospective birth cohort study with group-based trajectory modeling
summaries.population: 1512 participants from the Raine Study, followed from age 6 to 22 years in Western Australia
summaries.exposure_domain: Early-life environmental exposures (air pollution, maternal smoking), clinical factors (asthma, atopy, infections), and sociodemographic/birth characteristics
limitations: High dropout rate with symptom-biased retention
Reliance on parental recall for respiratory infections
Potential spirometry underestimation at age 6
Back-extrapolation of air pollution models over 19 years without antenatal data
Exclusion of pregnancy complications due to small numbers
summaries.data_availability_statement: Please note: supplementary material is not edited by the Editorial Office, and is uploaded as it has been supplied by the author.

summaries.title: Vaccine-Associated Measles Encephalitis in Immunocompromised Child, California, USA.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Clinical case report of a single 1-year-old infant in California, USA, with laboratory confirmation via brain tissue sequencing and nasopharyngeal swab.
summaries.summary: Case report of a fatal vaccine-associated measles encephalitis in an immunocompromised 1-year-old child in California, USA, confirmed by whole-genome RNA sequencing of brain tissue showing biased matrix-gene hypermutation.
key_findings: 38.0% (68/179) of uracil-containing codons in the matrix (M) gene contained >1 uracil-to-cytosine mutation at levels ≥5%.
Metagenomic RNA sequencing of brain tissue acquired 50.7 million reads, 190,303 of which aligned to Edmonston-Enders (Moraten) MV.
The patient experienced persistent dysautonomia, respiratory failure, and myoclonus, and died shortly after extubation.
summaries.population: 1-year-old infant, California, USA
limitations: single case report
family declined autopsy
limited to one patient
observational nature

summaries.title: Safety profile comparison of chimeric live attenuated and Vero cell-derived inactivated Japanese encephalitis vaccines through an active surveillance system in Australia.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were retrieved from SmartVax ( www.smartvax.com.au ), an active surveillance system for monitoring vaccine safety utilized by more than 450 clinics and other immunization providers in major cities and regional areas, in all states and territories throughout Australia including general practices, travel medicine clinics, and other immunization clinics (public, council, and hospital).
summaries.summary: Post-marketing safety comparison of chimeric live attenuated (Imojev) and Vero cell-derived inactivated (JEspect) Japanese encephalitis vaccines using active surveillance data from Australian clinics.
key_findings: Overall AEFI rate was 7.0% (systemic 2.8%, local 1.9%).
No significant difference in odds of overall (OR = 1.27; 95%CI: 0.91–1.77), systemic (OR = 1.23; 95%CI: 0.74–2.06), or local (OR = 1.20; 95%CI: 0.65–2.22) AEFIs between Imojev and JEspect.
Higher odds of overall (OR = 2.39; 95%CI: 1.10–5.19) and local (OR = 4.13; 95%CI: 1.08–15.74) AEFIs observed in patients aged <5 years compared to >50 years.
No statistically significant interaction between sex and number of concomitant vaccines, though a trend suggested increased AEFI odds in females with more vaccines.
captured_features: specific symptoms (tiredness, headache, pain, swelling, rash, fever, etc.)
summaries.study_design: observational cohort study using active vaccine safety surveillance
summaries.population: 2756 patients receiving Japanese encephalitis vaccines at Australian clinics (median age 34 years, 52.6% female)
limitations: small sample size for children <5 years and lack of symptom severity data
AEFI intensity difficult to ascertain in young children
limited to 5-day post-vaccination follow-up due to SMS timing
small subgroup sizes prevented statistical analysis for some vaccine combinations and sex

summaries.title: Prenatal exposure to insecticides and child cardiometabolic risk factors in the VHEMBE birth cohort.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Mothers giving birth at Tshilizidini hospital in South Africa’s Limpopo Province were recruited into the VHEMBE study between August 2012 and December 2013.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating associations between prenatal exposure to DDT and pyrethroid insecticides and child cardiometabolic risk factors at 5 years of age in Limpopo, South Africa.
key_findings: Maternal concentrations of all four pyrethroid metabolites were associated with reduced BMI z-scores (e.g., β cis-DBCA = −0.18, 95% CI = −0.33, −0.03), smaller waist circumferences (e.g., β cis-DBCA = −0.57, 95% CI = −1.09, −0.06), and decreased body fat percentages (e.g., β cis-DBCA = −0.75, 95% CI = −1.34, −0.17) per 10-fold higher concentration.

Reductions in BMI z-score were observed only among children of mothers with sufficient energy intake during pregnancy (β cis-DCCA = −0.43, 95% CI = −0.73, −0.14; β trans-DCCA = −0.40, 95% CI = −0.67, −0.12; p interaction = 0.03 and 0.04, respectively).
Maternal p,p’-DDT concentrations were associated with a reduction in body fat percentage (β = −0.39%, 95% CI = −0.76, −0.02).
Pyrethroids were not associated with child height or weight z-scores or blood pressure overall.
trans-DCCA concentrations were associated with higher height z-score among girls (β = 0.23, 95% CI = 0.05, 0.41) but not boys (β = −0.06, 95% CI = −0.25, 0.14; p interaction = 0.04).
captured_features: child height, weight, BMI, body fat percentage, waist circumference
household wealth and food security indices
summaries.population: pregnant women and their children in Limpopo, South Africa; children assessed at 5 years of age (n=637)
summaries.exposure_domain: prenatal exposure to insecticides (DDT, DDE, pyrethroids) from indoor residual spraying
limitations: single peripartum measurement of exposure may introduce nondifferential measurement error
residual confounding or chance could explain findings
relies on untestable causal assumptions
exposure may originate from sources other than IRS

summaries.title: COVID-19 mRNA Vaccine-Associated Myocarditis Presenting as STEMI in a 48-Year-Old Male.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Clinical case report based on direct patient evaluation, laboratory testing, and imaging at Memorial Healthcare System.
summaries.summary: Case report of a 48-year-old male presenting with STEMI and myocarditis shortly after receiving the second dose of the Moderna COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, with rapid resolution of symptoms and cardiac markers.
key_findings: Peak troponin was 13.60 ng/mL.
CRP was 5.10 mg/dL.
Coronary angiography revealed normal and patent coronary arteries.
Symptoms and cardiac markers resolved rapidly following discharge.
summaries.population: 48-year-old male
limitations: single case report limits generalizability
cardiac MRI unavailable for definitive diagnosis
lack of long-term follow-up data
unclear predisposing factors

summaries.title: Early-life exposure to hardship increased risk tolerance and entrepreneurship in adulthood with gender differences.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Our study used data from multiple sources. The principal sources of information are 1) the 1990 Population Census (1% sample) for the population by county and year of birth used to estimate cohort losses; 2) the 2005 Population Mini-Census (20% sample) used to measure entrepreneurship defined in two ways— narrowly as those who owned an enterprise in the private sector and broadly to also include the self-employed; 3) the 2013 nationally representative CHFS for business ownership and risk tolerance; and 4) the China Meteorological Administration for daily instrumental temperature records at 727 stations between 1951 and 1970
summaries.summary: Quasi-experimental study using Chinese census and survey data to investigate how early-life exposure to the Great Famine affects adult entrepreneurship and risk tolerance, with a focus on gender differences and conditioning versus selection mechanisms.
key_findings: In counties where the famine was one SD more severe, women and men were 17.1% and 12.7% more likely to engage in entrepreneurship, respectively (beta=0.058, SE=0.010 for women; beta=0.111, SE=0.018 for men, P<0.01).
Among male entrepreneurs, the coefficient of famine intensity on log income was 0.724 (SE=0.169, P<0.01), while for females it was positive but not statistically significant (0.423, SE=0.279).
If hardship was one SD higher, women and men were 18.4% and 13.2% more likely to be risk tolerant, respectively.
Male entrepreneurship increased with the wife’s risk tolerance (coefficient=0.081, SE=0.023, P<0.01), but not vice versa.
Among women, neither hardship nor risk tolerance significantly increased engagement in entrepreneurship.
summaries.study_design: Quasi-experimental observational study exploiting geographical variation in famine intensity due to random weather shocks
summaries.population: Adults born before 1962 in China residing in their county of hukou registration for ≥5 years
summaries.exposure_domain: Early-life hardship (Great Famine intensity proxied by weather-induced cohort loss)
limitations: Relies on correlation between risk tolerance and ambiguity aversion rather than direct ambiguity tolerance measures.
Individual-level estimates combined effects of selective mortality and operant conditioning, potentially overestimating conditioning.
CHFS only surveyed risk tolerance of one spouse, preventing joint estimation of own and spouse's risk tolerance.
Limited quantification of the exact degree to which hardship conditioned individuals to engage in entrepreneurship.

summaries.title: Willingness toward COVID-19 vaccination, coadministration with other vaccines and receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster: a cross-sectional study on the guardians of children in China.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The self-administered questionnaire was distributed through the “Xiao Dou Miao” app and 9424 guardians with access to this app participated in the survey that was conducted from September 15 to October 8, 2021.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional survey study investigating changes in guardians' willingness to vaccinate their children against COVID-19, allow coadministration with other vaccines, and receive booster doses, conducted 6 months after a previous survey in China.
key_findings: 86.68% of guardians were willing to vaccinate their children with the COVID-19 vaccine.

Guardians aged 40–49 years (OR=1.54, 95% CI: 1.19–2.00), ≥50 years (OR=2.37, 95% CI: 1.29–4.35), healthcare workers (OR=1.65, 95% CI: 1.17–2.31), and those with children aged ≥3 years (OR=1.50, 95% CI: 1.30–1.73) were more willing.
77% were willing toward coadministration of COVID-19 and influenza vaccines.
64% were willing toward coadministration of other nonimmunization program vaccines.
92% were willing to receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster and 82% were willing to vaccinate their children with a booster.
Higher education and income were associated with lower willingness to vaccinate (e.g., postgraduate education OR=0.40, 95% CI: 0.28–0.58).
captured_features: willingness to vaccinate, coadminister, and receive booster
summaries.population: 9424 guardians of children aged <6 years in China
limitations: online questionnaire prevents effective random sampling and limits representativeness
privacy protection prevented longitudinal follow-up of individual respondents
self-reported data may contain information deviation

summaries.title: Active surveillance of adverse events after immunization (AEFI) from the Local Health Unitof Ferrara, Italy.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The tools used included an informatic platform, VigiFarmacoVax, and a mobile phone system.
summaries.summary: Active SMS-based surveillance study evaluating the reporting rate, characteristics, and severity of adverse events following immunization (AEFI) in young children in Ferrara, Italy.
key_findings: 1,494 consents and 983 SMS replies were obtained from parents.
561 AEFI reports were validated, comprising 1,248 adverse events.
99.5% of AEFI were classified as not serious.
Pyrexia was the most frequent adverse event (37.5%), followed by mood disorders (26.5%) and gastrointestinal disorders (12.5%).
summaries.population: children aged ≤ 2 years who received vaccinations per the regional calendar in Ferrara, Italy (March 2018 - May 2019)
limitations: impossibility of knowing the outcome of the adverse event at the time of reporting
lack of guarantee of equity in adhering to the study due to language and mobile phone requirements
potential confounding by increased vaccination coverage and mandatory law debate

summaries.title: Repeatable enhancement of healthcare data with social determinants of health.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We requested electronic health records from the Clinical Data Repository (University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences Translational Research Institute, 2022) for all patients with chronic conditions (i.e., asthma, diabetes, heart disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, heart attack, and stroke), or contagious respiratory illness (i.e., influenza or COVID-19) between 2015 and 2020.
summaries.summary: Proof-of-concept study developing a repeatable process to integrate commercial consumer data with EHR to enrich social determinants of health (SDOH) factors, followed by preliminary analysis of SDOH differences between COVID-19 positive and negative patients.
key_findings: Consumer data coverage ranged from ~90% to ~54% across two vendors, with inter-compiler match rates between ~21% and 64%.

Several SDOH factors (home-ownership, marital status, presence of children, household size, economic stability indicator, and education) were significantly different between COVID-19 positive (N=1,092) and negative (N=54,330) groups (p<0.001), while estimated family-income and home market-value showed no significant difference (p=0.4 and p=0.9, respectively).
pathologies_diseases: chronic conditions (asthma, diabetes, heart disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, heart attack, stroke)
summaries.study_design: proof-of-concept data integration study with preliminary cross-sectional comparison
summaries.population: 55,422 patients with chronic conditions or respiratory illness (2015-2020) from a US academic medical center
limitations: restricted to only two commercial data vendors due to budget
significant missing data across datasets
low concordance between overlapping data elements from different vendors
