summaries.title: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan: Booster shots and paediatric vaccinations.
summaries.ehr_evidence: reporting has been mandatory for any myocarditis/pericarditis cases within 28 days after receiving a COVID-19 vaccine, for further investigation.
summaries.summary: National pharmacovigilance safety monitoring report of COVID-19 vaccine adverse events in Japan, covering booster shots and paediatric vaccinations from December 2021 to May 2022.
key_findings: Overall reporting rates of serious adverse events for the third shot were generally lower than for the first and second shots.
Myocarditis/pericarditis reporting rates in young men with third shots tended to be higher than first shots but lower than second shots.
No confirmed causal relationship between vaccination and death was established.

In children aged 5-11 years, reporting rates for suspected myocarditis were very low with none confirmed by Brighton classification 1-3, and one confirmed pericarditis case (0.9 cases per 1 million shots).
captured_features: adverse event reports (myocarditis, pericarditis, anaphylaxis, TTS, deaths)
summaries.population: general population of Japan, including adults receiving booster doses and children aged 5-11 years
limitations: inherent reporting bias and potential underreporting of spontaneous adverse event reports
lack of individual-level clinical data beyond reported cases
reliance on mandatory reporting from healthcare professionals and marketing authorization holders
summaries.data_availability_statement: The data for this report are available to the public on the webpage (Japanese language only) of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan ( https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/shingi/shingi-kousei_284075.html).

summaries.title: Maternal use of methamphetamine induces sex-dependent changes in myocardial gene expression in adult offspring.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The study utilized adult Sprague-Dawley rat offspring from pregnant dams administered methamphetamine or saline during gestation.
summaries.summary: Experimental study examining sex-dependent changes in myocardial gene expression in adult rat offspring following prenatal methamphetamine exposure.
key_findings: RNA sequencing identified 346 differentially expressed mRNAs in adult hearts.
184 changes occurred only in females, 89 only in males, and 74 were common to both sexes.
BDH1 protein expression was significantly decreased in both male (p < 0.01) and female (p < 0.05) offspring.
DDAH2 protein expression was significantly decreased in female hearts (p < 0.01) but not in male hearts.
summaries.population: Adult Sprague-Dawley rat offspring
limitations: Animal model limits direct translation to human physiology
Small sample sizes per group (N=5-6)
Lack of in vivo functional cardiac outcome measures
Cross-sectional assessment without longitudinal follow-up

summaries.title: Quantile regression to examine the association of air pollution with subclinical atherosclerosis in an adolescent population.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Participants included in this study were part of the Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy (PIAMA) population-based birth cohort established in the Netherlands in 1996.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional analysis using quantile regression to examine associations between early-life ambient air pollution exposure and carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) at age 16 in a Dutch birth cohort.
key_findings: PM2.5 absorbance exposure at birth was significantly associated with a 6.23 μm (95% CI: 0.15, 12.3) higher CIMT per IQR increment at the 10th quantile of CIMT.
No significant associations were found for NO2, PM2.5, PMcoarse, or ultrafine particles at other quantiles after false discovery rate correction.
PM2.5 exposure at birth was weakly associated with higher CIMT at the 10th quantile (estimate: 4.85 μm, 95% CI: −0.41, 10.10) and 20th quantile (estimate: 3.73 μm, 95% CI: −0.74, 8.20).
PMcoarse and ultrafine particles did not display any consistent patterns across CIMT deciles.
captured_features: Carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) measured via ultrasound
Annual average air pollution concentrations (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles)
Covariates (age, sex, BMI, cholesterol, blood pressure, parental education, indoor smoke, maternal smoking/BMI, breastfeeding, nationality)
summaries.study_design: Cross-sectional analysis within a prospective birth cohort using quantile regression
summaries.population: 363 adolescents aged 16 years from the PIAMA birth cohort in the Netherlands
summaries.exposure_domain: Ambient air pollution (NO2, PM2.5, PM2.5 absorbance, PMcoarse, ultrafine particles)
limitations: Cross-sectional design with only one CIMT measurement
Air pollution exposure estimated only at residential addresses, missing school/outdoor exposure
Low model R2 for PMcoarse (38%)
Relatively small sample size
Findings limited to the lowest decile of CIMT distribution

summaries.title: Cognitive and Behavioral Development of 9-Year-Old Children After Maternal Cancer During Pregnancy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The INCIP Child Follow-up study evaluates the general health and neurocognitive development after prenatal exposure to maternal cancer (treatment) using age-adapted standardized test batteries.
summaries.summary: Long-term follow-up study assessing cognitive and behavioral outcomes at age 9 in children prenatally exposed to maternal cancer and its treatment.
key_findings: Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (FSIQ) increased by 1.6 points (95% CI, 0.7 to 2.5; P < .001) for each week increase in gestational age.
No difference in FSIQ was found between treatment types (F[4,140] = 0.45, P = .776).
No associations were found between FSIQ and chemotherapeutic agent, exposure level, or timing during pregnancy.

FSIQ was lower in children with a deceased mother before age 2 years (93.13 ± 12.65) than in children with a surviving mother (104.08 ± 14.88), but this association disappeared after adjusting for gestational age (P > .3).
Maternal education level remained a significant predictor of FSIQ (P = .005).
Four children were diagnosed with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder and one with autism spectrum disorder.
Thirty-one children (24.4%) received remedial care.
summaries.study_design: Prospective multicenter cohort study (cross-sectional analysis at age 9)
summaries.population: 151 children (mean age 9.3 years) born to mothers diagnosed with cancer during pregnancy
summaries.exposure_domain: Prenatal exposure to maternal cancer and oncologic treatment (chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy)
limitations: Cross-sectional analysis at a single timepoint (age 9)
Small sample size, particularly in the chemotherapy-exposed subgroup
Multicollinearity between prematurity and maternal bereavement effects
Lack of comparison with general population rates for remedial support
Potential underpowered analysis for detecting chemotherapy effects on cognition

summaries.title: Evaluating Demographic Data to Improve Confidence in Equity Analytics in a Children's Hospital.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Before we assessed any analyses or revision of analyst procedures, it was necessary to understand how we collect the data in Epic (Epic Systems, Verona, WI), ACH’s electronic health record (EHR).
summaries.summary: Evaluation of demographic data collection, standardization, and visualization across multiple reporting tools at a children's hospital to improve health equity analytics.
key_findings: Race 2 was missing in 95% of EDW universe encounters.
Payer data was missing in 28% of appointment universe encounters.
Including null values significantly altered the distribution of race categories across all reporting tools.
summaries.population: Pediatric patients and encounters at Akron Children's Hospital, Ohio (January 1, 2021 to June 30, 2021)
limitations: Tools and technical infrastructure may be unique to ACH
Limited to 7 prioritized demographic fields
Upstream data collection accuracy was not fully assessed

summaries.title: Evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in pregnant and breastfeeding women.
summaries.ehr_evidence: An anonymous online questionnaire created via Google Forms was addressed to vaccinated women from Slovakia and Czech Republic, and was used to collect data.
summaries.summary: Evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 vaccine safety and efficacy in pregnant and breastfeeding women using a self-reported online questionnaire.
key_findings: Breastfeeding women experienced higher adverse event rates than pregnant women.

Significant differences in adverse event incidence were observed for fatigue (RR 1.230, 95% CI 1.051-1.444, P=0.0098), headache (RR 1.822, 95% CI 1.379-2.418, P<0.0001), myalgia (RR 1.633, 95% CI 1.269-2.110, P<0.0001), chills (RR 2.027, P<0.0001), subfebrile temperature ≤38°C (RR 1.697, 95% CI 1.240-2.335, P=0.0007), arthralgia (RR 1.924, 95% CI 1.340-2.776, P=0.0002), fever >38°C (RR 6.410, 95% CI 2.890-14.30, P<0.0001), and shivers (RR 2.204, 95% CI 1.264-3.863, P=0.0049).
Menstrual cycle bleeding disorders occurred in 0.7% of breastfeeding women after the first dose and 0.5% after the second dose.
93.1% of pregnancies were carried to term, 5.6% late preterm, 0.9% moderate preterm, and 0.3% very preterm.
Vaccine efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 infection was 96.3%.
Serious adverse event incidence was 0.3% (7 SAEs in 2165 respondents).
summaries.population: pregnant and breastfeeding women (n=2192) from Slovakia and Czech Republic
limitations: convenience sample with voluntary participation
no inclusion/exclusion criteria
self-reported data without trained personnel verification
efficacy analysis limited by voluntary post-vaccination isolation
data collected before the Omicron variant era
only original monovalent mRNA vaccines assessed

summaries.title: The exposome in respiratory diseases: multiple preventable risk factors from early life to adulthood.
summaries.ehr_evidence: This journal club article reviews three recent publications investigating the effects of environmental exposures... using data from the INMA and RHINESSA cohorts... NutriNet-Santé cohort. The actual sources were prospective/retrospective cohort data, questionnaires, biospecimen assays (urine), and environmental monitoring/GIS, not EHR.
summaries.summary: Journal club commentary reviewing three cohort studies investigating the impact of environmental exposures (phthalates, air pollution, greenness, lifestyle factors) on respiratory health outcomes (lung function, asthma, rhinitis) from early life to adulthood.
key_findings: Gestational phthalate exposure associated with lower FVC and FEV1 in children, especially early childhood (e.g., FEV1 z-score coefficient at age 4: −0.024 for 10% increase in MiBP).
Air pollutants associated with increased risk of asthma attacks (adjusted OR 1.60–2.46), rhinitis, and impaired lung function.
Greenness not associated with asthma or rhinitis, but associated with impaired lung function (adjusted OR 1.68–1.53).
Three early-life and one lifestyle exposure profiles associated with increased risk of asthma symptoms (mean score ratio 1.11–1.96) and uncontrolled asthma (OR 1.45–2.88).
captured_features: air pollution levels (NO2, PM10, PM2.5, black carbon, O3)
summaries.study_design: journal club commentary reviewing cohort and cross-sectional studies
summaries.data_source_type: cohort study data, questionnaires, biospecimen assays, environmental monitoring, spirometry
summaries.population: mother-child pairs from Spain, adults from Norway and Sweden, and adults from France
summaries.exposure_domain: phthalates, air pollution, greenness, socioeconomic, early-life environment, lifestyle-anthropometric factors
limitations: small sample size and sociodemographic differences (INMA)
low response rate and selection bias (RHINESSA)
highly correlated exposures and lack of multi-pollutant models (RHINESSA)
health-conscious participant bias and lack of generalizability (NutriNet-Santé)
missing indoor/aeroallergen exposures
classification bias using symptom scores

summaries.title: Memory-like innate response to booster vaccination with MF-59 adjuvanted influenza vaccine in children.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Blood for transcriptomics, HAI and cellular response was collected at all of the time points indicated in Fig. 1a.
summaries.summary: Clinical study comparing transcriptional, cellular, and antibody responses to MF59-adjuvanted trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in children (15–24 months) and young adults.
key_findings: Post-boost vaccination induced a stronger transcriptional response with 221 significantly regulated genes (FDR < 0.05, fold-change > 1.5) in children.
Adults showed a stronger response with 678 significantly regulated genes.
Seroconversion rates for children were 23/24 for H1N1, 22/24 for H3N2, and 19/24 for B/Phuket.
Seroprotection (HAI ≥ 1:629) was achieved in 6/24 for H1N1, 20/24 for H3N2, and 0/24 for B/Phuket.
Elevated interferon response pathways correlated with early-onset local reactogenicity (erythema/swelling), but no correlates were found for fever.
summaries.study_design: Prospective clinical trial with staggered sample collection
summaries.population: 90 children aged 15–24 months and 30 healthy young adults aged 25–40 years
limitations: Staggered sample collection design limited blood draw frequency per child.
Cohorts B and C lacked pre-vaccination baseline at day 1 and 3 post boost.
Small adult cohort size (n=30).
Most innate immunity module correlations with HAI titers did not reach statistical significance.

summaries.title: Parental, gestational, and early-life exposure to indoor environmental hazardous factors on allergic rhinitis among preschool children in Urumqi City: a case-control study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Questionnaires were developed for all children in the case group and control group; the questionnaire contents were adapted from the questionnaires used in the CCHH survey study and were slightly revised according to the specific context of Urumqi City.
summaries.summary: Case-control study investigating the association between parental, gestational, and early-life indoor environmental exposures and allergic rhinitis in preschool children in Urumqi City, China.
key_findings: Cesarean section was associated with AR (OR = 1.31, 95% CI = 1.02-1.67, p < 0.05).
Father with AR was associated with AR (OR = 2.67, 95% CI = 2.08-3.44, p < 0.05).
Mother with AR was associated with AR (OR = 3.70, 95% CI = 2.88-4.74, p < 0.05).
Mother with asthma was associated with AR (OR = 3.11, 95% CI = 1.18-8.20, p < 0.05).
Newly purchased furniture in parents' residence during pregnancy was associated with AR (OR = 1.49, 95% CI = 1.03-2.14, p < 0.05).
No significant association was found for passive smoking, petkeeping, or indoor dampness in the multivariate model.
captured_features: Parental history of AR and asthma
Living habits (pets, plants, smoking, air conditioning)
summaries.population: preschool children in Urumqi City, China (mean age 5.18 years; 404 cases, 1616 controls)
limitations: case-control design limits causal inference
conservative case definition restricted to physician-diagnosed AR
self-reported exposure subject to recall bias
unmeasured confounding from regional air quality improvements
summaries.data_availability_statement: The datasets generated and/or analyzed during the current study are not publicly available due to the data belonging to the School of Public Health of Fudan University but are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

summaries.title: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan: booster doses for Omicron variants and vaccinations for infants and young children.
summaries.ehr_evidence: individual case safety reports from healthcare professionals and the marketing authorisation holder (MAH)
summaries.summary: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan covering booster doses for Omicron variants and vaccinations for infants and young children until March 2023.
key_findings: 39 confirmed cases of myocarditis and 18 of pericarditis for any Pfizer booster doses.
24 confirmed cases of myocarditis and 13 of pericarditis for any Moderna booster doses.
Only 1 death was confirmed as causally related to vaccination (42-year-old woman, Pfizer BA.4/BA.5).
Reporting rates of serious adverse events for bivalent Omicron vaccines were generally not higher than for any booster doses.
Reporting rate of serious adverse events was low in children aged 6 months to 4 years.
captured_features: adverse event types (myocarditis, pericarditis, anaphylaxis, death)
summaries.population: individuals aged ≥12 years and infants/young children aged 6 months to 4 years in Japan
summaries.exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (booster doses for Omicron variants)
limitations: underestimation of the numbers and incidence rates of adverse events by using the spontaneous reporting data

summaries.title: Laboratory response to an infant with suspected measles vaccine associated fever and rash in Sri Lanka.
summaries.ehr_evidence: This single center, laboratory-based case investigation was carried out in NML, Department of Virolgy at MRI, SL.
summaries.summary: Laboratory investigation of a single 9-month-old infant in Sri Lanka who developed fever and rash following MMR vaccination, identifying vaccine-type measles virus and influenza A co-infection.
key_findings: Measles vaccine-type A (Edmonston-strain) virus was detected in 1 throat swab via RT-PCR and sequencing.
Measles IgM and IgG were positive at the sixth week of illness onset.
Influenza A RNA was detected in 1 throat swab at day three.
Parvovirus B19 IgM was detected in serum at the sixth week.
No evidence of human-to-human measles transmission was detected.
summaries.population: 9-month-old immunocompetent infant in Sri Lanka
limitations: single case report (n=1)
potential confounding from concurrent influenza A infection
limited clinical and laboratory data due to sample volume constraints
resource-limited setting
summaries.data_availability_statement: Data sharing not applicable to this article as no datasets were generated or analyzed during the current study.

summaries.title: Adverse event following immunization or vaccination in children in Minas Gerais: 2015 to 2020.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data for this study were collected in January 2022, using ESAVI notifications resulting from immunization errors registered in SI-PNI.
summaries.summary: Ecological descriptive study analyzing immunization errors and adverse events following immunization in children aged 0-9 years in Minas Gerais, Brazil, from 2015 to 2020 using national immunization registry data.
key_findings: 3,259 immunization error events were recorded out of 39,903,277 doses administered (0.008%).
91.86% of immunization errors did not result in adverse events.
56.02% of errors occurred in children under 1 year of age.
The most frequent error diagnosis was application outside the recommended age (29.12%).
Fever was the most common manifestation (40.85%), with 71.91% of events being local or systemic.
Incidence rates were 7.50/100,000 doses for errors without adverse events and 0.66/100,000 for errors with adverse events.
2019 recorded the highest incidence rates for both error categories.
summaries.population: children aged 0-9 years in Minas Gerais, Brazil
limitations: underreporting of adverse events following immunization
inadequate completion of notification records
lack of simultaneous implementation of the notification system across all macro-regions
potential underreporting due to fear of professional reprimand

summaries.title: Nasopharyngeal carriage and antibiotic susceptibility patterns of streptococcus pneumoniae, haemophilus influenzae, moraxella catarrhalis and staphylococcus aureus among urban Ugandan children post-PCV10 introduction: a cross-sectional study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Nasopharyngeal samples were collected from the children by using single sterile swabs... sent to the Clinical Microbiology Laboratory... an interviewer-administered questionnaire was used to collect clinical and demographic data.
summaries.summary: Cross-sectional study assessing nasopharyngeal carriage and antibiotic susceptibility patterns of four respiratory bacterial pathogens among urban Ugandan children 5 years post-PCV10 vaccine introduction.
key_findings: Overall bacterial carriage prevalence was 62% (120/194).
Carriage was significantly associated with a history of antibiotic use (p=0.0159) and respiratory symptoms (p=0.0003).
S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, and S. aureus carriage prevalences were 46% (90/194), 21% (40/194), 7% (14/194), and 6% (12/194), respectively.
Species co-carriage occurred in 17% (32/194) of children, predominantly S. pneumoniae + H. influenzae (23 children).
Pneumococci showed high resistance to cotrimoxazole (100%), erythromycin (76%), and tetracycline (52%), with 42% being multidrug-resistant.
H. influenzae isolates were highly resistant to cotrimoxazole (100%) and tetracycline (75%).
Post-PCV10 introduction was associated with decreased pneumococcal carriage and increased H. influenzae carriage compared to pre-PCV10 data, alongside increased antibiotic resistance.
captured_features: antibiotic susceptibility testing (MIC and disc diffusion)
summaries.data_source_type: primary microbiological sampling and laboratory testing with questionnaire survey
summaries.population: children 6-60 months of age attending outpatient clinic at Mulago Hospital Assessment Centre, Kampala, Uganda
summaries.exposure_domain: PCV10 vaccination status, history of antibiotic use, respiratory symptoms, household crowding
limitations: 52 isolates not recovered due to freeze-thaw episodes and fastidious nature of bacteria, reducing sample size
lack of pneumococcal serotyping
isolates collected from sick children without clinical evaluation to determine pathogenic relevance
cross-sectional design limits causal inference

summaries.title: Acute appendicitis in a patient immunised with COVID-19 vaccine: A case report with morphological analysis.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Clinical case presentation and hospital records of a single 58-year-old female patient at Careggi University Hospital.
summaries.summary: Case report describing acute appendicitis occurring approximately 48 hours after the first dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine in a 58-year-old female, with histological evidence of Th1-driven granulomatous inflammation.
key_findings: A 58-year-old female developed acute appendicitis approximately 48 hours after her first Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine dose.
Histopathology revealed diffuse acute and chronic inflammatory infiltrates with non-necrotizing granulomas.
WHO causality assessment indicated a B1 rating (temporal relation consistent but insufficient definitive evidence).
summaries.population: single 58-year-old female
limitations: single case design
no control group
temporal association only
insufficient evidence for causality
summaries.data_availability_statement: Data are available upon reasonable request to the corresponding author.

summaries.title: COVID-19 Vaccination Responses with Different Vaccine Platforms in Patients with Inborn Errors of Immunity.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Blood samples from patients and healthy adult donors were collected prior to vaccination (T0), 28 days (+ / − 3 days) after the first (T1) and the second (T2) doses.
summaries.summary: Observational study evaluating the safety and immunogenicity (humoral and cellular responses) of different COVID-19 vaccine platforms in patients with inborn errors of immunity and healthy controls in Argentina.
key_findings: No moderate or severe adverse events were observed in IEI patients following vaccination.
Anti-S/RBD IgG titers were significantly lower in IEI patients compared to healthy controls (p < 0.05 for adults, p < 0.005 for pediatrics).
Neutralizing antibody IC80 titers were significantly lower in IEI patients than in healthy controls (p < 0.01 for pediatrics, p < 0.05 for adults).
Positive S-specific IFN-γ response was observed in 84.5% of IEI patients, and 82.1% presented S-specific TFH cells.
Moderna vaccines elicited significantly stronger humoral responses and neutralization capacity compared to other platforms (p < 0.01 and p < 0.005, respectively).
No significant difference in humoral response was observed between vaccinated patients with or without previous SARS-CoV-2 infection.
captured_features: IgG anti-S/RBD and anti-N antibodies by ELISA
Neutralizing antibody IC50/IC80 via pseudo-virus assay
S-specific circulating TFH cell frequency by flow cytometry
summaries.population: 118 patients with inborn errors of immunity (79 adults aged 19-78, 39 pediatrics aged 12-18) and 37 age-matched healthy controls in Argentina
summaries.exposure_domain: COVID-19 vaccination (mRNA, adenoviral vector, inactivated platforms)
limitations: Small sample size for specific IEI subtypes
Lack of long-term follow-up for immunogenicity
Observational design without randomization
Limited PBMC samples for healthy pediatric controls prevented cellular response comparison
summaries.data_availability_statement: All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this published article (and its supplementary information files).

summaries.title: Open-label phase I/II clinical trial of SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain-tetanus toxoid conjugate vaccine (FINLAY-FR-2) in combination with receptor binding domain-protein vaccine (FINLAY-FR-1A) in children.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were collected through physical examinations, parent interviews, and clinical laboratory assays (PCR, ELISA, neutralization titers, T-cell response) conducted as part of the clinical trial.
summaries.summary: Open-label phase I/II clinical trial evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of a heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccine regimen in children aged 3-18 years in Cuba.
key_findings: Local pain was the most common adverse event (47.7%), with no serious or severe vaccine-associated adverse events.
Two doses of FINLAY-FR-2 induced seroconversion in 96.2% (95% CI 93.5; 98.0) of participants.
The third heterologous dose increased seroconversion to 100% and anti-RBD IgG to 325.7 UA/ml.
Geometric mean neutralizing titers were 173.8 (95% CI 131.7; 229.5) vs Alpha, 142 (95% CI 101.3; 198.9) vs Delta, 24.8 (95% CI 16.8; 36.6) vs Beta, and 99.2 (95% CI 67.8; 145.4) vs Omicron.
Predicted clinical efficacy against D614G was 91.3% (95% CI 84.6; 95.1) after two doses and 97.4% (95% CI 91.5; 99.2) after three doses.
Immune response was non-inferior to young adults (cVNT50 GMT ratio 1.25, 95% CI 0.77; 2.02).
summaries.study_design: Open-label, adaptive, multicenter phase I/II clinical trial
summaries.population: Children and adolescents aged 3-18 years in Havana, Cuba
limitations: Lack of a placebo-controlled design due to ethical concerns
No concurrent reference population for immunobridging
Approximate comparison of viral neutralization titers between children and adults due to different sampling timepoints

summaries.title: Associations of longitudinal BMI percentile classification patterns in early childhood with neighborhood-level social determinants of health.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We obtained patient-level EHR data from Nemours Children’s Health - a large, multi-state pediatric health system in the US.
summaries.summary: Longitudinal analysis of BMI-percentile trajectories in early childhood using EHR data, identifying distinct trajectory clusters and assessing their associations with neighborhood-level social determinants of health.
key_findings: Five BMI-percentile trajectory clusters were identified in a cohort of 36,910 children: always having obesity (n=429; 1.16%), overweight most of the time (n=15,006; 40.65%), increasing BMI-percentile (n=9,060; 24.54%), decreasing BMI-percentile (n=5,058; 13.70%), and always normal weight (n=7,357; 19.89%).

Children in the obesity, overweight, and increasing BMI-percentile groups were significantly more likely to reside in neighborhoods with higher poverty, unemployment, crowded households, single-parent households, and lower preschool enrollment compared to the decreasing and normal weight groups.
Multinomial logistic regression confirmed significant associations between neighborhood SDOH and cluster membership, with all confidence intervals for odds ratios excluding 1.
captured_features: patient race, ethnicity, and insurance type
patient addresses linked to census tracts
neighborhood-level SDOH variables (poverty, unemployment, crowded households, single-parent households, preschool enrollment, median household income, etc.)
summaries.study_design: Longitudinal cohort study with data-driven and algorithmic clustering of BMI trajectories, followed by multinomial logistic regression analysis.
summaries.population: Children aged 0-7 years from a multi-state US pediatric health system (Nemours Children's Health), N=36,910
limitations: Linkage to a single census tract using the last available address may not capture residential mobility effects.
Potential selection bias from excluding children with sparse clinical data or those who left the health system.
Regional differences across the five states were not accounted for.
Did not exclude children on weight-affecting medications or with monogenic obesity.
Did not analyze interactions between different SDOH variables.

summaries.title: Correction: Neonatal blood lead concentration predicts medium term lead-related outcomes in children ≤5 years old with congenital lead poisoning: A retrospective cohort study in Northern Nigeria.
summaries.summary: Correction notice for a retrospective cohort study investigating neonatal blood lead concentration as a predictor of medium-term lead-related outcomes in children under 5 with congenital lead poisoning in Northern Nigeria.

summaries.title: Association between prenatal exposure to alkylphenols and intelligence quotient among preschool children: sex-specific effects.
summaries.ehr_evidence: This research was conducted using a subset of mother-child pairs from the Guangxi Zhuang Birth Cohort (GZBC), a prospective population-based study initiated in June 2015, to examine the effects of prenatal environmental exposures on the health outcomes of both mothers and children [23].
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating the association between prenatal maternal serum alkylphenol exposure and childhood intelligence quotient at ages 3-6, including sex-stratified and mixture effect analyses.
key_findings: Each unit increase in log10-transformed maternal NP exposure was associated with a 2.38 (95% CI: -4.59, -0.16) decrease in full-scale IQ.
Maternal 4-T-OP in the second tertile was inversely associated with working memory index (β = -5.24; 95% CI: -9.58, -0.89).
Maternal 4-N-NP in the third tertile was positively associated with fluid reasoning index (β = 4.95; 95% CI: 1.14, 8.77).
Among girls, each unit increase in log10-transformed maternal 4-N-NP exposure was associated with a 13.48 (95% CI: 1.09, 25.87) increase in working memory index.
Among girls, each unit increase in log10-transformed maternal 4-N-OP exposure was associated with a 10.30 (95% CI: 1.18, 19.43) increase in working memory index.
Combined maternal AP mixture exposure above the 50th percentile exhibited a decreasing trend on VCI, VSI, WMI, PSI, and FSIQ in total children and girls.
captured_features: childhood IQ scores (VCI, VSI, WMI, FRI, PSI, FSIQ)
summaries.population: 221 mother-child pairs from the Guangxi Zhuang Birth Cohort in China; children aged 3-6 years
limitations: small sample size (n=221)
potential unmeasured confounding (e.g., maternal occupation, maternal IQ)
single early-pregnancy serum measurement may cause exposure misclassification
cross-sectional IQ assessment at 3-6 years

summaries.title: Activated fibroblasts modify keratinocyte stem niche through TET1 and IL-6 to promote their rapid transformation in a mouse model of prenatal arsenic exposure.
summaries.ehr_evidence: BALB/c female mice, aged five weeks, were acquired from the animal rearing facility at the CSIR- Indian Institute of Toxicology Research.
summaries.summary: In vivo and in vitro study examining how prenatal arsenic exposure in mice activates dermal fibroblasts to secrete IL-6, which modifies the keratinocyte stem cell niche via TET1-mediated epigenetic changes and JAK2/STAT3 signaling, promoting epithelial-mesenchymal transition and skin tumorigenesis.
key_findings: Prenatal arsenic exposure increased α-SMA positive cells in offspring skin at PND 2 (37 ± 2.7) and 18 weeks (26.2 ± 2.6) compared to controls.
Conditioned media from exposed fibroblasts increased IL-6 levels (MFI 7919 ± 350.4 vs 4086 ± 50.4) and reduced KSC apoptosis (2 ± 0.3% vs 10.4 ± 0.5%).
KSCs cultured in exposed fibroblast media showed increased proliferation (BrdU uptake 11.2 ± 0.7% vs 3 ± 0.8%) and EMT markers (N-cadherin 1.6 ± 1.2 fold, Vimentin 2.9 ± 1.8 fold).
TET1 protein increased 1.8 ± 0.06 fold and IL-6 mRNA increased 8.1 ± 1.4 fold in exposed fibroblasts, with an 8.4 ± 1.5% rise in 5-hmC/5-mC ratio at the IL-6 promoter.
summaries.study_design: in vivo mouse model and in vitro cell culture study
summaries.data_source_type: animal model / in vitro cell culture
summaries.population: BALB/c mice (prenatally exposed to arsenic and control offspring), primary dermal fibroblasts and keratinocyte stem cells

summaries.title: Genetic exploration of Dravet syndrome: two case report.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Whole genome sequencing (WGS), whole exome sequencing (WES), and Sanger sequencing were performed at 3Billion (Seoul, Korea).
summaries.summary: Case series of two Indonesian children with Dravet syndrome, detailing clinical presentations, genetic findings via NGS, and treatment outcomes.
key_findings: Patient 1 (n=1) had a 552.9 Kb heterozygous deletion spanning TTC21B, SCN1A, and SCN9A, experiencing 6-7 seizures per day.
Patient 2 (n=1) had a heterozygous splice site mutation in SCN1A (c.4003-2A>G), with seizures reduced to one per year after medication adjustment.
Greater genetic mutation severity correlated with more severe clinical manifestations and poorer seizure control (n=2).
summaries.data_source_type: clinical case series and genetic testing
summaries.population: two Indonesian children (aged 11 years 2 months and 1 year 4 months) with Javanese ethnicity
limitations: small sample size (n=2)
lack of parental genetic testing for inheritance confirmation
single-center design
no control group

summaries.title: Comparison of 1 Versus 2 Doses of Quadrivalent Influenza Vaccine in 3-8-Year-Old Children with Different Immunological States - Jiangsu Province, China, 2021.
summaries.ehr_evidence: In this open-label, self-paired clinical trial conducted in Donghai County, Jiangsu Province, China (ClinicalTrials.gov number: NCT05313893), we enrolled healthy children aged 3–8 years.
summaries.summary: Open-label, self-paired clinical trial comparing immunogenicity and safety of one versus two doses of quadrivalent influenza vaccine in children aged 3–8 years, stratified by prior vaccination history.
key_findings: Group A (previously vaccinated) showed GMT fold increases of 4.84–8.51 after dose 1, with slight decreases after dose 2 for H1N1 (0.92-fold, 95% CI: 0.85, 0.99) and BV (0.86-fold, 95% CI: 0.80, 0.93).

Group B (vaccine-naive) showed GMT fold increases of 6.09–20.41 after dose 1, with further increases after dose 2 for H1N1 (1.48-fold, 95% CI: 1.04, 1.31), BY (2.15-fold, 95% CI: 1.74, 2.66), and BV (1.57-fold, 95% CI: 1.33, 1.84).
Baseline serostatus significantly impacted antibody titers, with seropositive individuals consistently exhibiting higher titers regardless of dosage.
Adverse reaction incidence was 38.8% in Group A and 22.5% in Group B over 28 days, with no serious adverse events reported.
summaries.population: children aged 3–8 years in Jiangsu Province, China
limitations: failure to investigate the durability of immune responses following vaccination
did not assess vaccine efficacy
lack of randomized comparison between one and two doses for long-term durability
summaries.data_availability_statement: Supplementary data to this article can be found online.

summaries.title: The Epidemiological Characteristics and Spatiotemporal Clustering of Measles - China, 2005-2022.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We utilized data from the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System for our comprehensive analysis.
summaries.summary: Spatiotemporal and epidemiological analysis of measles incidence trends and clustering in China from 2005 to 2022.
key_findings: 732,218 measles cases were reported in China from 2005 to 2022, with a male-to-female ratio of 1.43:1.
The highest incidence was observed in infants under 8 months (75.41 per 100,000), followed by the 0–4 year age group (26.03 per 100,000).
51.18% of all cases occurred in children under 5 years old.
A high-incidence spatiotemporal cluster persisted from 2005 to 2008 (RR=4.69, LLR=140,816, P<0.001), while a low-incidence cluster was detected from 2016 to 2022 (RR=0.08, LLR=113,675, P<0.001).
summaries.population: children and general population in China, 2005–2022
limitations: using provincial administrative divisions as spatial units may underestimate clustering and miss localized outbreaks
early reporting system stages may have introduced information biases such as underreporting or misreporting

summaries.title: Association between prenatal glucocorticoid exposure and adolescent neurodevelopment: An observational follow-up study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Pregnancy and birth data were obtained from hospital records or the German maternity passport.
summaries.summary: Prospective observational follow-up study assessing the long-term effects of prenatal betamethasone exposure on cognitive performance, neuroendocrine stress reactivity, autonomic nervous system activity, and electrocortical activity in 14- to 15-year-old adolescents.
key_findings: No statistically significant difference in global IQ between betamethasone-exposed and unexposed groups (adjusted mean difference −2.0, 95% CI: −7.12 to 3.12, p = 0.44).
No significant differences in ADHD symptoms, BMI, or HOMA-IR between groups.
No significant differences in HPAA or ANS activity overall.

Betamethasone-exposed adolescents exhibited reduced electrocortical activity in the frontal brain region compared to controls (adjusted SEF 16.0 Hz vs 17.8 Hz, mean difference −1.83 Hz, 95% CI: −3.21 to −0.45, p = 0.01).
summaries.data_source_type: Direct clinical assessments, questionnaires, biological sampling, and historical hospital/maternity records
summaries.population: 56 adolescents aged 14–15 years (21 exposed to prenatal betamethasone, 35 unexposed controls), born at term or near-term in Germany
limitations: Small sample size and reduced statistical power
Selective participation and loss to follow-up
Potential residual confounding
Observational design limits causal inference
No adjustment for multiple comparisons
Possible confounding by tocolytic treatment and late preterm birth

summaries.title: Newborn glomerular function and gestational particulate air pollution.
summaries.ehr_evidence: From February 2010 onwards, the ENVIRONAGE cohort includes over 2200 mothers giving birth at the East-Limburg hospital in Genk, Belgium.
summaries.summary: Observational study assessing the association between gestational particulate air pollution exposure (PM2.5 and black carbon) and cord blood cystatin C levels as a marker of newborn glomerular function.
key_findings: Every 0.5 μg/m³ increment in gestational black carbon exposure was associated with a 0.04 mg/L (95% CI 0.01–0.07; p < 0.01) increase in cord blood cystatin C levels.
Every 5 μg/m³ increment in gestational PM2.5 exposure was associated with a 0.07 mg/L (95% CI 0.03–0.11; p < 0.01) increase in cord blood cystatin C levels.
Third-trimester exposure showed significant associations (BC: 0.04 mg/L, 95% CI 0.00–0.08, p < 0.02; PM2.5: 0.06 mg/L, 95% CI 0.04–0.09, p < 0.02).
No significant associations were observed for first and second trimester exposure.

Higher PM2.5 and BC exposure during the entire pregnancy and last trimester were significantly associated with a higher risk of having cord blood cystatin C levels above the 10th percentile (PM2.5 OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.23–2.65, p < 0.01; BC OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.04–1.80, p = 0.02).
summaries.data_source_type: birth cohort with environmental exposure modeling
summaries.population: 1484 mother-newborn pairs from the ENVIRONAGE birth cohort in Genk, Belgium
summaries.exposure_domain: ambient air pollution (PM2.5 and black carbon)
limitations: lack of other kidney function markers such as creatinine
exposure estimated via residential address spatial modeling rather than personal monitoring
single time-point measurement at birth limits longitudinal assessment

summaries.title: Associations between gestational exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances, fetal growth, and the mediation effect of thyroid hormones.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Study participants were selected among subjects of the Ezhou birth cohort study, which is an ongoing longitudinal study initiated in January 2019 that aims to evaluate the impact of environmental factors on the health of pregnant women and their children.
summaries.summary: Prospective birth cohort study evaluating associations between prenatal PFAS exposure, maternal thyroid hormones, and fetal growth outcomes in China.
key_findings: Increasing PFNA concentration was associated with decreased birth length (β = -0.54 cm; 95% CI: -0.90, -0.18).
Increasing PFHxS concentration was associated with decreased birth length (β = -0.64 cm; 95% CI: -0.86, -0.42).
Increasing PFOA concentration was associated with decreased head circumference (β = -0.73 cm; 95% CI: -1.19, -0.27).
Increasing PFHpS concentration was associated with decreased head circumference (β = -0.30 cm; 95% CI: -0.53, -0.07).
Increasing PFDA concentration was associated with decreased gestational age (β = -0.18 week; 95% CI: -0.26, -0.10).
Maternal FT3 mediated 36.7% of the effect of PFNA on birth length, and FT4 mediated 30.8% of the effect of PFOA on head circumference.
No significant mediation by thyroid hormones was observed for birth weight or gestational age.
In female infants, higher PFOA was associated with lower birth weight (β = -53.6 g; 95% CI: -77.8, -29.4).
captured_features: maternal thyroid hormone levels (TSH, FT3, FT4, TT3, TT4, TG)
summaries.study_design: prospective birth cohort study with mediation analysis
summaries.population: 379 mother-infant pairs from Ezhou City, Hubei Province, China, recruited in early pregnancy (2019-2020)
limitations: PFAS-thyroid hormone associations are cross-sectional, limiting causal inference
single first-trimester measurement may lead to exposure misclassification
only 8 of over 23 detectable PFASs were measured
single-city cohort limits generalizability to other populations
summaries.data_availability_statement: The datasets used and/or analysed during the current study available from the corresponding author on reason-able request.

summaries.title: Early Life Exposure to Manure-Fertilized Soil Shapes the Gut Antibiotic Resistome.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Soil samples were collected from two distinct locations: red soil (RS, classified as Ultisols) from Xinhui District, Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province and black soil (BS, classified as Mollisols) from Hailun City, Suihua, Heilongjiang Province.
summaries.summary: Experimental study investigating how early life exposure to manure-fertilized soil alters the gut antibiotic resistome and microbiome composition in mice.
key_findings: Manured red soil ARG abundance was 0.63 ± 0.03 copies/cell, a 10.5% increase over unfertilized soil (0.57 ± 0.005 copies/cell, P < 0.05).
Manured black soil ARG abundance was 0.45 ± 0.02 copies/cell, a 12.5% increase over unfertilized soil (0.40 ± 0.02 copies/cell, P < 0.05).
Mouse gut ARG abundance in the manured red soil group was 3.34 ± 0.34 copies/cell, a 48.4% increase over the control group (2.25 ± 0.37 copies/cell).
Mouse gut ARG abundance in the manured black soil group was 3.89 ± 0.62 copies/cell, a 109% increase over the control group (1.86 ± 0.54 copies/cell).
Tetracycline resistance genes comprised 84.9% of gut ARGs, with tet(Q) constituting 90% of tetracycline ARGs.
MGE abundance was significantly higher in manured groups (Manured RS: 34.21 ± 2.47 copies/cell, 12.5% increase; Manured BS: 36.07 ± 4.43 copies/cell, 19.8% increase).
Virulence factor abundance was elevated in manured groups (Manured RS: 12.78 ± 1.09 copies/cell, 8.7% increase; Manured BS: 11.61 ± 0.61 copies/cell, 13.44% increase).
captured_features: Gut microbiome composition (phylum and family level)
summaries.data_source_type: metagenomic sequencing of soil and fecal samples
summaries.population: BALB/c mice (pregnant dams and offspring from birth to 8 weeks)
limitations: animal model (mice) limits direct human translatability
small sample size per group (n=3 pregnant mice)
controlled laboratory conditions may not reflect real-world agricultural environments
cross-sectional sampling at a single timepoint (8 weeks)
summaries.data_availability_statement: The raw metagenomic sequence data are publicly available under the accession number PRJNA1206751.

summaries.title: A comprehensive atlas of the bonobo gut bacteriome and its associated host and exposome factors.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Data were collected using observations, historical records retrieved from the studbook or from the Zoological Information Management System (ZIMS), questionnaires and diet sheets filled in by zoo staff.
summaries.summary: Comprehensive atlas of the bonobo gut bacteriome and its associated host and exposome factors, comparing wild and zoo-housed populations to identify drivers of microbiome composition and social transmission.
key_findings: Gut bacterial beta diversity was significantly associated with captive vs wild lifestyle (PERMANOVA: R2 = 28.7%, p < 0.001).
Wild bonobo alpha diversity was higher than zoo-housed bonobos (LMM: β = 0.935 ± 0.311 SE, p = 0.020).
Dietary diversity was negatively correlated with alpha diversity in wild bonobos (LMM: β = −0.353 ± 0.077 SE, padj < 0.001).
Antibiotic use was associated with lower similarity to the wild phenotype (posterior mean = −0.298, 95% CI: [−0.407, −0.189]).
Current cohabitation led to the highest gut bacteria sharing (36.5% Bray-Curtis similarity on average), followed by past cohabitation (30.1% similarity).
Grooming bond strength strongly correlated with gut bacteriome similarity (posterior mean = 1.055, 95% CI: [0.496, 1.609]).
summaries.study_design: Cross-sectional observational study with dyadic analyses comparing wild and zoo-housed bonobos
summaries.data_source_type: Fecal microbiome sequencing and field/zoo observational data
summaries.population: 212 bonobos (Pan paniscus) from European zoos and two wild communities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
summaries.exposure_domain: Diet, antibiotic use, social contact, cohabitation, age, maternal effects, and environmental conditions
limitations: Assumes wild bonobo bacteriome represents a native baseline
Relies on 16S rRNA sequencing rather than metagenomics, limiting strain-level resolution
Dietary intake estimated from group distribution rather than individual consumption
Cross-sectional design limits causal inference for social transmission
summaries.data_availability_statement: Sequencing data have been deposited at the European Nucleotide Archive under project ENA: PRJEB86099 and are publicly available as of the date of publication. Pseudonymized sample data have been deposited and are publicly available as of the data of publication at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14913431. All original code has been deposited and is publicly available as of the date of publication at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14911049.

summaries.title: Using machine learning to predict future foster care admission.
summaries.ehr_evidence: We make use of data from CareSource Ohio, a nonprofit health plan with the largest Medicaid enrollment in the state of Ohio.
summaries.summary: Machine learning predictive modeling study using Medicaid claims and social determinants of health data to identify children at risk of future foster care admission.
key_findings: The gradient-boosted tree model classified 2408 children as at risk, with 1599 (66.4%) actually transitioning into foster care.
The SDOH model achieved a positive predictive value (PPV) of 84.72%, compared to 27.44% for the non-SDOH model.
Logistic regression yielded a PPV of 0% without SDOH variables and 12.7% with SDOH variables, both substantially worse than the gradient-boosted tree model.
Average precision was 0.75 for the SDOH model and 0.16 for the non-SDOH model.
captured_features: linked parental adult diagnoses and utilization
Johns Hopkins ACG System health analytics scores
21 SDOH risk scores (geographic and household-level factors)
summaries.study_design: Predictive modeling study comparing gradient-boosted tree machine learning to logistic regression
summaries.population: Children under 18 years enrolled in CareSource Medicaid plan in Ohio (2019-2022), with linked parental adult data
summaries.exposure_domain: Social determinants of health (SDOH) and clinical/healthcare utilization factors
limitations: Potential missing foster care admissions due to enrollment in different health plans
Model may not generalize to demographically or clinically distinct populations
Lack of sibling status data preventing proper training/validation split
Risk of replicating racial, disability, and socioeconomic biases in the existing child welfare system

summaries.title: Moderate prenatal alcohol exposure differentially alters acute ethanol sensitivity of GABAergic transmission in CRFR1- and CRFR1+ CeM Neurons.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Male CRF1-Cre transgenic rats were obtained for breeding from Dr. Nicholas Gilpin, Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center (New Orleans, LA, USA).
summaries.summary: Experimental study investigating how moderate prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) on gestational day 12 alters acute ethanol modulation of GABAergic neurotransmission onto CRFR1+ and CRFR1- neurons in the central amygdala of adult rat offspring.
key_findings: PAE increased basal sIPSC amplitude in CRFR1+ neurons (F(1, 127) = 5.026, p = 0.027).
In air males, 66 mM EtOH decreased CRFR1- sIPSC frequency (t(11) = 2.658, p = 0.022), but PAE males showed no significant change at 44 mM (p = 0.279), 66 mM (p = 0.138), or 88 mM (p = 0.484).
PAE males exhibited a significant decrease in CRFR1+ sIPSC frequency at 44 mM EtOH (t(8) = 2.465, p = 0.039).
PAE females showed significant decreases in CRFR1- sIPSC frequency at 44 mM (t(11) = 3.805, p = 0.003) and 66 mM (t(9) = 2.775, p = 0.022) EtOH.
PAE females exhibited significant decreases in CRFR1+ sIPSC frequency (t(8) = 3.196, p = 0.013) and amplitude (t(9) = 2.719, p = 0.023) at 44 mM EtOH.
summaries.population: Adult CRF1-Cre transgenic rat offspring (P80-110), both males and females
summaries.exposure_domain: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) and acute ethanol
limitations: Use of transgenic reporter lines may alter neurophysiology via insertional mutagenesis or promoter leakiness.
Recordings performed at room temperature rather than physiologically relevant temperature.
Potential incongruence between reporter gene expression and endogenous CRFR1 expression.
Small sample sizes per experimental group (n=9-12 cells/animals).

summaries.title: Sugar restriction in the first 1000 days after conception, and long-term respiratory health: a quasi-experiment study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Dates of death and causes were obtained by linking to the National Health Service (NHS) death registers in England and Wales, as well as the NHS central registry in Scotland.
summaries.summary: Quasi-experimental study linking UK Biobank participants born during UK sugar rationing (1951–1956) to NHS health records to assess the long-term impact of early-life sugar restriction on adult respiratory disease risk, disease onset, and lung function.
key_findings: Early-life sugar rationing (in utero plus 1–2 years) was associated with a lower risk of asthma (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.61, 0.91).
Sugar rationing was associated with a lower risk of COPD (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.62, 0.88).
Rationed participants experienced a delayed disease onset of up to 3.6 years.
Rationing was associated with improved lung function: FEV1% increased by 6.0 (95% CI: 2.9, 9.1), FVC% by 5.9 (95% CI: 3.3, 8.5), and FEV1/FVC ratio by 0.045 (95% CI: 0.011, 0.079).
No significant association was found for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (HR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.46, 1.13; P for trend = 0.145).
Diabetes and hypertension mediated 18.2% of the effect on lung disease risk, while birth weight contributed only 1.6%.
Placebo outcomes (influenza and herpes zoster) showed no significant associations (HRs close to 1).
summaries.population: 58,670 UK Biobank participants born October 1951–March 1956, predominantly White, aged 40–70 at recruitment
summaries.exposure_domain: early-life sugar restriction/rationing during the first 1000 days after conception
limitations: Unmeasured confounding and secular trends cannot be fully excluded
Right censoring and survivor bias due to lack of prestudy mortality data
UK Biobank is not nationally representative and is predominantly White
Lack of detailed individual-level dietary data
Recall error for early-life variables like breastfeeding status
Use of London air pollution data as a nationwide proxy may not be accurate
Median-based polygenic risk score grouping may not reflect true genetic risk distribution
summaries.data_availability_statement: The data are accessible through a public, open-access repository . Data from the UKB, ELSA, and HRS are available to researchers on request.

summaries.title: Impact of maternal fasting blood glucose in pregnancy on body composition, anthropometric, and metabolic outcomes in newborns and 3-Year-Old offspring: results from the lifestyle in pregnancy and offspring study.
summaries.ehr_evidence: The analysis used data from the Lifestyle in Pregnancy (LiP) study and its 3-year follow-up, the LiPO study.
summaries.summary: Secondary analysis of the LiP RCT and LiPO follow-up examining associations between maternal fasting glucose at 28 weeks gestation and offspring body composition, anthropometry, and metabolic outcomes at birth and 3 years.
key_findings: Higher maternal fasting plasma glucose at 28 weeks was associated with a significantly higher birth weight z-score (β = 0.48, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.75, p = 0.001).
The association with birth weight in grams was not statistically significant (β = 103 g, 95% CI −43 to 249, p = 0.167).
At 3 years of age, maternal fasting glucose was not significantly associated with BMI z-score or other cardiometabolic measures.
Newborns to women meeting WHO2013 GDM criteria had higher birth weight z-scores compared to those who did not (0.474 vs. 0.135, p = 0.01).
Fasting glucose ≥5.6 mmol/L was associated with a higher proportion of large-for-gestational-age infants (p = 0.01).
Fasting glucose >5.3 mmol/L was associated with higher cord c-peptide levels (592 pmol/L vs. 430 pmol/L, p = 0.01).
Fat mass at 3 years did not differ significantly between children of mothers meeting WHO2013 GDM criteria versus those who did not.
summaries.study_design: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial and 3-year follow-up cohort
summaries.population: 301 obese pregnant women (pre-pregnancy BMI ≥30 kg/m2) and their offspring assessed at birth and 3 years
summaries.exposure_domain: Maternal fasting blood glucose / gestational hyperglycemia
limitations: Approximately 50% follow-up rate at 3 years
Missing DXA data due to scan quality issues
Small subgroup sample sizes limiting statistical power
Potential type II error for non-significant outcomes
summaries.data_availability_statement: The data that support the findings of this study are available from C.A.V., but restrictions apply to their availability. The data were used under license for the current study and include unpublished results that are still being analyzed. Therefore, they are not publicly available. However, data may be obtained from the corresponding author on reasonable request and with permission from C.A.V.

summaries.title: Maternal exposure to cyclophosphamide during prepubertal life does not affect the cryosusceptibility of in vitro derived mouse embryos.
summaries.ehr_evidence: Using a mouse model, this study evaluated the impact of prepubertal CY exposure (2 successive weekly doses of 75 mg/kg body weight at 2 weeks of age) on the cryosusceptibility of embryos derived via in vitro fertilization (IVF) at their reproductive phase.
summaries.summary: Experimental study using a prepubertal female Swiss albino mouse model to evaluate the impact of cyclophosphamide exposure on the cryosusceptibility, developmental competence, and pluripotency marker expression of in vitro derived embryos.
key_findings: Cyclophosphamide exposure caused a significant (P <0.0001) decline in total ovarian follicle count compared to controls.
Fertilization rates were comparable between control (84.3 ± 6.8) and CY (88.3 ± 4.9) groups.
Post-warming embryo survival rates were comparable between control (99.5 ± 0.5) and CY (99 ± 1) groups.

Blastocyst formation, apoptotic index, ICM outgrowth rates, and mRNA levels of Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog showed no significant differences between vitrified and non-vitrified CY embryos compared to controls.
captured_features: mRNA expression of Oct4, Sox2, Nanog
summaries.population: prepubertal female Swiss albino mice
limitations: inability to assess in vivo implantation potential
restricted to a single chemotherapeutic agent and specific dosage
mouse model limitations for direct human translation
lack of direct dosage equivalence between mice and humans
